Operators identified wiring on battery bank that had begun to smolder / melt the coating upon turning on battery power to check Diesel Generator for operation. Power was immediately shut off to Generator and it was not running at the time. The Field Electrician was called, and opened the panel door, found the wiring starting to smoke and then a small 2" flame ignited. Cut the negative ground wire going to the battery and the flame ceased. There were no injuries or further damage except the 3 wires coming from battery.
ROOT CAUSE:
Initial findings:
. Initially found wires from the battery burnt. The negative wire was burnt from the battery to ground terminal in the panel. Also found other wires that had pieces of the coating melted from being close to the above mentioned negative wire. 
. Possible cause: High amp draw during start-up.

Repairs made:
. Changed out the wires from the batteries. Spliced additional wires that had parts of the coat melted. 
. All wires affected or damaged were changed in its entirety.

Conclusion
. Checked the amp draw that was coming from the starter to verify what it was reading. 
. With the generator running the amp draw was at a 2, and with it not running it's also at a 2. 
. Once personnel attempt to crank the generator the amp draw shoots up to a 28amp.
. Currently awaiting a confirmation from electrical foreman on what the engine starter is supposed to be using when attempting to crank. 
INVESTIGATION & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS:
We have confirmed with a volt meter that the DC Voltage when read from the positive side of the battery to the negative post is slightly different than the reading from positive side to panel chassis ground. This is fairly common when grounding is done at different locations. This would indicate that there are different ground potentials based on the distance from the battery negative and the materials resistance (steel and copper wire) between battery negative and grounding location. There is a possibility before the technicians cleaned up the connections on the main feeder grounds, the panel became part of the return circuit for the starter, which burned the original wiring. With a fuse in place of the original ground block in the panel, the wire is now protected in the event that the starter circuit was to have a ground issue and use the chassis for return.

A contractor employee was in the process performing hot work to cut a section of 12" pipe on the pipeline skid.  In doing so, he was using a 5 foot cutting torch to complete the task.  During the cutting on pipe, a flash fire occurred - the fire watch quickly extinguished the fire.  The employee cutting was struck by fire on the right side of his face.  The employee was stabilized and was transported to shore by crew boat.  

The employee was taken to a medical facility where they were treated for 1st degree burns to right side of face and released to modified work.  

Prior to commencing hot work activity, the pipe was checked by opening several needle valves in which clear salt water was discharged.  This was a contributing factor to incorrectly consider the line did not contain flammable material. There were two (2) cuts made into the pipe.  The 1st cut was made on the lower end of pipe without incident and that it further was an indication that the line did not contain flammables.  When the 2nd cut was made on the upper end of the pipe, it caused a flash fire due to due combustible material inside of pipe. 
 
The pipeline skid was flushed using (4 volumes) of salt water between 12/8/2020 and 12/16/2020.

Key factors that aided with minimizing the injury was the use of personal protective equipment and body positioning to perform task. The employee was wearing Fire Retardant Clothing, Hood Cover Worn over the Head and Partially Covered the Face, Leather Gloves, and a Burning Face Shield. The employee was using a 5 foot cutting torch that allowed him to distance himself from the hot work.

The deckhand returned to shore for further evaluation. X-rays showed no signs of a break. He has some swelling but was released for full duty.

The IP was transported to the nearest manned facility where he was then transferred by helicopter where the Field Medic could evaluate and provide treatment.  IP was transported by a field helicopter where he followed-up with an Occ-Med clinic.  He was released to regular duty.

While skidding the production work over rig, smoke was observed by the Tool pusher coming from the generator house. Further investigation revealed sparks emanating from the hydraulic pump breaker. Hydraulic pump was immediately shutdown resulting in sparks to stop and the smoke to dissipate. UWA/PIC notified, and the area was secured.

IP well-head tech was in the process of making repairs on a well SSV bonnet assembly. The rigging (1" x 6' strap and come-along) was being used to pick up the actuator to put back on the bonnet assembly. When it got to the height to go over the spring, it had to be pulled away a few inches to clear the spring. When it was pulled away, it became unbalanced and slipped out of the strap and fell two feet onto the top of IP's right foot. The facility Medic checked the IP's injury and coordinated a case evac flight for IP to be flown in for further evaluation.

Instrument Tech was going to put his tools up in the gas sales meter shack. When he stepped on the edge of the skid his foot slipped striking his shin on the edge of the skid causing a laceration on his shin. The HSE Manager met the IP at the heliport and brought the him to an Occ-Med clinic for evaluation.  The IP received 9 sutures and was released to regular duty.

At approximately 14:07 on 7/4/2021, smoke was seen coming from the temporary 3rd-party nitrogen skid on the East drill deck. Workers in the area discharged a fire extinguisher, the alarm was sounded, and the facility achieved full muster.  Emergency protocols were followed.  Fire teams responded to the scene and observed smoke coming from the skid.  Water was deployed for thermal cooling of equipment.  No injuries occurred during the incident or the muster.  Operations is investigating the event.

On 07/04/2021 at approximately 18:50 hours operators noticed a small fire on the gas compressor. Three of the four operators on the facility were near the flotation cell montioring the fluid level of the vessel. The facility had just been brought back on line following a LSH on the floatation cell. At that time, they heard the compressor shut down and almost simultaneously a noise (one described it sounded like a backfire) coming from the compressor building. When the first operator rounded the corner, he noticed a flame near the second stage discharge. He activated a nearby dry chemical wheeled unit and extinguished the fire. The fire was extinguished in less than a minute. Operations personnel notified Supervision and the compressor was left shut-in until investigation could be completed. As a result of the fire, the company replaced the damaged piece of stainless steel tubing as well as wiring, fittings, gaskets, filters, gauges, and regulator impacted by the flame/heat.

While POOH, the Pipe Racking System (PRS) was being operated to the end of the track in preparation to grab the next stand of drill pipe. Once at the track, the Zone Management System (ZMS) malfunctioned and allowed the PRS arm to extend towards well center which allowed the top drive, being operated upward, to come into contact with the PRS arm lifting it about 7 feet. No visible damage noted to either piece of equipment. No dropped objects noted.

On 07/05/2021, the east crane operator noticed that the top boom chords were slightly bent as well as a few lacings on cab side of heel section while sitting in the cab. After further investigation it was noticed that lacing was also bent on engine side of heel section. Crane operator notified operations management and the crane was taken out of service. An investigation is currently underway to determine the cause of damage. No injuries were associated with this event.

IP reported to their supervisor this morning that IP woke up with eye irritation. IP believes they may have got something in the eye yesterday.  IP was lifted off the boat to be checked out by the medic.  The medic determined there was a piece of metal in the eye.  Medic attempted to flush the metal from the eye with no success. Medic called a doctor who advised IP be transported to the beach for further evaluation. The IP was seen at a clinic where the foreign body was removed from the eye.  IP was released to full duty.  This incident will be classified as a First Aid case.

07.07.2021:  As required by 30 CFR 250.188(a)(4), Talos ERT LLC respectfully made notification on evidence of a fire that occurred on a light fixture on VR 331 (G02572) on 07.07.2021.  The crew was installing tracks for the ceiling tiles. While installing they had to move the light out of the way. When they did the light started to smoke at the pin connectors and connection.They immediately stopped work, killed the light switch, and notified the PIC.  The PIC went and locked out the breaker to the lighting circuit until an electrician could come to evaluate the issue.

An operator reported to the Safety Medic with pain in the left shoulder. The IP states they were pulling on a 1" hydraulic hose when they felt sudden pain in the shoulder. The IP was taken for further evaluation and treatment by the Safety medic and SPAR medic. The IP has been sent in for further evaluation and treatment by onshore physician. X-rays taken by the onshore physician were negative. IP has received instructions to take over-the-counter medication and use ice pack and heat compress for discomfort. IP had an MRI on 7/12/21 and appointment with Orthopedic on 7/15/21.  IP was diagnosed with a rotator cuff tear and rupture in the left shoulder.  IP was given prescription medication for treatment.  BSEE was notified of re-classified injury from FAC to MTC on 7/19/21.

Individual was climbing down ladder from a scaffold set when his foot slipped off of the bottom rung of the ladder. IP fell approximately 2' where he struck the half round pipe edge of the skid with his tailbone. IP complained about pain in the tailbone area, he is being sent in at his company's request to be evaluated by company physician. The IP was seen at the Urgent Care facility where he received a Full Return To Work.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition
column24: While back loading equipment from lift boat to field boat, a lift was landed on the boat, unhooked from the load and crane operator started booming up.  While booming up, the load block swung over and caught a 1" pipe on the flare boom.  This caused a 3 ft. section of the pipe to fall off.  The pipe landed on the back of the boat 80 feet below.  There were no personnel in the area and no injuries or other damage.

On July 10, 2021 at approximately 1815 hrs. Just after tour change, the crane operator was in the process of moving a sub to the rig floor for making up BHA. A roustabout was tailing the load with a tagline to help assist in guiding it to the rig floor through the V-door. The roustabout then moved down the v-door walkway away from the load, while a floor hand took over the load. The floor hand then signaled with their head to lift the load, so they could pull the sub onto the rig floor. As the crane operator proceeded to lift up, the stinger hook caught the top of A-frame walkway handrail causing a 5 1/2 foot section (weight 13.6 lbs.) to break off and fall approximately 78 feet. The section of handrail came to rest on top of the Haliburton vacuum frame. No injuries occurred and the closest person was working 6 feet away from drop area.

At approximately 2100 hrs the crane was offloading personnel from the motor vessel. As the crane operator began lifting the personnel basket the boat pulled away prematurely and the personnel basket caught the gangway at the back of the boat dragging the gangway into the water. No personnel were injured.

Drill crew was in the process of transferring the subsurface test tree from the aux side of the drill floor to the main side using the PRT Hoss Transfer System attached to the aux hydraracker with ratchet straps to guide it across the floor. Test tree came into contact with lower tail arm gripper on the main hydra-racker resulting in the head shifting and causing the retaining bolt to pull up out of guide plate.  The bolt remained in the frame of gripper head. No injuries, dropped objects or spill occurred as a result of this incident. Damage was limited to the bolt - initial estimate is less than $250.

On 7/12/21 an operator (IP) was stabbing power swivel into TIW.  Another worker began tightening up power swivel and TIW.  The IP started to walk away when the IP heard a loud noise and felt something hit their left foot.  IP was knocked to the deck and hit their right elbow.  First aid measures and evaluation were initiated by the site medic.  Medivac was dispatched and IP was transported to a hospital. IP sustained a laceration to left interior ankle near heel and secured with sutures.  IP has been placed on Restricted Duty.

On 07/13/2021 at approximately 12:00pm the electricians were performing a 12 month PM on the hypochlorite unit when they noticed what appeared to be a glow near the Omniclor cells of the unit.  The team immediately shut down the unit using the emergency stop button and secured the access panel to the unit with no further issues. The team did not see any smoke or flames at the time the glow was observed. The team discussed a path forward and developed an isolation plan, gained the appropriate approvals and put the isolation in place.  At around 1900hrs, the electricians were able to gain access into the unit after the full isolation was installed and discovered evidence of melting and charring on the Omniclor cell connecting bar and adjacent plastic mounting bracket. The initial investigation revealed that one of the bolts on the connecting bar between two Omniclor cells was loose.  The loose bolt created high resistance across the connecting bar, causing it to heat up excessively.  The equipment will remain offline until it can be further inspected and repaired.

The oral notification was made to NOLA District after-hours phone on 07/13/2021 by phone call.

IP was found wandering alone on the drill deck. He was incoherent with trauma to his face and a noticeably dislocated right shoulder. He was taken to the onboard medic. The medic contacted the shore base doctor and the IP was evaluated. Because IP was still incoherent and could not dialogue with the doctor to explain what had happened to him the doctor gave instruction to medivac IP to shore.

While training in the crane with a mentor, the crane operator was communicating with deck personnel. Communication is established with a button that is located by his left foot. The Crane operator picked up the load and lost power to the crane. Crane operator lost power because they did not realize that operator's foot accidentally stepped on the hydraulic kill switch located in proximity to their left foot instead of the communications button. When hydraulic power was lost to the crane, the load was in movement and bumped the cover to a GAI-Tronics box in the vicinity and damaged the cover to the box. The Crane Operators' mentor immediately knew what the issue was and rectified the problem.

At approximately 16:57 hours, while peforming routine maintenance to install and grease new wire rope, and while booming down, the headache ball on the Aux line that had been pulled up passed the Anti-2 Block and into the boom tip. At this point the wire rope attached to the headache ball separated from each other and the headache ball fell into the waters. Item was unrecoverable. There were no injuries.
IP was attempting to pick up a 4' beam when they felt a pain in the abdomen. IP was sent in to the shore base and met by he company's representative. IP refused treatment.

While replacing the water sprinkler hose in the lifeboat, charred wiring was observed behind the battery selector switch.  There was no fire, smell or other incident associate with this observation.  Wiring was replaced and put back in service.

A Roughneck (IP) was using a pry bar to release the latch on the flow head side door elevators (positioned on deck of rig floor). As IP applied downward force with the pry bar, the latch opened as intended. As the door opened, the weight of the elevator door forced the pry bar in a downward motion. Subsequently, the pry bar made contact across the top of the worker's foot. The job was immediately shut down and the IP reported the incident to supervision prior to seeing the medic for evaluation. Upon evaluation shoreside, x-rays revealed 2 broken metatarsal bones in the top of the foot.
During normal operations the flash gas compressor shuts down due to a TSE causing a full facility muster.  Heat in the area of the exhausted caused this TSE to be activated.

Fluid engineer was in the process of weighing ZnBr2 fluid. The graduated cylinder slipped from his hand and hit bottom first splashing up between his face shield and glasses. While removing face shield and safety glasses, fluid ran into left eye. He flushed at the eyewash station and proceeded to his unit and flushed with saline, after several minutes reported to the medic for treatment. Medic treated and consulted with company doctor and was advised to medevac in as soon as possible.

At 0130 am, while splashing the SS tooling basket with Beacons for deployment, one of the beacon with floatation broke loose from weight at electronic/hydrostatic disconnect device, and floated away (at about 1.5 kts in 210 deg direction). With 2 ROV's in water, we stopped their descent and attempted to chase down at 1 kt, as it was out running vessel. Vessel stopped chase as it was approaching assets with ROV's suspended. Beacon not recovered.  Update: The estimated cost of the beacon is $1,500.00.  Beacon was inside tooling basket when it broke loose.  Crane was holding tooling basket.

Wireline unit (9,500 lbs) was lifted off the M/V. When the load was swung to position over the platform, the crane operator heard a loud popping sound and the crane ceased to swing. The load was safely lowered and landed. The boom was secured to prevent movement. Crane was inspected and it was discovered that the swing drive gear had moved down approximately 1.5?. No injuries or damage to load.

The driller was breaking out of a connection with the top drive and the clamp was not released while activating "spin mode". This caused the bolts that connect the cylinder links to the lower pipe handler assembly to fail. There were no dropped objects or injuries. Damage of the eight bolts is estimated to be <$50.

Vessel went into Dynamic Positioning (DP) Advisory Yellow Condition due to total power loss. The vessel was unable to regain power, resulting in a Dynamic Positioning (DP) Red Condition. With the vessel in DP Red Condition, an Emergency Disconnect Sequence (EDS) was performed to release from the well. Following the EDS, the vessel continued to drift without power for a total of 1,001 meters at which point the power was restored and the DP system was reconnected. DP was established stable, and the vessel was confirmed stopped. Once the power system was inspected and confirmed stable, the rig's ROV was placed in the water to assess the bottom of the Lower Marine Riser Package (LMRP); upon inspection, it was observed that the LMRP made contact with the seafloor and had drug across the seafloor for approximately 320 feet. No subsea assets were in the area where contact was made with the seafloor. Tug Boats and ROV Vessel mobilized to location to stand-by. ROV Vessel utilized to assess the well, subsea assets, and to standby for further wellhead monitoring. Recovery plans for the LMRP and Marine Riser ongoing. Notes: The Blowout Preventer (BOP) Upper Blind Shear Rams were functioned closed along with the ST Locks while still in DP Yellow to proactively secure the well prior to the notifications made post EDS activation. LMRP 2 successfully performed an EDS function on SA008. This was confirmed with visual inspection with ROV of LMRP2 and BOP2. No visible damage was found on LMRP2 once pulled and secured at surface. LMRP1 was run, latched up and tested to BOP2.  

LMRP2 inspection is ongoing, minimal damages found. Proactive maintenance, repairs, and general cleaning/painting have been made. 
. Replace POD components due to evidence of mud
. Overhaul LMRP connector due to evidence of mud
. Change out of termination spool as a precautionary step due to some unknown factors (stress that it may have seen)
. Blasting/Painting LMRP frame
. LMRP1 was run, latched up and tested to BOP2.

The work Being done at the time of the incident was replacement of handrails and kick plate throughout work area after the removal of the riser and J tubes for the wells. A contractor was completing the task of reinstalling handrail including Firewatch operations.  At the time of the incident the Person of Interest was instructed to be Firewatch on the +15. While on fire watch duty, the POI climbed to a mezzanine deck to remove a fire blanket and fell off of that mezzanine deck to the +15 below.

While lowering cutting box onto boat, the load contacted and damaged an aluminum handrail on a personnel ramp. NOTE: The ramp was not in service at the time but was lying on the deck against the side rail of the boat. Also Boat deck was not crowded at the time.

The subject facility experienced a failure of the #4 mooring chain which is located in the NE quadrant. At this moment, there have been no adverse effects and the facility is stable. We are currently monitoring the situation.

While discussing operations in the welding shop, personnel in the area noticed the smell of something burning and then saw the receptacle on the wall smoking. The welder unplugged the vent fan and contacted the electrician to kill power to the receptacle. Flames began coming out of the receptacle and a worker used a 20lbs. dry chemical fire extinguisher to put out the flame. No personnel were injured or no additional equipment was damaged beyond the receptacle.

A gas release  initiated a process shut-in at 16:45 hours.  While making rounds, the operator noticed gas seeping from a pinhole in the piping downstream of the production header. The operator made immediate notification to all personnel, shut-in platform, and bled down associated piping. No pollution event occurred.

While the crane operator was lowering a 6000# scaffolding basket with the load line on to the M/V, the scaffold basket struck the boats gangway handrail resulting in a damaged handrail on the gangway.

While backloading wireline equipment to the M/V, the wireline unit began to spin during the decent. The deck hand stopped the spin with the use of the tagline.  The door of the unit swung open and hit the side of the boat lifting it off it's hinge pins. The door fell into the Gulf of Mexico. This was the fourth lift of a planned ten lift load-out.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition
column24: A bundle of scaffolding material was being lifted with the crane. It was in a spot that was closer in than the crane boom could accommodate. Because of this, the rigger was pulling back on the lift as it was being lifted in order to miss the handrail. They didn't realize that the lift had gotten under the handrail until it was too late and the handrail was lifted out of its sockets and it fell into the water. There were no injuries and no additional damage to the platform. A temporary handrail was put in place utilizing scaffold material. Material has been purchased to permanently replace the handrail.

On July 15, the IP slipped off a beam that he was working on (~1ft above the deck) and his left shin and calf struck chiksan piping resulting in bruising and swelling.  Following the incident, the medic performed an examination and released the IP to full duty. On the morning of 7/20, the IP began complaining of increased swelling and pain and was sent in this afternoon on a regularly scheduled flight for further medical evaluation.

Production Supervisor detected a strange, burnt sulfurous smell in his office.  Shortly afterward, the alarm on the UPS/battery backup under his desk started beeping.  Upon closer inspection, it was determined the smell was being emitted from the UPS and the unit was very hot. He shut the unit down, removed it to a safe location and allowed it to cool.  Upon inspection of the removable battery pack, he found it to be swollen and disfigured. Replaced the UPS/battery backup with a new unit and properly disposed of the damaged unit.

On 07/21/2021 at ~20:00hrs the control room received a smoke alarm from the Upper Living Quarters, which caused a platform audible alarm requiring muster of personnel. After full muster and fast responders confirming no smoke or fire in the area, it was identified that a floor drying fan was turned on to circulate air and the alarm sounded right after the fan was turned on. After further inspection, the fan being used was not the proper fan for cooling the room and was full of dust, which was blown into the detector once operated.

Employee was putting food into the food waste Macerator (Food Grinder) when he noticed that the electric motor had started smoking. He stopped the Macerator and a person that was standing by called the control room and let them know about the Motor having smoke coming out of it. When the Electrician arrived the Macerator motor was no longer smoking, the Electrician opened the Breaker and did a LOTO of the motor. The cause was determined to be a fork entering the macerator. The motor was replaced.

At 2:44 p.m. in the afternoon - During operator rounds, observed a leak in the overhead piping between HP and IP Separator. An ESD was initiated. A PA announcement was made stating a gas release. All personnel mustered in the galley. Piping was then isolated and the Asset was depressurized. A new spool piece was fabricated for installation over the weekend of July 23, 2021.  Piping repair was completed Sunday, July 25, 2021 at 20:00 hrs.  Facility was brought back on line at 02:30 hrs, Monday, July 26, 2021.

Individual Inspected the load bank and started running a battery capacity test on the hurricane UPS battery on 07/22/2021 and noticed some odd indications during the test.  The next morning 07/23/2021, the load bank was inspected again to try and solve the issue before running another test.  During inspection, it was found that one of the small contactors was partially melted likely due to a bad connection heating up during the test. No smoke or smell was detected at the time.

On July 22, 2021 at approximately 16:20 hours, the 20% ASH alarm sounded for compressor #3 on ST 151 Compressor platform.  Upon hearing the alarm, the PIC noticed the gas reading continue to climb via his SCADA controls and at that time shut in the #3 compressor prior to reaching 40%.  Workers on the facility reported to the muster area and roll call was taken by platform PIC.  Once all personnel were accounted for, the platform PIC and mechanic went to investigate cause of alarm. The investigation determined the following contributing factors:  
- Loose bolts were identified on a flange between the fuel manifold and the fuel valve. This allowed fuel gas to leak around the gasket, into the rocker arm box and subsequently into the compressor building.  
- The bolts are believed to have loosened due to normal operation of the compressor over time.

A fire event occurred at 2230 hours.  The construction crew was cutting out deck plate sections inside of a PWE when the hot slag built up in one spot causing a very small fire inside the PWE on panel material.  The fire was immediately extinguished by the fire watch via a fire extinguisher and SWA was initiated.

CI was removing the magnet (Approximate 35 pounds) from trip tank to remove metal shavings from milling operation. CI lost his footing and fell from work platform. During his fall, the magnet struck the right middle finger resulting in a crushing avulsion injury. CI can not say if he slipped or what was the cause of his loss of footing. Platform is 2' x 4' in surface dimensions and elevated 2' above deck. Immediate report to supervisor and UWA. Safety/Medic examined and provided first aid. Arranged for transportation of CI. Made required notifications.

The IP stepped out of the galley, misjudged the step outside the galley which steps down onto the grating, and landed on one foot, breaking his leg above the ankle. He was flown for medical treatment. The IP was supervising blast and painting crew, but at the time of the injury he was walking out on deck from the galley.

IP was holding onto the Self Adjusting Basket (SAB) railing while climbing into the basket. IP's coworker, who was already in the basket, opened the SAB basket gate allowing the IP to enter. As a result, the gate pinched the IP's right ring finger between the gate and SAB basket railing. IP was evacuated. Pinched tip of right ring finger. Recieved stitches.

Contract crane operator reported to the PIC that main hoist line jumped sheave during vessel loading/back loading operations. Upon inspection of the cable it was noted that cable damage had occurred during this event. The cable has been repaired and the crane is back in service.

IP was eating around 4:45 PM. While eating a piece of steak became lodged in his throat. He got up and went to the garbage can attempting to throw up and dislodge food, unsuccessful. Then he proceeded to the near by rest room. A co-worker went to the rest room to assist and then called for the medic. Rig medic examined IP, and consulted with H&P company doctor. Unable to dislodge the obstruction, was advised by company doctor to send in for further medical assistance.

An injury occurred at GC-18 (G04940) at 1355 hours on 07.27.2021. A third-party valve technician was tasked with conducting routine maintenance on valves located on the LP/HP gas header.  His work scope at the time of the event included lubrication of the valves in situ. During greasing operations of the "Piper" header valves, the valve technician applied 2,000 psi of grease to the valve, and it became pressure locked in the open position. The valve technician used the valve handle extension to operate the valve. While pushing down on the valve handle the pressure released causing the tool to swing down and pinch his left ring finger between the valve handle tool and another valve. This resulted in the tip of the finger being fractured and an open laceration that required three stitches to close.

Third party vendors were performing bolt torquing operations on the VRU gas compressor piping using an air-driven impact driver (jGun).   The IP completed the torque on one of the nuts and was in the process of removing the gun from the nut at the time of the event.  While removing the gun, he accidentally engaged the trigger, causing the impact driver to actuate and tighten up.  This caused the J-gun to shift clockwise rapidly and pinch the IP's left thumb between the gun and the vertical gas piping.  Although the IP was wearing impact-resistant gloves, the IP's thumbnail was separated from the thumb. The jobsite was secured and the IP immediately reported to the medic's office for evaluation.

A contract electrician was bending over moving battery's inside of a SCADA battery box when he felt a discomfort in his lower back. Contract electrician remained at work working until this morning when he requested to go in for further medical evaluation. Contract electrician was transported to clinic. He received a release to light duty and was diagnosed with a muscle strain and muscle spasm in his lower back.

A worker was tightening the last 2 -bolts on the cover of a strainer for Wet Oil Slop Tank ABJ-415. While tightening a nut, the box wrench that was being used slipped from the nut and struck the worker's left knee. This caused an injury with pain and swelling. The medic examined the injured person with a consultation from Medical Control. A decision was made to medevac the injured person. A representative from the injured person's company met and escorted him to a follow up medical examination.

IP consulted site medic for pain in his left arm and shoulder. He stated he slipped in the shower and caught himself with his left arm. IP was given OTC Tylenol, ice for injured area and rested for 24 hours, after which IP was flown to shore for evaluation on regular scheduled flight.

While cooking steaks on the Char Broiler in the Galley, a grease fire flared up. Camp Boss was cooking steaks to order on the galley Char Broiler. The grease that was dripping into the waste tray below the heating element, flared up allowing flames to burn up through the cooking grates. Camp Boss tried using salt to smother the flames, but was unsuccessful at smothering the flames. The Prep-Cook laid a fire blanket over the flames and the Galley hand discharged a Dry Chemical extinguisher which extinguished the flames.

column22: Pipeline Lay Vessel Pb: Lay Barge
column24: At ~19:30 hrs, the vessel while using the main hook of the crane to lift THS from the seabed, the weight for the safety switch on the crane jib suddenly parted. The lift was stopped and the situation assessed by the captain, chief officer and crane driver. With special attention so that nobody was in the vicinity of the load or the crane jib, the lifting operation was completed and the load was landed onto the deck of M/S Charlotte, as planned. After that the crane was lowered onto the deck for inspection and repairs. Inspection showed all four bolts used to mount the two parts of the weight around the crane wire had parted, probably due to the vibrations of the crane wire during the lift. Three of the bolts had been dropped on the sea, while one was remaining in place. Inspected damage and commenced repairs. Inspected crane for other possible damages, crane found to be in good condition apart from the safety switch weight.

Water maker gasket failed causing oil to leak out into the skid and onto the engine.  The engine didn't shut off and kept running since the leak was small resulting in smoke which triggered the smoke detector.  The detector caused a full facility muster and facility shut in.  After investigation it was determined that there was no sign of fire, charring, soot or signs of degradation.  It was just smoke from the engine and hot oil.  No injuries associated with this incident. The gasket failed only because the bearings wore down causing the failure.

Construction personnel were hot bolting on corroded piping, when a pin hole leak was sprung on the fuel gas scrubber drain line at the outlet flange.  Operations immediately shut in the platform and installed a temporary clamp until repairs could be made.  Construction personnel replaced the outlet flange on 08.01.2021 and the fuel gas scrubber was placed back in service. Repair cost:  $2,661

At approximately 11:30 hours on July 31, 2021, AI and a production operator coworker were using a swing rope to transfer from facility to the M/V.  The first production operator made a successful transfer.  During the AI's transfer, he struck his left shin on the rear of the vessel as he completed the swing.  His coworker assisted him on the jump deck and noticed that he was bleeding.  The workers offered the AI first aid care on the vessel and notified the PIC on the facility of the event.  The PIC utilized the crane and personnel basket to get the AI back to the facility from the vessel.  Following transfer back the platform, the AI was flown to shore by the field helicopter for medical evaluation.  The AI was treated and received 8 sutures for the laceration and subsequently released to full duty.

While the crane operator was backloading a cargo box it contacted an aluminum ramp that was stored against the side rail of the M/V. The impact caused damage to the aluminum ramp. The cargo box was then safely landed onto the deck of the boat. There were no injuries from this incident.

Crew was servicing Fire Pump B unit, fire pump was shut down from  previous service inspections/running. Crew was filling reservoir with diesel, sight glass was not reacting as expected then suddenly diesel came from filled tank vent spilling onto the muffler making contact with hot muffler, igniting diesel. Shut down diesel source, shut in facility. Extinguish fire with fire hose, Monitored hot spots for re-ignition. Facility was previously reduced to safe manning level as a result of CV-19 out break, no muster resulted.

IP employed as a Roustabout stated on 08/01/2021 at approximately 02:30 AM he placed his right foot onto the first step of a stairway to ascend to the next deck on the rig package.  His right foot slipped causing his leg to twist clockwise and he felt a sharp pain to the inside of his right knee.  IP called for help and was then escorted by the rig crew with a medical stair chair to the medic's office where he received 400 mg ibuprofen, ace bandage wrapping around the right knee, and an ice pack for swelling. Medic administered prescription pain killer to ease the IP's pain level to move him to the helicopter.  Personnel was sent in on med-evac helicopter for further treatment.

A fire occurred at approximately 10:10 hours on 08.01.2021 at the facility. Operators went to make normal rounds on the platform and they noticed black smoke coming from the stack on the heater treater. They immediately shut the burners down and pulled the cover and arrestor on the fire box. They noticed a small fire in the fire tube at the burner even though the burners had been shut off. The operators utilized a dry chemical extinguisher to put the incipient fire out. Due to the fire being extinguished, the operators then shut the platform in by use of the master panel.  After the platform shut in was safely completed, the operators investigated the fire tube and noted a small stream of fluid coming down from the first weld of the tube.

This morning on the facility, operators started the platform diesel air compressor located on the AQ structure top deck. No issues at this time. Then operators walked to the AP structure to start the gas compressor. After the operators started the gas compressor on the AP structure, they both returned to the AQ structure. One of the operators went to the air compressor located on the top deck of the AQ structure to shut it down as it was no longer needed when a small flame about 3"-4" was observed. The flame was extinguished immediately using a 30# portable fire extinguisher. The battery for the diesel air compressor was then disconnected. No further damage to the diesel air compressor or facility occurred. No pollution occurred. No injuries reported as a result of this incident.

At approximately 6:45 pm operators and other facility personnel smelled smoke on the production deck. Lead Operator conducted on site investigation to identify the source and discovered the Instrument Air After Cooler was emitting smoke with visible flame coming out of the top of the unit. Additionally, the piping on the suction for the Air Cooler was smoldering from charred paint with evidence of intense heat. Power to the unit was shut off and the fire extinguished with portable extinguishers and a fire hose.
Root Cause: An investigation to determine the cause of this fire was initiated. Samples of liquids and residuals from the air compression system were gathered at the following key points: Cooler suction, cooler discharge, pipe inlet to cooler, and air cooler.
Samples were analyzed to determine the qualitative constituency and flammability. While no sample at or upstream of the fire exhibited potential fuel content, pyrophoric properties, nor flammability, it is suspected that potential hydrocarbon content from lube oil built up over time in a low spot in the header pipe from the discharge of the air compressors. It is also suspected that heat of compression at the discharge of the air compressors may have allowed for conditions to ignite the residual material within the pipe (i.e., presence of fuel source, oxygen, and heat) without any indication of a pyrophoric event. This was tentatively confirmed with the presence of deposits in the air cooler, downstream of the fire location, that exhibited flammability potential.
Corrective Action: The affected suction and header piping and other nearby equipment affected by heat or flame will be replaced. Additional equipment will be installed to allow operators to drain any buildup of lube oils or other residuals to avoid any similar occurrence.

On 8/23/2021 @ approximately 1700 while preparing the SS253-F platform for Decommissioning, EcoServe employee Jean Paul Mouton, a tank / vessel cleaning technician, was directed by his supervisor to start draining pressure from the 2" Meter Run Piping of the Gas Lift Header (GAS #4459) on the cellar deck of the platform.  The employee located the blind flange on the header with a 1" ball valve containing a 1" plug. The line was 15-18' long with a block valve on one end and several needle valves. The block valve was closed with apparent pressure trapped from the valve to the blind which was unknown to the employee who open the valve without first checking for and bleeding off pressure under control of the needle valve. When the employee opened the valve trapped pressure released onto the sleeve of his cover-all contacting his left forearm and hand. The employee sustained redness to the skin surface and was subsequently brought to shore for medical elevation. Employee was evacuated to shore on 8/23/21 at approximately 10:00PM. Employee was on the 4th day of a 14 day hitch.

Fieldwood Energy is investigating in conjunction with EcoServe HSE and will report contributing causes and corrective actions accordingly. 

8/25/2021 UPDATE: Ecoserv employee was evaluated at Gulf Regional Occ/Med Center and diagnosed with minor skin abrasion / redness (1st Aid) and released immediately to full duty / no restrictions. 

Based on the investigation and post incident interviews the following are writings specific to the root cause of the impactful event and provide prevention guidance to avoid such occurrences in the future.  Root Cause: The involved parties failed to identify PRIMARY and SECONDARY pressure relief controls and prior opening a discharge control device the internal pressure was not verified at a zero-energy state.  A) Primary pressure relief - Needle Valve used within the fluid processing or flow metering application as a device suited for pressure control.  B)Secondary pressure relief - 1" Ball Valve used within the fluid processing or flow metering application as a device to control fluid or flow, thus not intended to depressurize to atmosphere.  

Process Approach and Prevention Focus: 1) All pressures must be verified at a zero state before opening any discharge or access point of installed piping or a vessel. 2) Personnel opening discharge or access points must assume lines and/or valves are pressurized and contain liquids, therefore adequate secondary containment shall be in place and NO portion of one's body shall be positioned in a line of fire position.

Upon climbing down they noticed a chain binding down the crane boom. Operator walked back up and shut the crane down then made phone calls to report the incident. The crane boom is bent in several places as a result of the incident.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition

Battery Box Fire .  
At approximately 12:30PM on 09.03.2021, the crew arrived back at platform after Hurricane
Ida evacuation. While attempting to start the diesel generator to try to restore power and
communications, an operator observed a small flame in the 24V battery box for the generator PLC /control panel. They immediately proceeded to grab a fire extinguisher from a nearby extinguisher station and extinguished the flame. The battery box cover was still open at time of incident allowing for an unobstructed visual of smoke and flame. This was due to the fact that personnel had just
changed out the drained batteries in the battery bank with spare charged batteries on location.

Injury : On 09/05/2021 at approximately 08:00hrs:
the IP was working on top of the Dry Oil Tank attempting to repair the TSE loop circling the top corner of the tank. The IP needed to take  plyers out of their back left pocket, and therefore took off their gloves to reach
into their pocket. After removing the plyers and transitioning them to their right hand, the IP reached up with their left hand to help balance themselves on the beam directly above. When letting go of the beam they  received a
laceration on the tip of their middle left finger from a sharp blistered section of paint coating on the beam. They immediately came down from the Dry Oil Tank, wrapped the injured finger with a rag, and reported the
incident to the PIC in the office.

column24:
Platform Damage Description:
Several handrails missing on the +10.

Platform Damage Description:
Initial assessment from fly-by inspection:
- damage to ladder to/from the boat landing & cage guard around it
- boat landing is missing a section of grating
- damaged solar panels on helipad 
- foghorn control box is loose

- one piece of helideck skirting broken and fell to the stairway going down to the sump deck obstructing same and damaging two steps
- hand rail to the boat landing is broken, 
- damage to ladder and cage guard which looks to go to the vent scrubber

Generator sparks: While attempting to restore power, sparks were witnessed coming from the power generation end of the Auxiliary Generator during startup. The unit was shut down and secured. Upon further investigation, water was found leaking into the package from roof of the generator enclosure. The water was rain water following damage from Hurricane Ida.

Vessel had a fire alarm on vent at 11:59 AM due to lighting. Vent snuffing system dump all 10 bottles and put out fire before Fire Team responded to site of the alarm all other personal don lifejacket and muster at life boat A  all personal was accounted for. Fire team reported no fire, OIM call all clear from fire alarm at 12.05 PM.  POB of 22 at time of muster. Cleared alarms and reset safety systems, crew return to normal duties.

Crane mechanics (2) were conducting post hurricane maintenance checks on the crane. Lowering and raising the lifting block is part of the integrity check. One mechanic was operating the crane lowering the block up and down just inside the handrail, while the other was visually inspecting the lines for damage and other functionality parameters. Neither of the mechanics realized that there was a previously installed temporary dome shaped satellite dish near the handrail where they were lowering. The block came in contact with the dome and distorted it's shape in the form of an inward dent. The damage was not discovered until 9-11-21.

Missing equipment. On August 27, 2021, platform was evacuated ahead of Hurricane Ida.  Upon returning to the platform for damage assessments on September 9, 2021, it was found that 71 life jackets were missing.  Also missing were two fire hose reel covers and a Helifuel toolbox (small black plastic box containing two empty glass jars, box of kits to check moisture, bag of rags)  were missing. Corrective Action:  Materials have been ordered to replace the missing items.

Fire: This morning, the facility reported a small fire while performing hot work.  The facility remains shut in from hurricane Ida.  There were no injuries, no pollution or damages resulting. The fire was extinguished by bottled drinking water. A weld was being done on a 2" vent line using a plumbers plug as isolation. We believe the heat released hydrocarbons from pipe allowing a drip of oil to get passed the barrier. Stop work was initiated and safety stand down held.

A rig crane was in process of hoisting a 40' basket with drilling tools from the vessel.  As load was hoisted approximately 3-5 feet, crane operator began receiving load angle alarms which halted the ability to continue hoisting basket. Crane Operator immediately communicated the situation to boat captain. Boat captain waited to be on low side of swell and then attempted to get out from under basket. Subsequently, the basket made contact with gangway handrails as the stern rose, causing the handrails to bend.  Tag line(s) were attached to the basket.  Tag line(s) were not being held at the time of the incident.  This was not a blind lift.  Crane operator was communicating by radio.  At the time of the lift, the gangway was not in use and it was not specified if the boat crew had barricaded the gangway.

9-12-21: While tripping in the hole with 5" drill pipe, an employee (floorhand) had just latched up a stand of pipe and began to back away from the elevators. In the process of backing away from the elevators, IP stated that employee felt like they struck their right hand on something. When they removed the glove the IP noticed that the right small finger was bleeding and cut open at the tip. IP was seen by rig medic and directed to go to shore for further evaluation where it was discovered that the IP had a slight fracture to the tip of their small finger bone. IP's finger was put in a rigid brace and released to regular duty.

Fire: On 9/12/2021 at approximately 05:30 hours, galley and operations personnel noticed smoke near the stove.  Upon further investigation of the smoke, an operator noticed a small flame reflecting off the wall at the rear of the stove.  The Operator immediately grabbed a fire extinguisher and attempted to extinguish the flame.  Operator was unsuccessful in their first attempt due to the angle at which they were positioned.  Operator then pulled the stove forward and successfully extinguished the flame which was identified as being in a void area of the stove.  During this time, the platform PIC isolated power to the stove using the breaker. No injury or environmental damage occurred as a result of this event.  No damage was noted to the stove or the facility.  A muster was not required.

Facility was pressuring up during cold start up after returning from storm evacuation. Cameras detected seep on 2 inch valve and seep from gasket on door to gas filter separator. Isolated and bled system down to make repairs. Replaced packing in valve and replaced gasket.

Personnel Transfer: While conducting a personnel basket transfer from a vessel to a platform at approximately 12:00 hours on 09/15/2021, one of the three passengers on the collapsible basket fell into the water.  The event occurred just after the basket was lifted from the deck of the vessel with the crane.  As the crane began to lift the load and the basket was no longer in contact with vessel, the basket began to shift towards the front bit and railings.  The affected individual (AI) being concerned a fellow passenger would strike the vessel with their back stuck out their right leg to push off the bit and alter the path of the basket.  As the AI tried to push off, their foot slipped causing the AI to lose their balance and fall from the basket to the water (approximately 8-10' fall distance).  Seeing what occurred the Captain immediately announced man overboard.  The vessel crew responded quickly and retrieved the AI to the vessel.  The AI complained of sore ribs so they were evaluated by the rig medic on board facility and then transferred onshore via field helicopter for further evaluation onshore. AI was diagnosed with rib contusions on the right side, minor abrasions and back spasm. AI was released to full duty.

Lifting incident: At 1445 hrs on September 16, 2021 while offloading the vessel, the ADCP frame that was in an 8x24 basket was being lifted from the boat deck to theplatform by the AFT Crane. The slings became entangled on the lift causing a sensor housing to be broken off the frame of the ADCP. The sensor fell into the basket and the lift was completed without further issue.

Lifting: Workers were completing sanding and prep work for paint job on the south side of the facility living quarters at height in a personnel "spider lift" basket. While workers began to descend in basket, the basket came in contact with an outdoor hazardous location light fixture. The weight of the basket caused the bolts to break and the fixture to move slightly.

Lifting: While orienting the crane to begin making deck-to-deck lifts, the crane operator was booming up on the crane and noticed a leak coming from the boom tip.  At that time, the operator noticed they only had the ability to continue booming up and could not boom down.  The crane operator stopped the job and alerted the PIC of the issue.  A third-party crane mechanic was onboard.  The mechanic was able to identify leak was associated with anti-two block hose.  He was able to cap the connection and lower the boom into the cradle until permanent repairs can be made.  The crane is currently out of service.

Lifting: A third-party crane maintenance company had replaced the gantry sheaves on the platform crane.  Scaffolding had been erected to allow access to the sheave.  The scaffold builders were in the process of rigging down the scaffolding.  While attempting to lower the second scaffold crossbar, it was dropped from a height of approximately 40 feet.  The bar struck the walkway around the cab of the crane and went overboard.  It was not recovered.  The drop zone had been barricaded off prior to the erection of the scaffolding and no personnel was in the line of fire.

Lifting: On 9/20/21 at approximately 4:30pm, a forklift was going to be used to move a bulk material super sack containing G-Seal (LCM).  As the forklift operator started to tilt back on the forks to lift the super sack, the front two lifting straps parted.  The other two straps did not part.  The super sack remained on the deck and it was not suspended at any time.  In the process of attempting to secure the super sack and stabilize it on the deck, approximately 1.5 gallons of G-seal dry chemical product spilled onto the sack room deck.  The job was stopped, and the spillage was cleaned up.  There was no potential for any of the material to affect any personnel or go overboard.  There were no dropped objects as a result of the incident and no personnel were injured.

On September 20, 2021 at approximately 9:55 AM, an employee working at the facility was engaged in normal work activities that required the individual to transition over a section of process piping approximately waist high. While transitioning their weight from one leg to the other, over top of the piping, the employee felt a popping sensation in their left knee causing the employee to collapse onto the decking immediately below the piping.  During this time the employee was with two other co-workers. One worker stayed with the employee while the other notified the HSE lead who was nearby.

Vandalized facility: One personnel flew to the platform to gather clothes out of lockers in living quarters and noticed that inside of the living quarters had been trashed. They then made a walk through and found the Platform had been vandalized, tools stolen, lockers broken into,  wiring cut etc.

Notification was given of a material handling incident that occurred in the South Marsh Island Area. During the process of backloading a connex box, the crane operator safely lowered the load to the deck and the deckhand was attempting to remove the rigging when a swell came through and shifted the load pinching their finger between the stinger and the hook.  There was no injury associated with the incident and the IP was wearing impact gloves. Production personnel went down to the M/V to evaluate the employee and give coaching on the line of fire and using situational awareness at all times.

A gas detector alarm was tripped during the process of bleeding down an isolation for upcoming work. The relased vapor was a controlled release and all the gas detection, in the area of the compressor isolation, was in by pass.  This lead to a full  POB muster.

In the Ewing Bank area, operator reported a a material handling incident where the item was not retrievable (lost overboard). A construction crew was attempting to remove a section of steel tubing from a damaged portion of a facility building damaged during hurricane Ida.  After the crew rigged up to the tubing, the crew made two cuts releasing the load from the building.  The load unexpectedly rotated due to the rigging placement, and an unsecured corroded section of tubing fell approximately into the GOM.  No personnel or equipment was affected as the section was over water.  Item was not retrievable (lost overboard).

Talos Energy Offshore LLC will provide a written follow up report upon completion of the incident investigation as required by 30 CFR 250.190.

column24: A fire broke out in a compressor building with a Fixed facility stucture in the Main Pass, South And East Addition area. The Facility was ESD'd and evacuated to an Offshore Support Vessel, where the crew was dropped off at a nearby facility while the Offshore Support Vessel returned to extinguish the fire using her onboard fire monitor. The Offshore Support Vessel remained on station and was joined by the another to deluge the facility all night of the incident.  A damage assessment and root cause team was placed on site to investigate the incident. As a result, the Unit was removed and sent for tear down and rebuilding.

An FPSO located with the Walker Ridge Area reported two gas detectors alarms, initiating a facility ESD. Simultaneously, the Gas Release alarms sounded, triggering a full facility muster. The ICS team accounted for POB, confirming all personnel safe with a full Muster. When the facility was "blown-down" and confirmation made that gas was no longer present in the area. An Emergency Response Team was dispatched to locate and isolate the source of release.  Upon investigation, a needle valve was found in the open position with the isolation plug removed.  Corrective Action was taken where the   equipment was then isolated, and notification made to the ICS team. The facility was deemed safe, at which time the OIM released the ICS team and ship crew members back to general duties.  The MGC A was in the process of being brought online after an extended period of downtime for maintenance. The LOPC became apparent the moment shutdown valves were opened, allowing gas to enter the unit.  No other HSE incidents were the result of this event.

A reported investigation of a crane / material handling incident that occurred in the Green Canyon Area. During crane handling operations, a super sack of material was dropped to the top deck.  At the time of the incident, the crane operator lifted the super sack (4000lbs) by the manufactured 2" straps that was shipped out inside a 6'X12' basket. As the crane operator then moved the load one of the manufactured straps parted causing all weight to shift to the remaining strap. All the weight shifting to the remaining strap caused it to part. This resulted in the super sack dropping to the grating below.  . The operation was shutdown until the investigation was completed.    No personnel were injured as a result of the incident and no property damaged.

After landing a load from the boat onto the drill deck, a metal clanging sound was heard. The crane operator and rigger noticed the weight from the anti-two block device had slid down the auxiliary line to the striker plate. A small piece of the anti-two block switch also fell to the drill deck. Crane was secured, and the crane mechanics were dispatched for investigation. No damage to the boom, cable or other parts of the crane was found and no evidence of impact to the boom.

Report of a material handling incident involing an offloading motor vessel using a crane with a metal sling becoming wedged under a 2" vent pipe on the operator's de-sander filter pot weighing 25000lbs. This was due to the movement of the vessel from the swells and wave action. When picking up the load the sling knocked off a section of vent pipe 2" x 1' in length causing it to go overboard. Notification has been made on the item lost overboard.

A rig within the Garden Bank Area  reported a crane incident while lifting an empty chemical tote of defoamer. As the crane moved the tote, the drain valve contacted a walkaround on the loading station, resulting in the drain valve being disconnecting from the threaded connection on the tote tank. A safety standdown was held with the crane crew, before work was resumed.  Additional information:  Tag line(s) were attached to the empty tote tank to control the tank.   Tag lines were being held at the time of the incident.  This was not a blind lift.  The crane operator was using a radio to communicate.

A low-level H2S Alarm was triggered on a Drilling ship operating in Mississippi Canyon after wash water was being pumped from sump tanks in mud pump room to a slugging pit using a diaphragm pump. Incident report on a Drilling ship operating in the Mississippi Canyon area. Reported gas dection leak on a Semi-submersible structure within the Mississippi Canyon Area. On a Drillship operating in the Green Canyon Area, it was noted that while transiting to pull the Subsea Tree on a Deepwater well, a 24 feet pack off service connection on the DPRRT pulling tool BHA fell to the sea bead.  Tool connection weighs approximately 700 pounds and dropped approximately 580 feet. On a SPAR facility within the East Breaks area, A contractor noticed smoke coming from the wiring box on top of the water heater recirculation pump. Contractor notified the control room and the power switch to the recirculation pump was turned off. Charring seen on the wires inside the box.  No fire or other damage noted.

On a Fixed facility within the West Delta Area, A technician was working on well panel and moving it to be repaired, the door opened in the back pinching a finger between the side of the panel and the hinge of the door. The technician was sent in for further medical evaluation, recieving wound treatment.

On a Semisubmersible facility in the Mississippi Canyon area while performing a 3 year purge inspection on an explosion-proof electrical box, located on SW Filters in panel, charring to wires and soot build-up inside of the box was identified. Water intrusion was also identified in the box. It is unknown at this time when the damage took place.  No alarms were activated due to the event.

- What is the purpose of the 3 year purge inspection? 
  Generally this is detailed inspection, meaning entry into the encloser or device encompassing a visual, close and detailed inspection under isolation.  Therefore, this type of inspection's purpose is to  highlight deficiencies not normally apparent without the use of access tools (e.g., wrench's, opening enclosures). 

- Was there any lost of production or shut down as a result of the charred wires and sooth build-up? 
  No loss of production or shut down

On a SPAR facility within the Mississippi Canyon Area, personnel were using an ROV to clean sea growth and clear the water visibility at the point of inspection. Personnel turned the Cavity-blaster on. Simultaneously personnel saw a flash from the electrical control box. Personnel observed smoke and a flash but no fire. The supply breaker tripped as designed and shut off power to the malfunctioning Cavity-blaster. An all STOP was immediately initiated. The event was reported to the OIM and the Cavi-Blaster was swapped out for the back up unit that was on site. Upon further inspection with the platform electrician and due to the visible signs of damage. It was determined there was a loose connection that caused the Arc-flash.

On a fixed facility within the South Marsh Island Area, operators noticed smoke coming around the platform compressor building.  The operators went to investigate the incident and noticed a fire coming from the 3" discharge line off the air compressor.  The operator sounded the alarm and everyone mustered and was accounted for.  The foreman and (2) operators shut off the breaker to the platform B compressor and extinguished the flame using a portable fire extinguisher.  The foreman continued to cool the 3" line by using a fire hose.  Initial investigation shows that the discharge line is insulated and covered a leak that allowed oil to get trapped and saturate the insulation and caught fire.

On a FIXED facility within the Mississippi Canyon Area, an operator's employee was attempting to move a life jacket box when they injured their back in trying to pick up the box. The employee was seen by doctor and given full release late in the afternoon, prescribed over the counter medication and is waiting on transportation to return to work this morning pending weather.

On a multi-service semi-submersible facility in the Mississippi Canyon area, an incident occured involving the vessel experiencing a power loss, resulting in a vessel blackout. Within 30 seconds back up power generation allowed for control recovery with thrusters available for DP. Vessel was brought back on DP with a minor drift of 1 meter noted.  Troubleshooting led to a faulty relay and was repaired.  No injuries, no damages. 
Cause - Troubleshooting found Generator #4 tripped due to an air stop on the fuel system which was caused by a fuel pump failure. The fuel pump was replaced upon discovery. Fault finding into the black ship caused by the Advanced Generator Supervisor (AGS) system was investigated. The AGS had failed to recognize that the #4 gen was experiencing fuel pump problems and remove it from the bus as designed.
Findings and corrections:  
 Solenoid valve on Diesel Generator No. 4 was determined to be defective that caused a voltage droop and subsequent reverse power failure on the day of the incident.  During this episode the AGS inadvertently tripped the other two diesel generators resulting in momentary black ship.  The Manufacturer  updated the the AGS protection to include: 
- "Net voltage to AGS" to 1, to send the net voltage for calculation. 
- "Inconsistency on delay" from 5 seconds to 10 seconds.  This delays the switching of the KVAr signal from measured to calculated. 
Vessel crew created a pneumatic jig that simulated the previous fault, including the same movement for Kw, fuel rack and frequency.  AGS witnessed two tests on Diesel Generator No. 4 and one test on Diesel Generator No 3 with the simulated fault using the updated AGS protection system parameters.  AGS was able to correctly identify the healthy generators while tripping the simulated fault generator on reverse power with the ring bus remaining connected.   

All testing on the AGS protection system completed to satisfaction of attending Surveyor.   

Note - ABS Survey Report Attached.

On a TLP facility within the Mississippi Canyon, while assessing damage from Hurricane Ida, the asset was advised to swap a card which resulted in failure of the processor. The operator reported to USCG some degraded fire detection ability in mostly utility and quarters areas, however all firefighting systems are operational.  Corrective Action:  Mitigations put in place with 24 hour fire watch rounds, fire-fighting systems all still work, drilling has ceased and the asset is not producing. USCG approved the mitigations as a temporary measure until we install the spare fire panel motherboard.  The Fire panel was put back into service.  The repair cost was over (>) $25,000.

On a FIXED facility within the Eugene Island Area, while bringing the platform back online following a process upset, the flare boom was ignited by a lightning strike.  Although listed as a flare boom it is not normally lit.  The flame on flare boom self extinguished a short time after facility came online.  Approximately 20 minutes later another lightning strike occurred that ignited the vent line of the wet and dry oil storage tanks.  Operators initially tried to extinguish the flame using a water hose but they were unsuccessful.  At that time, they decided to connect nitrogen through the drain line of the oil tanks vent line.  The nitrogen purge successfully extinguished the flame. No injury or damage to the facility or environment occurred as a result of this event.  A muster did not occur.

On a FIXED facility within the South Timbalier Area,  while lowering an air tugger from the deck of the liftboat, the liftboat auxiliary crane boom contacted and damaged an inflatable lift raft cannister mounted near the first floor of the living quarters platform.  Stop work authority was immediately invoked and the facility Person In Charge (PIC) was notified.  The life raft was placed out of service.  Muster points and raft assignments on location were updated accordingly.  The life raft cannister (fiberglass) was damaged by crane boom contact.  Estimated repair cost for life raft cannister was approximately < $25,000.  No injury to personnel, harm to the environment or damage to crane boom occurred.

On a Drillship facility operating within the Walker Ridge Area, the DCQ received a Fire and Gas System  single smoke alarm for the Energy Storage Room.  The Chief Mate and 3rd Mate on watch were dispatched to investigate and the 3rd Mate arrived shortly after and confirmed.  Shortly after, the F&G system received a second smoke alarm and the system automatically activated the GA/PA as designed.  All personnel Mustered and responded accordingly, and the Well was made safe.  Fire was initially put out with portable CO2, but quickly re-flashed and then finally extinguished at with portable CO2 Extinguishers.  Initial Muster was achieved in 13 minutes, and a confirmed full muster achieved in 20 minutes.  Once fire was out, reflash watch set and maintained while the electrical department and engineering confirmed safe to secure.  Non-essential personnel was released.  Re-Flash watch maintained while Crews investigate and determine cause.
Damaged Equipment / Initial Assessment - Ultra capacitor module failed in cabinet P311 in Energy storage room. This is on the drilling drive bus for port drilling lineup. Appears to be internal failure of the unit upon initial assessment.
NO injuries to personnel, the environment, or damage to the integrity of the hull structure.  
No loss or affect to the DP Station Keeping or Safety of the Well Bore.

During a chemical transfer, a contract operator was not aware of the differently positioned 2-inch drain on one tote.  The open/close valve was situated opposite from what she was used to as as she "closed" the valve before removing the cap, she unknowingly opened the valve.  As she removed the cap to hook up the drain hose, a little over 5 gal. of "Corrtreat 12254" spewed out, drenching her. She attempted to close the valve but the lock device engaged and have her a difficult time. After finally closing it back up, she was quickly escorted to a safety shower to rinse the chemical off her thoroughly. She took a second shower in the quarters area and was evacuated to on onshore clinic for a medical evaluation. She was cleared to return to work without restrictions. The corrective measures to prevent reoccurence include the preparation and implementation of a daily checklist for wellbay operators identifying key tasks and additional safety measures, PPE and JSAs specific for chemical transfer operations.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition
column24: On a FIXED facility within theMain Pass Area, South And East Addition, At 16:50 this afternoon, MP69 personnel reported that a 2" regulator on the platform gas supply line failed and began releasing fuel gas to atmosphere. The fuel gas system was isolated. Platform is currently operating on diesel generators. Investigation to determine the root cause of the equipment failure is underway. Regulator will be replaced with new.

On a FIXED facility within the Ship Shoal Area, a material handling incident occurred. A diver was working on connecting heavy lift slings to platform jacket leg and they fell off into the water. The diver did not realize the temporary handrail barricades had been removed. The diver retrieved the items with the personnel basket and brought back onto the deck. The IP sustained no injuries and was cleared by the medic to return to work.

On a TLP facility within the Mississippi Canyon Area, a DOCO Insulators' employee dislocated their shoulder while climbing on scaffolding.  The employee was able to reset the shoulder into the socket and report to medical.   Note: The worker has a preexisting condition.  No medical treatment was administered, however, the employee's condition continued to be monitored.  At approximately 6:00 pm the employee reported that pain had not subsided and the decision was made to medivac the IP onshore for further evaluation.   Upon evaluation by the Urgent Care facility, no medical procedures were performed.  Diagnoses was pain in right shoulder and subluxation not a dislocation. With a subluxation the muscles, ligaments and tendons are loose and allows the joint come out of socket partially but snaps back in place without medical intervention.  Later the employee was released as fit for duty without restrictions.

On a TLP facility within the Walker Ridge Area, the east crane operator was in the process of backloading the M/V with trash bags from the facility weighing 800lbs total. The vessel shifted causing the load to lift from the deck. When the loaded lifted from the deck, it moved towards the bulwark which contacted the IP's left leg which then made contact with the bulwark. The boat was positioned parallel to the structure on the east side, experiencing small waves (1-4ft) with wind speeds 11-16 knots. Material: 4' cube, 800lbs., trash, white super sacks. Employee on the M/V was not injured during this crane event. No equipment or structure were damaged during this crane event.

On a Drillship facility operating within the Mississippi Canyon, a 4.5 inch drill pipe was inserted into the rat hole for derrick management at well.  When slack was made, the traveling block came in contact with the top of the joiner pipe. The joiner pipe was damaged.  No injuries occurred as a result of this incident.  Corrective Action: Record the serial number when picking up each joint of drill pipe instead of recording all of the serial numbers when the bundle is laid on the pipe skate.
