On a supply vessel operating within the Mississippi Canyon  Area, a deck crewmember was in the process of picking up a load to re-locate to the forward area of the deck to be able to transfer Barite to the Rig. The deck crew connected the lifting sling from the load unit to the crane line. However, when the crane operator proceeded to pick the load up with the direction of the supply vessel Banksman, a sea swell moved the boat upward causing the sling to loosen and wrap around the lower section of the units ladder and a control knob from control panel. As the boat lowered when the sea swell moved the lifting sling tighten causing minor damage to both the lower section of the ladder and the control handle. Note: Winds SE 12 knots and seas 4 ft.

On a FIXED facility within the Green Canyon Area a gas release incident occured. While an operator was making rounds, gas blowing from 2" piping was observed on the Gas Scrubber. The Operator quickly isolated & bled down the system. No hydrocarbons went overboard due to solid decking & containment. The construction crew was on location and built a replacement spool piece. The repairs were completed, hydro tested, and the gas scrubber placed back in service on 10.02.2021.  The platform was shut in for 6 hours while repairs were made.  Property Damage: 2" XH 45 degree elbow
Repair Cost: <$25,000

On a FIXED facility within the Vermilion Area, an incident occurred while scaffolding crew, with help from the construction crew, started assembling the scaffolding under the south side of the platform and transferring a rack of scaffold material with a crane and an air tugger to the top of jacket area. A 2" x 10' nylon strap parted while being used to transfer the load to the top of jacket, prior to entering the Gulf of Mexico. The stitching that held the strap together separated without warning, starting from the lifting eye where the rack was connected, all the way to the opposite lifting eye of the strap. 
Personnel utilized improper rigging by placing the tugger shackle inside the nylon sling eye for load transfer contributing in the nylon strap failure. The air tugger that was used to pull the rack into the top of the jacket area was connected by a shackle to the lifting eye of the nylon strap alone with the shackle that supported the full weight of the scaffold rack. This caused excessive stress on the lifting eye of the nylon strap that failed. The correct rigging of this set up should have been the shackle of the air tugger connected to the final load shackle. This would have reduced the stress on the nylon strap from two points to one point. No injuries or facility muster occurred during this incident.

October 2, 2021: during a line ride, an oil sheen was detected off the coastline and reported to the platform personnel at approximately 8:00 am PT. Upon notification of the oil sheen, platform personnel initiated the Oil Spill Response Plan and notified regulatory agencies. On October 3, it was announced that a Unified Command was established to respond to the oil spill. The cause, timing, and details regarding the spill are currently being investigated and this information is preliminary.
Cause Update, 3-17-22: During a large winter storm on January 25, 2021, the two supertankers were driven by winds and waves and drug their anchors across the seafloor and into areas where federal law prohibits anchoring. As the two supertankers dragged their anchors, both anchors hooked onto the concrete-encased pipeline and dragged a 4,000-foot section of the pipeline across the seafloor. The anchor-dragging bent and bowed the pipeline, displacing some parts of the pipeline by more than 100 feet and breaking off the concrete casing around the pipeline. Neither vessel nor the Marine Exchange of Southern California, responsible for managing ship positions in the harbor, informed anyone at Beta or Amplify that there was an anchor dragging incident across the exclusion zone. 
Timing Update 3-17-22: Over the course of the later afternoon and evening of October 1, the offshore platform and onshore pipeline personnel worked together to troubleshoot and rectify what were believed to be false leak detection system alarms. Following each alarm, the crews investigated various components of the platform and the pipeline's instrumentalities to determine what could be contributing to what were thought to be false alarms. Unbeknownst to the crew during this period, and further complicating their efforts, however, was the fact that the pipeline's leak detection system was not functioning as designed, but was repeatedly and wrongly signaling a potential leak at the platform where no leak could be detected by the platform personnel and where no leak was occurring. Instead, as the factual record shows today, the leak occurred over four miles away, where the pipeline had been displaced more than 100 feet by a ship's anchor - a fact not shared with knowledge of that anchor -dragging incident. Had the crew known there was an actual oil spill in the water, they would have shut down the pipeline immediately. When a line ride the morning of October 2 identified a sheen in the water, the Company immediately began to execute its federally-approved oil spill response plan. BOEM Row/Segment Number P00547; Pipeline Segment #2610300

On a FIXED facility within the West Delta Area, a contract crane mechanic was working from a ladder to drive a heel pin into the crane boom heel when the crane boom shifted, causing the pin to dislodge, striking the worker in the right side of their face. The worker was approximately 1 foot away from the boom pin when it dislodged. The strike caused the worker to fall from the ladder, approximately 4'. The workers fall protection arrested the fall. The worker was evaluated by on-site paramedics, and at this time, only minor bruising a pain has been observed; however, the worker is being evacuated via SAR for further evaluation by an onshore medical director. 
The injured worker was evaluated onshore with no additional injury noted. Was discharged to full duty. Event remains a First Aid Case. Investigation is ongoing. At this time, we have learned that an eddy swell caused the semisubmersible, which was holding the new crane boom, to move. This movement caused the boom to shift. As the boom shifted, the involved worker reached up to brace the 35# pin, but the pin dislodged and the worker lost balance. A safety stand-down was initiated to discuss the initial findings, including line of fire risk. The remaining heel pin will be installed using hydraulic equipment mobilized to the platform to eliminate the need for the semisubmersible and for workers to be at height during the pin installation.

On a SPAR facility within the Garden Banks Area, two gas leaks were discovered: one on the 4" Eductor line to the VRU and one on the 4" VRU discharge line. After discussion it was decided to shutdown the facility and make repairs. Update: The old piping is being cut out and prepping to weld new flanges. The new piping was installed.

On a FIXED facility within the High Island Area, a contractor was walking over the steps on the skid beam and when the contractor reached the bottom of the steps where the grating and skid deck slightly gave way under their heel, causing a knee strain.  The IP was evaluated to have a torn ligaments in the knee. More medical evaluation is planned for IP.

On a TLP facility within the Viosca Knoll.  IP was holding back up wrench on nut using a box end wrench.  Coworker applied torque with an air operated impact wrench.  IP's finger tip was smashed between wrench and fan housing causing a laceration.  IP was sent in for medical evaluation and subsequently received stitches and release to full duty.

On a Rig facility operating within the Viosca Knoll Area, IP was cleaning out a paint locker so the locker could be moved to the welding shop to have one of the doors repaired. In the bottom back side of the locker was a two-part foam system, the system has two pressurized cans banded together. When in use the chemicals come through a hose on each can and mixes together at the nozzle to create foam. When the IP reached in to pull out the foam system, one of the bottles opened at the bottom causing the contents of the container to escape rapidly. It appears the bottle ruptured due to being rusted at the bottom and galvanic corrosion thinning the wall of the pressurized container and welding the shelf and container together. The IP received several small lacerations to the top and bottom of their hand. The IP was treated with first aid and returned to work with no restrictions.

On a Rig facility operating within the Viosca Knoll Area, a material handling incident involving a dropped object event that occurred. Two crew members were placing aluminum plating inside the paint locker as a new bottom shelf.  One member turned around to place one piece of plate on the grating and lean it against the handrail.  Instead of landing the plate on the grating, it landed in a 1" x 51.25" gap in grating dropping 28' to the walkway below.  Please see the pictures under the attachment section.  No person was injured or in the immediate area below at the time of the incident.

On a Semi-submersible facility within the Mississippi Canyon Area, smoke was observed coming from one of the dryers in the laundry room. No visible flames were observed. The alarm was activated by personnel that witnessed the smoke. Nobody was injured. The fire team responded, and an investigation was conducted. Response to comments: There was not any malfunction with the dryer. It's possible the wrong detergent was used and leaving some rags in the dryer that built up heat. Response to comments: The offshore team states that the ZEP powerplex was the suspect detergent so they have switched to Royal Brite Plus to prevent this from happening again.

Electrician entered the main Motor Control Center (MCC) and noticed smoke coming out of the main Beta Offshore Line Interrupter Switch Compartment. The electrician opened the Edith 34.5kv Line Interrupter Switch to shut off all shore power to both Edith and the Beta facilities. The affected equipment was installed by electrical contractors one week prior to the incident.

On a Rig facility within the Ewing Bank Area, a floorhand traversed over the top of hand rail on charging pump deck, in an attempt to access scaffolding work platform approximately 6 foot below. A ladder was not able to be installed to access the scaffolding work platform in this location. IP utilized the outside of the handrail to climb down to scaffold platform below. During the descent to the platform , IP's foot slipped causing a fall. Harness and lanyard stopped the fall after approximately 6 foot. IP was able to self-rescue by standing up on scaffolding platform below. Reported to medic on board with unspecified back pain. No other cuts/abrasions/bruising from fall. IP was flown by regular helicopter and being brought to Dr for further evaluation by his company HSE representative. Medical evaluation by an occupational medicine clinic found no internal injury. However, MRI confirmed that IP has pre-existing multiple-level degenerative disc disease.  
Further investigation into the incident have reclassified the incident as "Alleged Fall From Heights - First Aid". Noteworthy findings as follows:
- No personnel witnessed the alleged event. Co-worker for task was on the lower processing deck with his back to the IP during the alleged event timeframe.
- IP's weight and distance of claimed fall would be very likely to result in superficial/topical injuries at the contact points of the harness (i.e. inner thighs). No injuries/indications found. 
- The harness was evaluated for signs of involvement in a fall. The lanyards showed no indications of fall arrest (energy absorber deployment), nor were there any other indications of involvement of the harness in a fall arrest event.
- All medical evaluations resulted in no identification of injury associated with a fall arrest event. IP was determined to suffer from chronic condition (degenerative disc disease), for which he will seek continued care from his personal physician.
- The culmination of all diagnostic/evaluative processes and procedures was a full duty release with no restrictions.

On a Semi-submersible facility within the Mississippi Canyon Area, two smoke alarms were activated inside the North East hull. No smoke and no visible flame was observed and there was no smell of smoke.  Nobody was injured. The fire team responded, and an investigation was being conducted.  Investigation found alarms were set off by power tooling near vents. Update:
Background - All permits associated with power tooling in the hull that require the ventilation to be covered have a notation about leaving detectors in bypass when rigging up and down. 
Reported Incident Investigation results/actions - The smoke alarm was set off causing muster in NE pontoon and the control to prevent it from happening again will be to add to the following to the permit: when removing dirty filter media from intake ventilation in the pontoon, ventilation needs to be shut down and smokes placed in bypass. The PA and IA talked to the crew about placing smokes in bypass and shutting down ventilation when removing the dirty filter media in the toolbox talk. Language barrier between PA and some crew members is suspected as the problem as well. Moving forward, the PA will ensure everyone understands the plan clearly by using a translator in the toolbox talk.

On a FIXED facility within the Eugene Island Area Area, two contractor employees were unbolting a flange on a flow line using a hammer wrench and hammer. The injured employee (IP), an SSE was holding the hammer wrench when the second employee struck the wrench with a hammer. The IP's finger was smashed between the hammer wrench and a nut on the flange causing a laceration  The employee was immediately examined by the on-site Medic who rendered first Aid and wrapped the finger.  Medical evaluation reported that the IP sustained a minor partial amputation to the finger. The injury required minimal stitches to close and the IP was released to full duty.  Management has now committed to the use of a tool holder (not practical in all situations), specifically designed to handle / hold Hammer Wrenches and keep hands/fingers out of the striking zones.

On a Drillship operating within the Mississippi Canyon Area, after laying down the cementing head, the Aux drill crew was changing out the 6 5/8" Drill Pipe Elevator inserts from 45 deg tapper back to 18 deg tapper.  The insert slipped out of the Floorman's hand and pinched their finger between the insert and the Dill Pipe Elevators, causing a laceration to the finger. Onshore medical evaluation showed the individual received 6 sutures in his finger and was cleared for full return to work. No further treatment was given onshore and individual released for duty.

column24: On a FIXED facility within the Main Pass Area, South And East Addition, a Compressor 3rd stage discharge line failed during startup and before compressor was loaded. No further information given.

On a Rig platform facility within the Mississippi Canyon, a crane incident occurred with the crane crew as they were utilizing the tagline winch (also known as close radius winch) to land a load near the crane boom pedestal. Upon spooling the tagline winch back up on the drum the shackle, attached to the thimble, came in contact with the handrail and bent the handrail. No dropped object occurred, and no personnel were injured. Personnel were managing the red zone and staged a safe distance away at time of incident. The handrail is still intact. An inspection of the tagline winch is ongoing. No damage to the tagline winch is expected. Immediate action was taken to suspend use of tagline winches until the work instruction/permit is revised to prevent reoccurrence. An incident investigation will be conducted. Cost of the damages are <$25,000.

On a FIXED facility within the Garden Banks area, the IP was attempting to put a 6' bail into a becket; the becket moved and the bail slipped out of it.  As the becket began to fall sideways, the IP's hand was caught between the bail and the top of the hydraulic slips. The IP was wearing the appropriate impact gloves at the time of the incident, but suffered a laceration above the fingernail of the finger. IP was treated by the platform medic with ice and over the counter pain medicine.  Corrective Action:  Held a safety stand down to discuss with the crew on how we can change our JBD to prevent hand injuries while performing this task going forward. As of now, the plan will be to have a second individual using a push pole to stabilize the becket and utilize the winch to hold the bail upright while installing in the becket.  IP left on a medivac flight where medical evaluation where X-rays also confirmed a hairline fracture to the finger.

On a Drillship facility operating within the Mississippi Canyon area, two floorhands were in the process of sliding the manual 6 5/8" slips to the rotary, the bottom of the slips got caught on the track of the pipe catwalk machine near the rotary; subsequently, the slips tilted forward. The IP's grip slipped from the handle, resulting in a dislocated finger, which had to be put back into position by physician.  No other treatment was rendered.

On a Drillship facility within the Mississippi Canyon, a Crane boom came in contact with handrails on the drawworks deck while moving a load from the mechanic's shop hatch to the Aft Pod house hatch.  Bent handrails were the result of the contact with the boom.  No dropped objects or damage to the Crane occurred.  Corrective Action:  Stopped the operation, barricaded the area, inspected both crane boom and handrails for damage.  Additional information:  Estimate of the damage is less than $25,000.  Tag line(s) were attached to the load to control the cargo.  Tag lines were being held at the time of the incident.  This was a blind lift.  The crane operator was communicating by radio.  Handrail area was not barricaded at the time of the strike.

Crane operator was lifting a flip top roll-off bin from the cargo boat when sea conditions caused boat to shift its position.  This change in positioning caused two of the slings to wrap underneath the tracks for the lid of the roll-off as it was being lifted. No damage sustained to load or rigging.

On a Drillship facility within the Walker Ridge, while setting down a riser joint on skate the universal joint connection between the turning device and spreader beam was damaged. Work was stopped and damage assessed, no potential for drops or damage to crane.

On a SPAR facility within the Alaminos Canyon area, a contractor smashed their right ring finger between an existing handrail and a new handrail that was being lowered via a tugger. First Aid level care treatment was administered on-site. After onshore treatment, IP was released for work and no designation of RW/JT or LTI was assigned.

On a FIXED facility within the Grand Isle Area, while on the plus 10, a contractor was moving a sheet of grating into place. The grating was upright and one side was being held up by an air tugger and the contractor was controlling the opposite end. The individual stumbled while walking with the grating and landed on ankle. IP was looked at by the medic and but felt OK to stay offshore. However, symptoms didn't improve for 2 days, and when they realized it wasn't getting any better, they sent IP onshore for a medical evaluation. The results showed a small hairline fracture in a foot bone. The contractor's foot was placed in a walking boot and he will be on restricted duty for approximately 3 weeks.

On a FIXED facility within the Eugene Island Area, IP was picking up a plastic tote out of a basket. As the tote was being lifted, the tote slipped and the IP's hand got caught in between the tote and the basket. IP has a cut on finger and was being sent in to be evaluated. IP was evaluated by the facility's Medic. The evaluation determined the IP had a fracture of his left index fingertip and a laceration of the same fingertip which required 5 sutures. The IP was released to light duty.

On a FIXED facility within the West Cameron Area, a small flame occurred on a compressor's driver. The flame was identified during routine rounds, platform's ESD was pulled, and the flame was extinguished in under 1 minute with a hand held extinguisher. The flame was in the vicinity of the diver's turbo at the exhaust's "Y" pipe. The initial investigation indicates a turbo seal or turbo oil line failure. We will  continue to investigative to determine the cause. There was no injuries or damaged identified due to the flame.

On a FIXED facility within the West Cameron Area, IP was attempting to replace a roller standoff on a logging tool while tool was positioned in the tool rack. The tool rotated and shifted which resulted the IP's finger getting pinched between the tool and pallet skid. Note: No mechanical hoisting equipment contributed to tool rotation.  Corrective Action:  Worker was treated by onboard medic and sent in on crew change flight for further evaluation.  Safety Stand Down held to discuss incident and how to prevent re-occurrence.  Shore-based physician performed x-rays, and two fractures were identified on tip of injured finger.  The IP was placed on restricted work for 11 days beginning on October 17, 2021.

On a FIXED facility within the West Cameron Area, a fire alarm was activated in the turbine generator package thermal detector which shut down the turbine and activated the fire alarm and general muster. Fire team was dispatched and confirmed no fire in area. Full muster was achieved in 7 minutes. Upon troubleshooting, it was found that fan "B" had failed due to vibration earlier in the week and fan "A" failed due to a failed belt. As the belt on fan "A" weakened, the temperature inside the turbine increased which caused the activation of the fire alarm. 
There was no active fire and no injuries due to the event or muster.

On a SPAR facility within the Mississippi Canyon Area, an individual reported to the medical treatment room for examination of eye after reporting the feeling of a foreign object in the eye.   Prior to visiting the medic, the IP was needle gunning while wearing PPE and goggles. The IP's eye was flushed with a saline system.   Attempts were then made with a directed saline flush from a syringe at different angles in attempt to dislodge the remaining object ('speck'), but were unsuccessful.  Attempted to swipe object from IP's left eye with cotton swabs and were again unsuccessful at removing spec. IP was flown in to be seen at a medical treatment facility for further diagnosis.

On a TLP facility within the Garden Banks Area, a lighting cable on the lower walk around of the aft crane was found smoldering.  A group was in the process of performing the weekly equipment walk down on the aft crane when this cable was discovered. Corrective Action:  The circuit feeding the cable was immediately isolated and the OIM was notified. The cable has since been repaired and returned to service.  Damage estimate is less than $25,000.

On a FIXED facility within the Ship Shoal Area, while performing paraffin scratching, a paraffin solvent was being pumped into the well via a HP pump. The HP pump was being fed by a diaphragm pump. The diaphragm pump stopped pumping and the personnel bled the lines down. They were going to change the pump out and when they went to remove the lines, the solvent sprayed into their faces. Both personnel were assisted by other Liftboat/well work personnel with flushing their eyes with fresh water for over 10 minutes. Both parties stated they were fine. Both were released to full duty and are classified as First Aid cases.

On a FIXED facility within the Eugene Island Area, while making rounds on the platform an operator noticed smoke coming from the smoking area.  The operator saw smoke coming from a fire retardant tarp being used to cover water bottles in the area.  The operator immediately grabbed a nearby water hose and soaked the tarp with water. No injury or damage to the facility or environment occurred as a result of this event.  A muster did not occur.  Only damage was that of the tarp. This is initial and final report.
IP was opening a welding rod can when his hand slipped and caught the sharp edge of the lid. IP was sent onshore for further medical evaluation. IP received aid to the injury and was released.

On a FIXED facility within the Alaminos Canyon Area, a Multipurpose Supply Vessel (MPSV) was in the process of performing a subsea jumper install. While utilizing the main lift wire on the knuckle boom crane to raise a flexible jumper over the side of the vessel, a synthetic hold back sling parted. The synthetic hold back sling was not connected directly to the load but rather to the rigging apparatus. When the synthetic hold back sling failed, it caused the jumper to go vertical and the main crane wire to jump sheave at the boom tip. There was no injury to personnel and damage was limited to the synthetic hold back sling.  Corrective Action:  A visual inspection of the flexible jumper showed no sign of damage on deck. The synthetic sling was brand new and certified.  Reinstating the main crane wire into the boom tip sheave.

On a SPAR facility within the East Breaks Area, a galley rag was inadvertently washed and placed in the dryer. It began to scorch and smoke in the dryer. Corrective Action Identified: all crews are being retrained on laundry procedures.
