column24: On a FIXED facility within the Main Pass Area, South And East Addition, after a successful personnel transfer, the personnel basket was damaged when it was entangled with a stationary piece of equipment. The basket was taken out-of-service and replaced.

On a Drillship facility within the Green Canyon Area, a Roustabout  employee got their hand caught between the BOP cart top handrail and the riser. IP was in the process of running risers, installing clamps when the riser began to move from port to stbd.  At that point the riser caught their hand on the handrail.  IP was taken to the medic and DODI medical control and OIM were alerted.  Medevac was initiated. Employee sustained trauma to hand with  laceration, fracture and contusions.

While lifting a 500-gallon propane tank with the crane, one of the slings from the 4-ways got hung up on the valve located on the top of the tank. This caused the valve to break off the tank and began venting propane to atmosphere. The oiler contacted the control room and the flare was immediately shut off. The crane operator lifted the tank and hung it away from the platform until the venting stopped. The tank was then brought back to the platform and secured.

On a SPAR facility within Green Canyon Area, IP received injury from high pressure water gun, observing the function test of the nozzle, but got injured replacing and testing the UHP nozzle, while standing to the right of the test. IP received medical treatment at the facility and helicoptered to onshore hospital. IP was evaluated and released.

On a Semi-submersible facility within the Green Canyon Area, while a helicopter was on the helideck for scheduled passenger drop-off, the facility experienced a fire alarm on the helideck. The HLO and crane crew on the helideck at the time confirmed to the Control Room Operator no indication of fire or smoke. The facility responded by continuing the muster event that was initiated by the alarm. Fast responders mobilized to the helideck and confirmed no fire or smoke.  
The HLO continued helicopter operations since there was no indication of fire, and the helicopter departed the facility safely. The facility achieved full muster, and the muster event was stood down. Sotec was onsite and has inspected the detector and found no abnormalities. The detector was pointed to the west, directly at the sun since it was later in the day. Sotec believes this in combination with the helicopter exhaust and rotor turn caused the trip, by making the detector see a false 'flame". Automation is looking into the logic voting rights for the two detectors on the helideck.

On a SPAR facility within the East Breaks Area, electricians were testing the temporary generator prior to use.  After start-up of generator they observed smoke coming from the rental transformer panel.  After shutting down generator they opened the transformer panel and observed that wiring had arched and melted. Equipment was replaced with new equipment by contractor.

On a SPAR facility within the Green Canyon Area, while removing a button head grease fitting cap on a manual gas lift valve the fitting threads broke, ejecting the fitting resulting in a local gas release. Operations was notified and the facility was shut in. The line pressure was bled down and repair was made. Pressure associated with the gas release was 1600 psi with an estimated amount of 38.5ft3 gas released. Replacement cost is <$25,000. Facility did not muster. They were able to quickly isolate the leak (~45 seconds) and determine the pressure was bleeding down. No injury occurred.

On a Drillship facility within the Green Canyon Area,  In preparation to lay out 6-5/8" drill pipe, the drill floor requested more thread protectors.  The crane crew hooked to a white 1 ton bag full of loosley packed 6-5/8" tread protectors on the port transfer deck and was going to transport it to the pipe rack.  The banksman signaled the crane up and then performed an inspection to ensure there was no rips or tears.  There was no visual damage to the bag so the instruction was given to continue the lift. The Crane Operator swung the bag over the pipe rack  and came to stop 4ft. above a stack of drill pipe. This is when he noticed the straps were breaking one by one, and then the bag ripped. No injuries occurred. No equipment or structure damage.

During a decommissioning project, the 48" x 60" caisson was being lowered to the deck of the M/V by the crane on the Lift Boat.  After the end of the caisson was on the deck and being lowered the rest of the way down, the tail end slid across the deck.  This resulted in a damaged section of grating over a rudder assembly, a bent handrail, and a bent end on an exhaust pipe.  There were no personnel in the area and no injuries.  The cost for all repairs will be under $25K

Non-Work Related Fatality Onboard Rig - At approximately 06:30 an IP was found non-responsive with no vital signs in their stateroom. Vessel notified USCG Investigator. The USCG cleared the vessel to fly the body onshore. A flight departed the rig around 12:30 and transported the body stateside, where the body was released to the Coroner. Vessel notified the Marshall Islands by email communication at 10:03. A voice mail message was left with a manager within the dept at 08:43. This authority returned the call at 10:37.

An IP was moving material while performing house cleaning of the work area at approximately 0800 prior to performing maintenance on equipment.  IP reported to medic due to back pain.  Corrective Action:  Medic advised to send IP to shore for further medical evaluation.  Medevac flight was being arranged for October 25, 2021.  OIM later provided an update at 10:21 am on October 25, 2021 that symptoms that IP presented (sweating, pale skin in addition to back pain) have subsided and no longer considered for medevac or onshore evaluation.  OTC medication provided and IP monitored.  IP completed hitch and followed up with a physician upon returning home. IP was evaluated and treated with prescription medication and physical therapy; released to return to work without restrictions on 11/1/2021.

On a FIXED facility within the East Cameron Area, a fire that occurred when operators and mechanics were monitoring the booster compressor for a well due to recent flow changes and noted a small exhaust leak in the expansion joint area. Mechanics removed the original insulation to inspect the leak and take measurements for a replacement expansion joint. The mechanics then replaced the insulating blanket with a replacement from an equipment storage locker. During a period of approximately twenty minutes, the mechanics observed smoke emanating from the newly applied insulating blanket. The mechanics decided to remove the new insulating blanket for inspection. Upon removing the insulating blanket, a small incipient fire began on the approximately 8” x 30” blanket. Operators overseeing the work on the booster compressor initiated an emergency shut-in/shutdown of the platform. Additionally, Operators were there to
immediately apply dry chemical extinguishing agent to the insulating blanket. There were no injuries as a result of the fire.

The crane crew was preparing to bring wire line tools up from the work boat. The tools are 2 1/2" x 18' in size and were sent out in a 3'x35' basket. Due to limited deck space, the decision was made to move the tools from their basket to another basket that contained packer assemblies. The packer assemblies had to be brought up as well, so instead of bringing up 2 large baskets, the tools were placed with the packers. The packer assemblies and tools were brought up and laid out on the pipe rack and then the packer assembly basket was sent back down to the boat for storage. The crane operator then hooked to a smaller basket which was sitting under anther crane to back load it to the work boat. When the crane operator hoisted up on the basket it to swung slightly towards the center of the pipe rack about 2'. The operator set it back down in order to center the load and the basket landed on one of the wire line tools causing damage to a tool.

A compressor had just been started and was idling when it backfired and personnel saw a small flame on the unit near the exhaust manifold. The unit was immediately shut down and personnel extinguished the flame in less than 10 seconds with a handheld fire extinguisher. There were no injuries or pollution as a result of the incident. Damage appears to be only minor.

At approximately 8:00am a Motor Vessel was backing up to a boat landing to pick up  construction workers. Seas were calm with 3 foot swells. The platform boat landing was approximately 3 foot lower than the jump deck of the vessel. An IP in line to swing, climbed on the platform boat-landing handrail to increase the IP's elevation on the swing rope. The vessel was approximately 3' from the boat landing when the IP began to swing.  The IP was too low in relation to the higher vessel deck and did not reach the jump deck of the vessel. The IP lost his/her grip on the rope and fell into the water. The IP was immediately pulled from the water and was not injured. 



A company wide safety alert and been created and distributed on the hazards of Swing rope transfers as well as the proper procedures. The company has also communicated the learnings to the field.
Operator noticed a light fixture on the +17 level of the platform emitting smoke and sparking. The operator extinguished the smoking fixture with a fire extinguisher.

A vessel lined up the dehumidifier water circulation valves as per procedure. The Unit was Energized by closing the main disconnect and then turned the HOA (Hand-Off-Automatic) to Auto. The unit went through the startup sequence and a loud noise was heard from inside the control panel. The Tech switched the unit into the off position and opened the main disconnect. The Tech then called the Contract Tech to check the MCC Bucket that feeds the unit. The Contract Tech replied back that it was tripped. The Tech then had the Contract Tech lock the bucket out, which the Contract Tech did, and called back when the circuit was locked out. The Tech then opened the control panel and found there had been an arc on the 480 vac 3 phase feeder to the motor starter. The unit was online so the Tech shut it down as a precautionary measure and performed the LOTO on the unit.

Agitators on mud tank were not working.  To keep SBM particles from separating in the process of rolling the mud tank, there was a misalignment in the valve and SBM was discharged to the drilling sump, which was thought to have contained the SBM.

Crane Starboard side was lifting a cuttings box to the stbd transfer deck.  As the load was close to being landed, it bumped the florescent light mounted  on the hand rail approximately 2 foot from the deck.  The damage was to the light lens cover and the bulbs. No other damage to the the fixture or anything else.  The crane was operating within weather limits.  No injuries.  High wind and vessel motion were contributing factors.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition
column24:
Personnel were performing hot work. They were using the fire water pump to keep the production deck wet as a precaution while using a sawzall and grinder to cut U-bolts. A scaffold builder was retrieving parts from the cellar deck when smoke was observed coming from the fire water pump. The scaffold builder immediately notified  an operator of the situation. The operator saw smoke and a small flame, and sounded the fire alarm. The operator then turned off the pump and extinguished the fire using a water hose. The all clear was given and they began looking for the cause. It was determined the belts came off of the pulleys causing the pump to overheat. The pump sustained cosmetic damage only. The belts were replaced, the pump was tested, and was put back into service.

Update - An inspection of the fire water pump was conducted on Wednesday, 10-27-2021, prior to the incident (attached). The fire water pump was running approximately 2-3 hours before the belt came off. It has been determined that the cause was a broken idler pulley jack-bolt. The jack-bolt pushes the idler pulley to keep/maintain tension on the belts. When the jack-bolt broke, tension was released from the idler pulley and belts, which allowed the belts to come off.

Operator was making rounds when hearing a possible leak on Flash Gas Compressor(FGC) C. Upon further investigation, a minor gas leak was determined coming from 2" steel braided flex hose used for fuel inlet of gas fed compressor engine. Fuel gas inlet feed had 44psi as normal operating pressure at time leak was discovered. No gas detection was activated as a result. Reported to CCR. FGC-A was started and C was shut down for repair.

On another day, an electrician was working on SW cellar when detecting smell of gas and confirming with portable detector. Source was identified as a flame arrested vent for Flash Gas Compressor - C packing seals. Mechanic shut down FGC-C upon confirming source was 2nd stage cylinders 3&5 where packing had failed. 2nd stage pressure is 1545psi and it was ~8 minutes from the gas first detected until source was identified and compressor was shut down.
Mechanic shut down FGC-C upon confirming source was 2nd stage cylinders 3&5 where packing had failed.

IP was using a portable band saw to cut a 3" pipe which was sitting on a pipe stand.  The IP was holding the pipe with their left hand and using their right hand to operate the band saw.  As the IP was cutting the pipe the saw bit into the pipe causing it to roll on the pipe stand.  The IP's left hand rolled with the pipe which allowed the tip of their left index finger to come into contact with the band saw blade. This resulted in a cut to left index finger tip. IP was flown in on regular contract helicopter. IP was transported by the company for further medical evaluation. IP received stitches to the left index finger tip. IP was released to return to work.

An IP was pushing on a pipe wrench with their right arm to break apart a pipe union. When the fitting broke free, thrusting the IP's right arm forward, they felt a pop in the right shoulder followed by pain. Management suspected the IP's shoulder may have popped out of the socket. They added that IP has chronic shoulder issues with the right shoulder and that it has come out of socket on multiple occasions. 

As a precaution he was returned to shore and met by his company representative to be brought to a Medical facility for evaluation.

IP stated that as they were walking on scaffolding and one of the metal planks was bent. When the IP stepped on it his ankle rolled left causing ankle pain and was having trouble walking.  The following morningt IP requested to go in to be evaluated.  The IP was evaluated at an Clinic on and was released to full duty.

While attempting to land a 4x33 basket on the east wing deck a light fixture was damaged. While landing the load personnel noticed the basket would not fit in the designated area, so the DSP made sure everyone was clear and began to flag the operator up with the basket. In process of removing basket from area, the aux line became caught between the frame and the light on the upper bridge. Personnel stopped the job to reassess and attempt to free the aux line. Once the aux line was worked free the basket swung and met a light on the 1st deck knocking it overboard. Tag lines were on load and being held. The crane operator was communicating by radio.  The light was noted to not have any secondary retention, boat on location nor any personnel were in the line of fire of the load that was being lifted and light that was knocked loose. DSP immediately notified operator of what occurred.

While offloading a generator from the cargo boat, the generator struck the bullworks on the starboard side of the boat. The contact caused a nipple of a fuel tank of the generator to fail and leak fluid onto the deck of the cargo boat. The generator was set back down on the boat and the leak was repaired. No fluid was discharged into the ocean.

Drill hands were on the rotary and had secured a certified lifting clamp around a lift sub, the connections to secure the clam style clamp were the pelican type lifting hooks, as the vertical lift slowly began the clamp came unfastened and was reattached.  The lift sub pin end was resting inside the DAV sub box end on the threads. As the tugger came up, the driller noticed that the Lift sub had listed over incorrectly and was reaching for the microphone for an all stop, when the lift sub ejected upward about 3-4 feet, and rotated out of the clamp and landed on the deck. There were 3-4 personnel in the immediate area and the lift sub landed in close proximity of the floor hand that had slipped and fallen trying to get out of the way.

An all stop was called and equipment was secured.  No injuries occurred.
IP reported to medic for discomfort in the left elbow that began.  Possibly from using a hammer extensively for several days.
Operator making visit on satellite notice small pinhole leaking gas from gas line on deck. Isolated gas line and bleed down. No sheen was sighted.

While booming up during the pre-use inspection on the crane, the high angle limit did not function.  This allowed the boom to contact the boom stops resulting in damage to the top cord of the heal section and bent some angle lacing.  The crane was placed out of service.  There was not a load on the crane at the time and there were no injuries

A gas/fluid release from a corroded spot on the second stage scrubber dump line for Flash Gas Compressor 1 resulted in a manual facility bleed down and muster.  The process gas/fluid intermittently discharged from the line until the facility was successfully blown down while all non-essential personnel (i.e., those without emergency response duties) were safely mustered in the main living quarters.  The release to GOM waters is estimated to be in low gallons
 
No personnel were injured and the facility will remain shut in until the spool has been replaced and an integrity inspection is performed.

A compensator breakaway sling broke and was caught by the secondary retention sling while laying out a pup joint. The drill crew was attempting to break out and lay down a pup joint from the string. The driller had the block slacked off with the single joints on the floor. As the driller raised the block and the single joint elevators picked up OES grabbed the single joint elevators and latched them to the casing string below the pup joint and below the box of the casing string. The single joint elevators should have been latched above the pin end of the pup joint. As the driller continued picking up they realized the slings got tight way before they should have and driller tried to shut down the block. It was too late to stop the block and tension pulled tight on the compensator break away slings. One side of the breakaway slings broke and the secondary retention sling caught the slings and elevators preventing anything from falling. The pusher stopped the job and the crew discussed what was wrong and why. The slings and swivels were changed out and the job resumed.

The facility Fire Alarm sounded and the ESD activated, shutting-in the facility, as designed. All personnel mustered and reported to their Emergency Stations. The Fire Team responded to the Process Plant Power Generator No. 2 Enclosure because the Fire Suppression System (CO2) had been activated in this enclosure. Once the Fire Team had established and confirmed that there was no fire, the enclosure was purged with fresh air. Facility mechanics inspected the enclosure and observed no evidence of fire or burning. However, facility mechanics did establish the generator engine's crankcase had over-pressured and spilled a small amount of lube oil into the containment area of the generator skid. Facility personnel also established that the Fireye system had initiated the ESD and discharged the CO2. The generator containment skid was thoroughly cleaned of the above referenced lube oil. Once the facility was deemed to be safe, facility personnel began the process to return the facility to service.

While pumping corrosion inhibitor to  a holding tank, IP noticed a small leak on the threaded section of the cam lock fitting.  The IP started to remove the safety pins to be able to tighten the connection.  Once the IP started tightening the cam lock connection, while the pump was still pumping, the connection came apart.  IP was sprayed in the face and body with chemical.  The safety glasses the individual  was wearing were knocked off their face.  IP was sent in for further medical evaluation late that evening.

During crane operations lifting a 550 gal barrel of demulsifier off the fast boat onto the platform,  a sling on the tote tank hung under the access lid on the top of the tote popping it off when signaled to lift the load.  No spillage or injuries.  No apparent damage to the tank and tank never tilted.   Tag lines were being held at the time of the incident.  This was a blind lift.  The crane operator was communicating by radio.

The compression crane boom was staged on the main deck waiting to be installed onto the crane when a tote tank being lifted contacted the compression crane boom handrail. 
No injuries or other equipment damage occurred during this incident.

The facility Fire Alarm sounded and the ESD activated, shutting-in the facility, as designed. All personnel mustered and reported to their Emergency Stations. The Fire Team responded to the Process Plant Power Generator No. 2 Enclosure because the Fire Suppression System (CO2) had been activated in this enclosure. Once the Fire Team had established and confirmed that there was no fire, the enclosure was purged with fresh air. Facility mechanics inspected the enclosure and observed no evidence of fire or burning. However, facility mechanics did find a broken tubing fitting on the generator engine's left side turbocharger, which caused steam to be released into the enclosure. Facility personnel also established that the Fireye system had initiated the ESD and discharged the CO2. Once the facility was deemed to be safe, facility personnel began the process to return the facility to service.

While lowering a tool box from top deck to a lower deck to make room, the tool box hit a 6 inch PCV pipe.  A 10 foot section of the PVC pipe was knocked free and dropped to the lower deck.  A section of the pipe shattered when it hit the deck and grazed a flagger that was in the area.  Contact was made with the flagger's right knee. Flagger was checked out and only has a bruise.  First aid only.  Nothing went overboard.

IP was landing a work basket on the SW hull column using a tagline to manipulate the load. While applying pressure on the tagline, IP heard a "pop" in their right shoulder followed by discomfort and inability to move the right arm.  IP stopped the job and reported to the medic for evaluation.
When bringing a rental 480-volt generator online, smoke began coming out of the generator unit.

A welder was cutting off a padeye on the auger stand with a torch. Slag was being blown towards the section where two tarps are connected. The welder/fitter then began grinding on the area that was just cut when the firewatch noticed the flame on the nearby tarp. The firewatch grabbed a fire extinguisher and extinguished the flame. The firewatch was approximately 5' behind the welder with the fire extinguisher.  The firewatch then got a water hose and sprayed down the entire area.
While on the rig floor, the IP was forcefully pushing down on a ratchet in an attempt to remove a clamp from a geopilot when the individualtheirlt pain and heard a pop in his right shoulder.

While restoring the platform to production, IP was tracing down interconnect piping to identify the source of a small leak (contained in skid, no pollution).  As the IP traced piping on the cellar deck, they slipped on a small containment pan (2'x2') that was in the walkway.  The slip caused the IP to strike their right knee on the grating.  A short time later the IP noticed blood realizing that they suffered a laceration.  At that time, the IP reported the event to the platform PIC.  The IP was then flown to shore by the field helicopter for medical evaluation.  The IP was treated and received sutures and prescription medication for the laceration and subsequently released to full duty.   IP sustained a laceration to the right knee requiring sutures and prescription medication and was given full duty release.

The Aux Hydra-Racker passed a double of 4.5" drill pipe to the Aux Top Drive.  Once the drill pipe was in the Aux Top Drive the Driller attempted to lift the drill pipe.  Instead of being lifted as expected, the drill pipe slid through the elevators to the rig floor with the top of the drill pipe landing across the derrick.  The top of the drill pipe came to rest on the lower belly board. The drill pipe was secured and recovered.   One Floorhand was preparing to work the remote for the Iron Roughneck. Two Floorhands were stabilizing the pipe to set the pipe down on top of rotary. No injures or damage to the environment.

The vessel was performing diving operations.  It is believed that waves washed a removable guardrail overboard on the stern of the vessel. No one actually saw it go overboard. The handrail was not secured to the deck sockets with the safety pins and was lost to the Gulf of Mexico. The handrail weighed approximately 10 lbs, was 90" x 44"; and was made of 1 3/4" aluminum pipe.  Due to the make-up of the rail it most likely did not fall straight to the bottom of the Gulf of Mexico.

An employee #1 walked through the smoke area enroute to the galley when they noticed excessive smoke coming out of a metal cigarette butt disposal container. A second employee retrieved a large cup of water to pour into the container. Employee #1 lifted the lid to allow employee #2 to pour the water in. Upon lifting the lid, a flame flashed due to the introduction of air into the container. The water was applied immediately extinguishing and cooling the smoldering butts. All remaining butt containers have been emptied. 

We will reinforce daily cleaning of the butt containers minimizing the potential for such an event to reoccur.

Personnel were attempting to slide the sump grating to the side so they could access the moon pool. When one end of the grating fell into the opening. The weight of the grating was too much for one person to hold by themselves so the grating was released falling completely into the moon pool.

During our "weekly emergency generator test run", the generator started then over sped and did not shut down on over speed shutdown. In the process of manually trying to shut the generator down the right turbo caught on fire. After the unit was manually shut down diesel/oil was dripping out the exhaust pipe which caused a small sheen. One quart was reported to NRC, but it was probably less. Update: received failure inspection report. Additional platform operations information is being reviewed and additional time will be required to complete the final report.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition
column24: While performing routine rounds, the operator heard gas releasing from around the insulation wrap for riser. The operator pulled the ESD station to shut in the well and PIC isolated the well and pipeline and bled pressure down to zero. Boarding valve and manual valve were blocked off. Pipeline was isolated with zero pressure.

While troubleshooting the UPS inverter located in the UEB, the techs opened the front access panel on the inverter and upon inspection found that the transformer was burnt and that arc flash may have occurred. The facility had been without power  due to circumstances following the Hurricane. It was determined that windings in the transformer failed due to possible moisture accumulation because there was no air conditioning (AC) after the Hurricane Ida power failure.

IP was working on adjusting the shims on the Water maker pump when the IP kneeled with feet on the grating and knees on 2 eight-foot-long scaffold boards, these scaffold boards were in place covering a section of corroded grating as a temporary mitigation. IP proceeded to adjust the shims when a piece of grating approximately 36"x36" fell into the GOM. IP felt the grating that their feet were resting on give and grabbed a piece of pipe connected to the pump to maintain balance while still kneeling on the scaffold boards.

A clothes dryer caught fire at the facility. The fire was immediately extinguished and the dryer was disconnected at removed outside. No injuries occurred. 
No muster was initiated from the event.

A bunk light began sparking and causing smoke.  There was no fire observed.  Engineer turned off the light and called the control room. There was not enough smoke to set off fire and gas system in the quarters. Control room dispatched electrician to investigate and repair. Engineer locked out the circuit and installed a new style light.

At Transformer X inside control panel the temperature display lost power. Power source feeds transformer control panel and cooling fan motors.  
This morning an electrician was troubleshooting why a digital display was offline.  Through the troubleshooting he identified a tripped breaker.  The breaker was found to have overheated resulting in melting of plastic and eventually tripping.  All of the barriers functioned as designed.  The electrical enclosure contained the event and the breaker tripped as designed.

A section of walkway was being lifted from behind the subsea MCC. The swing path for this activity had the crane operator booming out over the facility and then into a tight area for placement. While lowering the walkway into position the facility made a hard "rocking" motion. Consequently the bottom edge of the walkway struck a PAGA speaker knocking it loose from the bracket. There were no dropped objects as a result of the incident and no personnel were injured.

A crane operator was conducting offloading operations with the P/F crane. He lifted a centrifugal pump from the vessel and landed the pump on the platform just inside the crane swing radius line due to limited deck space. After unhooking from the pump the operator swung around to latch onto another load when the crane ladder cage contacted the centrifugal pump on the platform bending the cage. 

Platform supervision, crane operator and riggers have been instructed that no items are to be placed within the crane radius parameter line. A company wide safety alert shall be distributed to remind employees of same.

Crew was in the process of moving a piece of 12'x19' pipe down to the hull column with air tugger. Workers were lowering the pipe while holding back-up with  3/4" rope to prevent the pipe from swinging.  The back-up rope broke causing the pipe to shift and hit the fire water panel breaking some indicator lights on the panel.

While lifting an  generator for the platform crane, the generator was lifted off-center causing it to shift slowly as it became elevated. As the generator shifted, it snagged and pinched a nearby diesel hose to the secondary generator causing damage. The pinched hose resulted in the secondary generator shutting down causing a platform blackout. Power was restored and the diesel hose was repaired; however, approximately a very small amount of diesel was released into the GOM causing a 2'x3' sheen.

Deck personnel doing some deck management utilizing a crane.  While picking up a basket and transitioning load, operator did not see a X communication dome that had been prepped for backload and was at deck level and not connected when the basket came into contact with it.

column22: Pipeline Lay Vessel Pb: Lay Barge
column24:
Equipment damage occurred on the vessel.
While in the process of preparing to deploy ROV into the water, the ROV control panel cover/lid was sitting on the toggle handle in the downward position causing the ROV to lower (instead of raise) onto the stand and landing causing damage to the ROV, the stand(s) and the landing grating.

While attempting to mate two sections of MPD hoses at the rotary table an unexpected vessel motion caused the hose to move out of the lower guide arm which was being used to stabilize the hose. When the hose moved it caused a 6" ring gasket weighing 3.5 pounds to dislodge from the connection and fall through the rotary and into the pool / sea.

X respectfully makes immediate notification of evidence of a fire that occurred on hot water recirculating pump.   A night operator reported to a smoke detector that tripped and initiated a fire alarm.  Upon investigation, the operator noted smoke; however, no fire was observed.  The operator remained at the pump location with a fire extinguisher until the Fire Team arrived on location.  All personnel mustered while the Fire Team dispatched to the hot water heater room.  The team confirmed no visible flame and the electrician secured the 480V power to the hot water heaters.  The OIM and PTL reported to the scene and isolated the water to the return pump and the proper notifications were made.  The all-clear was given.  There were no injuries and the only damage was contained to the recirculate pump.  Initial findings are that water was dripping from the overhead pipe and the water ran down the pipes and got into the recirculate pump causing the failure.  The platform was not shut-in as a result of this event.

While loading drill pipe bundles into racks loaded onto the stern of the vessel, the vessel pitched forward and rolled to port.  This brought the starboard quarter higher into the air, and the drill pipe coming down to the vessel contacted the headache rack and stern anchor light.  This contact resulted in the stern anchor light being sheared off.     Tag lines were attached to the cargo.  Due to heavy seas, tag lines were not in reach.  This was not a blind lift, the vessel was positioned where the asset crane could see the loading area.  The crane operator was using a radio for communication.

During cargo operations on the port side of the rig, Crewboat  stern made brief contact with ROV  Umbilical. Contact with umbilical was witnessed by the Bridge and vessel pulled away after brief contact.
Larger than expected 7' waves in sequence according to witness statement from the boat.

Operations began to delatch the BOP utilizing the Blat tool (BOP Landing Assist Tool) on drill string down the riser.
. While suspended above the wellhead,  riser system and BOP/LMRP suddenly dropped down approx. 18 feet and contacted top of wellhead.  Tensioners were still supporting the majority of the system weight. 
. After striking top of wellhead, BOP/LMRP upper connection to riser separated/ broke, the BOP/LMRP then leaned over, fell approx. 10 feet and landed next to wellhead on seafloor (west side of wellhead/pointed in south direction). BOP/ LMRP laying on its side. No releases seen from BOP/LMRP.
. No infrastructure around wellhead or in vicinity to impacted area. 
. FMC ROV was on bottom monitoring operations and will remain on bottom for continued well and BOP evaluation. 
. No well flow/environmental releases during or after the wellhead impact.
. General muster held. All accounted for. 
.

Crane operator was picking up a supply box from the boat with the 1100 crane, at about 20-30 feet off the boat the craneoperator noticed the fast line stopped coming up. the crane operator let off the winch then tried to pull on it again and at that time they heard a loud noise and the load free fell, subsequently hitting side of the boat (bulwarks) and rolled into the water.

A crane contact incident occurred.
While performing mooring operations in the corner of the facility the East Crane had handed off the line for the mooring chain section connected to the facility to the vessel. The crane hook was pulled onto the back of the vessel for this operation, and once it was complete, the crane hook was released from the back of the vessel. When the crane hook was released, the stored energy from the angle and position of the auxiliary line caused it to swing towards the facility and contact some structural components on the Tween Deck and a caisson running down the column. The resulting contact resulted in some paint scrapes to areas contacted by the crane line and crane ball.
This was the X mooring line operation we have conducted. This operation was different in that the Chain Jack line is obstructed by the flare boom, resulting in the increased angle of the crane line to the vessel. Additionally, the crane was at the farthest the crane boom can reach, and the crane operator was limited in the swing mitigation due to the proximity of the flare boom.
There were no dropped objects as a result of the incident and no personnel were injured.

An employee is being sent in for further medical evaluation due to an injury during swing rope activities.  The IP was performing swing rope activities.  The IP states that when they landed on the back deck of the boat, they slipped twisting the right knee causing the individual  to fall to the deck of the M/V.

The south crane was involved in completing personnel transfer from the supply vessel, for night shift tour change, when one of the pinion gears weighing approximately 300 lbs, fell a distance of 9' 3"to the crane walk around below. The crane operator at that time was able to land the personnel basket safely at the designated landing area.  Prior to the incident the south crane had been taken out of service by a third party company to repair a section of damaged crane cable. The repair was completed and mechanics released the crane back into service at which time the crane operator proceeded to begin personnel transfer. After the incident, the vessel along with crane operators with X and X production investigated the dropped pinion gear and discovered the two bolts holding the pinion in place had backed off resulting in the gear pinion falling to the crane walk around. The remaining gear pinions were all inspected to ensure none of the other gear bolts were backed off. Further investigation also revealed the gear bolts were not secured with any type of locking mechanism to prevent the bolts from backing off.

column14: Main Pass Area, South And East Addition
column24: Production operators were taking on water from the M/V when operators heard a gas release coming from the front side of the compressor cooler. They immediately saw smoke and flames. Production operators sounded the platform alarm, ESDed the facility, and announced where the fire was located. Two operators and a mechanic responded with purple-K fire extinguishers and extinguished the fire. They also utilized fire water to cool down the affected area.  There were no injuries to report and the team did an outstanding job getting the fire extinguished and making sure everyone was accounted for.

A crane incident occurred. While offloading WL spools tightly packet together on the deck of MV, spools became entangled during a lift and damage to the front guards occurred. No injuries occurred. 

Reels were loaded to MV with drip pans facing each other. When offloading of first reel commenced, the drip pan snagged on the telescopic leveler of other reel, when this happened the reel was lowered and deckhands  secured drip pan. Second attempt commenced with same result, however this time operator was not able to lower the equipment in time and that's when equipment was damaged.

The support vessel was assisting with mooring operations for the Production Facility. While recovering the messenger line, the tugger connected to the messenger rope parted at the tugger hook swivel. The messenger rope slid off the deck and into the water. An all stop was called, path forward discussed with the team, and the messenger line was recovered. 
No other equipment damage occurred and no injuries occurred during this incident.

Crews were lifting the Injector Head from the main deck and installing it into another location. At some point while transferring the load from the Crane whip line to the main winch, the whip line contacted the guard around the yoke for the Top Drive. It is dark in that area and damage was not seen until this morning. The guard was found to be bent this morning.

Roustabouts where in the process of moving a drum of thruster oil (412 lbs) from the POOP deck to the sack room. One roustabout was leaning the drum back to get the drum lifter underneath it. At this point the individual lost control of the drum and the drum returned to the upright position rapidly. The other roustabout who was placing the drum lifter underneath the drum did not get their foot out of the way fast enough and the drum struck the roustabouts foot as it returned upright. Employee sustained minor swelling and is being sent to shore for further evaluation.

Drill and Crane Crew were in the process of removing the old drill line spool from the rig floor which was sitting in the rotary in the vertical position. The drill  line spool was lifted in the vertical position by the top drive approximately 3' off the floor.  The starboard forward crane was attached to the bottom of drill line spool to assist in maneuvering the drill line spool from the vertical to horizontal position.  The crane began to pick up while the driller began slacking off on the top drive.  The drill line spool was approximately  from vertical when the Kevlar strap parted, allowing the drill line spool to come to rest on the rig floor.  The drill line spool weighs approximately 42000lbs, and the bottom of the spool was approximately 3 foot from the floor at the time the sling parted.  Closest personnel was approximately 10 foot away from the spool flagging. 
There were no injuries involved with this incident.

After returning to quarters at the end of the day, the Electrician found that the power was off in the room and the breaker feeding into the building was tripped. The wire was traced out and the shorted out wire was found. The wire shorted after the insulation of the wire was damaged due to rubbing against a support bracket over time. There was evidence of an electrical arc in the form of burn marks.

The drill crew was running in the hole to retrieve the split wear bushing from the hanger profile. The crew stood the retrieval stand on the rotary mat in preparation to back wear bushing off of running tool. The crew then installed 2 lift eyes in the wear bushing which was used to turn the wear bushing and jay the bushing off the running tool. 2 employees used the lift eyes as handles to turn the wear bushing and as it came off the running tool it dropped approx 8" to the rubber matt then bounced back up approx 3". IP's hand was caught between the top of the wear bushing and the bottom of the running tool.

IP was in the process of retrieving an empty Super sack. As IP was retrieving sack, IP had to step on a pallet in front of the sack. Upon turning around IP tripped on the pallet banding material, fell forward, contacting the wall with their right shoulder, then falling to the floor. The IP was evaluated by the rig medic, given OTC meds, and released back to duty. After the shift was over, IP reported back to Medic, indicating they still felt stiffness and soreness in the shoulder. The decision was made to medivac the IP for further evaluation and assessment by an onshore physician.  The medivac arrived. IP arrived back at heliport where the individual was be met by IP's company escort.  An MRI indicated a small labrum tear in the right shoulder. The IP is attending physical therapy for treatment of the shoulder.  Waiting for follow-up appointment with orthopedic doctor before IP returns offshore for next hitch.

During oil pipeline pigging operations, IP was closing 10" valve and felt sharp pain in right shoulder.  After pigging operations over, IP noticed pain and burning in right shoulder when lifting and movement of arm.  IP applied ice and anti-inflammatory ointment.  
IP went on days off and will return to work pending full work release from doctor.

Two  personnel were in the process of removing a 4-inch pipe on the deck. IP was standing on the deck holding the rope which was intended to be used to lower the pipe to the deck once it was cut. While the other person was cutting the pipe with a port-a-band, and just as the individual  was about to cut through, the weight of the pipe created a bind on the saw blade. The IP noticed the person trying to remove the saw blade from the bind it was in, so the IP stepped forward and placed one hand on the pipe to relieve the bind. At that moment, the pipe came free and swung towards the IP, striking the individual on the nose creating a 3 cm laceration. IP was wearing proper PPE at the time of the incident- impact gloves, clear-safety glasses, and hard hat. The IP was flown in for further evaluation and received 8 stitches - medical treatment beyond first aid.

Deck crew was involved in picking up 5 7/8" drill pipe on the pipe deck. They were utilizing the Pipe Deck Pipe Handling Crane (PDPH) and transferring the pipe to the pipe skate, on the forward side of the rig floor, so that the drill crew could rack it back in the derrick. While attempting to pick up a joint of 5 7/8" drill pipe from the deck using the PDPH crane the operator noticed that the weight indicator showed the load on the PDPH gripper head was more than a single joint of 5 7/8" drill pipe typically weighs. The crane operator stopped, realizing that the gripper head must have been hung up on another object, causing the weight to be inconsistent with the load being lifted. The operator set the load and gripper head down, repositioned the gripper head to free it from obstruction.  A second lift was attempted, and again the weight was inconsistent with the load being lifted. The gripper head was stuck under the top ledge of a 4' x 40' Bottom Hole Assembly basket, stored on deck next to the 5 7/8" drill pipe. The operator set the load down, released the pipe, and came up on the gripper head with no load.   As the gripper head became free of the basket, the head released. Momentum from the release caused the yoke to swing, striking the swing stop.  The force of impact broke the swing stop.  The broken object fell, contacting the basket stored on the deck below. The broken swing stop is approximately 12" x 4" and weighs 15.4 lbs. It fell approximately 5' to the point of impact. The entire pipe deck was a red zone (exclusion zone).  The nearest person was 40' away.

IP was removing an LED indicator light from the cement head due to low battery indication. Prior to removing the indicator, the IP verbally confirmed twice with the Driller that there was no residual pressure. While removing the indicator there was unexpected residual pressure. The indicator was ejected.

In an attempt to hold the indicator in place, the IP strained the left elbow. The indicator dropped but was held by a retention lanyard.

A Roustabout was assisting in removing the #2 inner bushings while running BHA. While setting down the first of two inner bushings on floor, the bushing tipped over making contact with the top of roustabout's left foot behind the steel toe. Personnel were using rig floor air hoist and two-way bushing pullers to lower the bushing. Bushing weighed approximately 235 pounds.  The Roustabout was examined by the rig medic and the on call physician was consulted.  The IP will be sent in for further evaluation.

X was making a lift of the coil tubing unit cab off of the M/V.  The X shifted and the corner of the CT cab caught the M/V  and caused damage to the CT cab base and slight damage to the M/V.   Tag lines were attached to the cargo and being loosely held due to packed deck.  This was not a blind lift.  The crane operator was communicating by radio.

While making rounds on the operator noticed a leak in the Incoming Gas lift line on the production deck. The platform was shut in and the gas pipeline was isolated. The Incident had no environmental impact due to dry gas.
Elbow injury while wrestling.  Contract employee sent ashore for further medical evaluation.  Confirmed fracture of the elbow/arm.

The crane operator was in the process of removing an unreliable rental generator from the facility and bringing aboard a replacement generator.  The crane operator successfully removed the old generator from the facility and set it next to the replacement generator coming aboard on the back of the boat. Once rigged to the new generator the operator picked up the load slowly and shortly after clearing the deck due to slight vessel movement the load came into contact with a door handle of the old generator and knocked it off.  No injuries occurred.

While backloading a conex onto the M/V, the conex made contact with a spider basket which was stored inside an open top cargo basket. The instruction to stop lowering was given by the signalman on the deck. The delay in crane movement as well as the boat heaving allowed the conex to contact the spider basket and bend the frame on the spider basket. There were no injuries.

Crew was working on the AUX rotary picking up a single joint of drill pipe approximately 29 feet long from the drill pipe skate.  The driller latched the joint in the elevators then raised the same to the vertical position with the link tilt extended outwards, towards the forward end of the rig.  The roughneck (IP) removed the pin thread protector as normal practice, but then moved over to pull the hole cover off the rotary at the same time the driller actuated the link tilt back to center position.  With the link tilt coming back to the center position the drill pipe moves towards the aft slightly striking the IP on the side of the face.
 
Floor hand stated he was fine, but was directed to be checked out by the Medic, and returned to work.
 
Medic examined IP and administer ibuprofen.

Pls find the attached photo of an reenactment of when the drill pipe contacted the Floor hand removing floor cover.  Employee is fine and is at  regular work.

The injured person is a floor hand.

X respectfully submits the investigation report for a gas release that initiated a process shut-in. 
While making rounds, the worker heard a gas leak.  The worker went to the production deck and found a pinhole in the A-3 gas lift line. The worker pulled the ESD to shut in the platform and called for assiatnce. The worker then isolated the leak by closing the casing valve to the A-3 well and the gas lift header valve.

A contractor working at the above well, is being flown in on the regular crew change today, due to a wrist/elbow injury.  
Details of the injury timeline as follows:

A - Employee was helping to unload groceries.  When the employee was picking up a box of frozen turkeys, they felt a pop in the wrist and elbow.  

B - Employee presented to the rig medic with complaint of tingling in the right arm that radiates from the elbow to the wrist, like pins and needles.  A physical assessment was performed and found no abnormalities in pulse, motor or sensory function and the skin was found to be warm and dry.  Physician onshore was contacted for medical direction.  Dr advised possible strain and to treat the employee with ibuprofen and an ice pack.  Employee could return to work as normal.

C - Employee contacted rig medic and complained of "stiffness" in the wrist and concern about possible long term affects.  The onshore Dr offered to the IP to be evaluated onshore and the IP accepted.  The IP was transported onshore via the crew change flight today.

D - Employee was sent to see our company doctor onshore. The IP had an x-ray done and was cleared to return to work.

Vessel experienced a fire inside turbine generator enclosure. Initial alarm came in, flame detectors in X generator enclosure which initiated control room to muster incident command team. Also had an operator in vicinity to look through window and the individual observed sparks but did not enter building. Then Incident Commander arrived on scene. Control room was getting CCTV focused. Observed flames outside of the building which they believe is due to vizqueen (clear plastic tarp from painters in the area) touching the enclosure. Initiated platform ESD. Simultaneously the fire team was in muster area, dressing out. Dispatched fire team to staging area. Validated building was de-energized. Fire team assessed and attacked fire from 2 directions using fire hose reels and fire water pump. Once fire was deemed out, Fire team made visual assessment and did not see sparking or fire or smoke inside building at this time. Fire team used thermal imaging gun to determine door was approximately 75 degrees and then went around to alternate door and came up with same temp. 

Fire team made entry (2 persons) under air and fully bunkered to assess damage and found that the exhaust inspection plate was dislodged from the mounting studs and nuts to the point of only being held in place by 1 stud and nut. Soot was observed on the wall around where the plate had been mounted. Directly below that a cable tray with electrical wire and conduit was observed to have soot and melted grating. Outside of the building- outer exterior wall had soot from fire. Also there is fiberglass grating with cable tray above observed to be hot. 

X's investigation into this incident is ongoing and will be shared once it's available.  Platform was initially shut-in but has since ramped back up.  The generator is not needed for platform production, so it will remain offline, while the investigation continues. 

There were no injuries to personnel, no explosions or harm to the environment as a result of this incident. Known damages include building insulation, electrical wiring/ conduit, interior fiberglass grating.

A west crane boom was suspended over the side of the platform. No one was in the cab as the boom began to rapidly drop making contact with the side of the platform. There were no injuries but a life capsule and handrails were damaged. No production equipment was effected and there is no pollution. The tip of the crane is near water and the headache ball is in the water. The operations at the time of incident were running in the hole with the packer on the well. The BOP is on the well and it is secure. Current rig operations have been suspended and the incident scene is secured

I made an oral notification to the after hours Petroleum Engineer regarding an evacuation of a person from a facility to shore for the purpose of receiving medical treatment beyond first aid.

IP reported to the ship medic with complaints of abdominal pain. The individual took anti-acids and resumed work. The individual returned to the ship's medic with continued abdominal pain. The individual had a fever of approximability 100. This individual had recently been treated for an appendicitis, but their appendix was not removed. Because of their symptoms and recent medical history, the decision was made to evacuate the individual out of concern of a burst appendix.  The patient was taken to X Hospital.

While engaged in the offloading and dumping of methanol, the crane operator swung the tote tank to the facility, the tote tank started to spin a little which made it difficult for the riggers to get a handle on the taglines, which resulted in the tote tank contacting a light fixture located outboard of the facility.

Job was stopped, crane secured and a standdown meeting was conducted prior to job being able to continue. The crew has the parts aboard and are currently replacing the damaged light fixture.

The PTL was making rounds when the individual smelled what seemed like an electrical device failure. The PTL found this to be coming from the vac plug on the PortaCool Unit on the upper deck of the production module. The PTL then turned off the device and disconnected it for the power. The PTL found the plug warm to touch with a gloved hand. Both plugs showed signs of damage. The PTL reported the event to the X and Y onboard.

During a blind lift of empty 4' x 3' cargo box from cellar deck back to top deck, the box contacted a scaffold pole near the NW stairs.  No one was on the scaffold nor nearby the area.  Slight dent to pole.

While hoisting riser joint out of the hold. The bolts on the aft end of the spreader bar separated causing the hook to slide out of the aft end of the joint falling +/- 25' on to additional riser joints in the riser bay leaving the fwd hook still engaged in riser and holding half the riser weight. No personal were injured and no pollution to the sea.

While performing hot bolting operations on a lower deck, the crew heard an unusual noise coming from the HP deck above them. They headed up to the HP deck to investigate and found a 1" gas makeup line on the H.P. Separator releasing gas through a pin hole.  A facility operator was notified and the HP system was shut in, isolated and bled down to contain the release.  Approximate volume of release of gas was estimated at .005 MCF.  The system will remain shut in pending repairs.

During the function testing of a linear winch used for SCR pull-in operations, it was noticed that an encoder needed to be changed out. Upon completion of the function testing the kit was deenergized and deemed safe for personnel to work on replacing the encoder. Upon completion of encoder replacement, the kit was re-energized and X began to calibrate the new encoder.  'A' block was in holding and stationary position and the 'B' block was traveling rearward toward the spool as part of calibration.  The 'B' block invertedly pulled the cable rearward causing the spelter socket at the end of the wire to contact the flagging sheave. This resulted in 1 of 2 guide rollers at the bottom of the flagging sheave to become dislodged from its holder and drop to sea.  During the drop the guide roller struck a cable tray on the side of the platform. Guide roller assembly weighs 524kg (1,156 lbs).  The guide roller was located on the sea floor but was recovered. When the roller dislodged it resulted in a vibration on the platform.

The M/V X was performing fuel transfer operations. The operations were stopped because weather conditions were deteriorating (spike in loop current). The Vessel Disconnected Fuel hose and secured it to the crane hook. As hose was being lifted by the crane, hose got hung up on a tote. IP recognized the hose tightening and was catching onto an NPT tote tank. IP reached up with their hand to keep the hose from catching and possibly damaging equipment. Simultaneously, the Crane Operator slacked off the lift. While doing this apparently the vessel fell into a trough resulting in the crane wire tightening and trapping IP's hand between lifting apparatus and the tote tank. IP evacuated by helicopter to X Hospital with a hand surgeon on standby. IP experienced an injury of partial degloving of left pinky and crushed injury to left ring finger.

While back loading equipment on the vessel, the lift shifted hitting the Bell Vent on the #3 Diesel Tank on the Port Side, breaking the bell vent. No one was injured or any fluids went into the water.   Weather: light SW wind, seas 1-3 ft, current .6 knots.

Shut down due to a Pressure Safety Low. During restart attempt , received gas confirmed alarm, and the facility "Gas Detected" alarm was initiated. All personnel mustered and were accounted for. 

During the initial investigation, Operation Technicians identified a broken 3/8" PSV supply (pilot) line. Further investigation revealed that the bolts that would have mounted the pilot to the PSV bracket and prevented vibration were missing. These missing bolts allowed for abnormal vibration on the tubing, ultimately leading to the tubing failure.

Contractor Supervisor: NA

Date of incident is the day the first confirm

Initial notification made  again  once the individual has departed the facility. Roustabout was struck in the mouth by a sling as they dis-connected the sling.  The incident caused damage/broke approx. three of the individual's teeth.  The individual was medevac'd off the rig at the first opportunity.

While offloading a bundle of tubing from the boat, the tubing caught the rigging of a 4 x 8 trash bin containing a port-a-potty. The crane operator stopped lifting the load when he noticed the rigging was caught on the load. The boat then dropped down due to the swells and the trash bin was pulled backwards and tipped on its back.

Contract Operator was assisting in relocating a large pulley on the upper deck. As the crane lowered the pulley to the deck, Operator and rigger unhooked crane's stinger from pulley and attempted to move pulley when it landed on the Operators left foot. Operator was sent in and taken to medical clinic wherethe individual  was diagnosed with a fractured big toe and two dislocated toes. Surgery will be required to correct his big toe. 
 Operator is expected to be out another X weeks prior to being released back to full duty.

Full muster was called due to errant vessel coming within 10nm of facility. Contact with vessel was attempted about 55min from contact with no acknowledgement or change. Within 30min of contact the muster alarm was called. Vessel shifted course. Full muster was achieved. No incidents or injuries occurred during the muster event.

Personnel were preparing to transfer a cargo basket containing an Automated Weather Observing System (AWOS) from the MV.  When attempting to lift the basket off the MV, one of the legs of the four-part slings on the basket got caught under one of the supports for the AWOS skid inside of the basket, bending a section of grating on the AWOS skid.   The basket had not been fully lifted yet and the crane immediately slacked off so the sling could be corrected.  No personnel were injured.

A facility had a gas release event that required muster. A gas detector went into high alarm. It displayed elevated gas readings as well but did not go into alarm. Platform automated "Gas Alarm" announced. Operations personnel shutdown the vessel from the control room, and the Incident Command Structure alarm was sounded. The fire team began suiting up, then the ICS muster completed.

Both fire teams headed up side of facility to the top deck. The teams investigated the area that the gas detectors cover. Once the area was deemed safe to enter, maintenance personnel were allowed in. A mechanic found blown out thermal well discharge line. Thermal well was replaced.

During the event one member of the fire team overheated and went to see the medic. The individual was fine once he removed his equipment.

While tripping in the hole a stand of 3.5" drill pipe was handed off to the block then the pipe rackers went after the next stand. As the Driller picked up off the slips and started to come down, the rackers brought the next stand out to center to be ready to run the next stand. This stand came from the first row closest to the block/rotary. As the upper racker operator brought the stand out, the momentum caused the upper end of stand to get under the block. This was due to the upper racker creating energy toward the rotary by extending the arm out too far and when it came out of the row that energy caused the top of stand to get under block. Once this happened it caused the stand to bow coming out of the lower racker head and glancing off of the air slip base coming to rest on the rotary, still being held by the upper racker. The lower racker then reached back and grabbed the stand and racked it back.  The job by design was in place and red zone established with no one in the area.

While engaging a joint of riser, the riser crane's spreader bar flange bolts broke/sheared off as the hook was engaging. Four bolts and their washers fell approx. 14' 9" and the drops calculator has the impact classified as a First Aid event.

As the gantry hook engaged the riser joint laterally the lower flange bolts on the forward end of the spreader beam broke free.

An all-stop was called and the driller alerted the night company representative. X's personnel began assessing the flange and evaluated what repairs should be made while riser handling is suspended.

No injuries occurred.

Operations was in the process of offloading equipment from a supply vessel. When making a lift, the crane fast line parted and the load was dropped into the water. No injuries or equipment damage reported other than the crane cable and lost equipment.

This incident occurred while the rig was running casing. IP was walking across top pipe rack and stepped onto grating covering motor shed vent. IP stated that when they stepped on the grating, it dislodged, and that their foot went a few inches into the vent causing the IP to loose  balance. This caused the IP to fall over and land on the left knee and left elbow. The IP was brought to the onboard medic and complained of minor pain in the knee. Onboard medic performed evaluation and called shore base doctor. Doctor's diagnosis was a bruised left knee, the IP was given Ibuprofen and the knee was wrapped with ace bandage. Medic told the IP to apply ice to the knee and relax the knee for the remainder of the shift. The medic requested that the IP come back for a follow-up visit before starting the next shift. This morning the IP went to see the medic again and complained of minor back pain. IP asked to be sent in to go see a Doctor. IP is being flown to X heliport on a regularly scheduled flight. The IP will be met at the heliport by a X adjuster and brought to the Doctor for evaluation.

After making up the wear bushing pulling tool, the ST80 operator was moving the equipment away from the rotary table. While positioning the ST80, the hydraulic ram failed, causing the equipment to move forward about 2 1/2 feet, striking an IP on the IP's right side. IP was taken to shore for further medical evaluation. IP was given a full release on 12/23.

Near Miss:  While laying out a single joint of 7 5/8" Riser, the 7 5/8" Elevators opened prematurely. The single joint was captured between the Catwalk Shuttle and the Catwalk Tail-In Arm to prevent joint from falling to the deck. The joint was secured with a tugger, lowered to the rig floor and elevators were inspected with no failures noted. No personnel were injured or property was damaged.

Weather - Winds 13 mph; Seas 4 feet; Air Temp 76 degrees; Visibility 5nm; Conditions clear; Current 1 kt

Generator #1 stopped producing power. That then triggered the fire panel in the building. All non-essential personnel mustered to their assigned area due to the fire alarm sounding. 
While essential personnel were looking into the reason the generator stopped producing power, they observed a glow coming through the air inlet filter on the generator housing. The engine was shut down, incoming start gas and fuel gas was isolated. The filter was removed and the generator head was sprayed with an extinguisher. Once the flame was extinguished, the fan was setup to cool the generator head and personnel remain on the scene until the unit was cooled.
There were no inquires to any personnel and no damage other than that to the generator.

While ascending in a work basket to conduct pressure washing, the work basket contacted the round bar protection cage of the upper winch and camera of the main hydraracker. The contact resulted damage to the upper frame of the work basket. No damage to the Hydraracker. Red Zone barriers were in place. No personnel injured.

While engaged in recovery efforts, the BOP was being supported by the auxiliary block and 250k of the BOP weight sitting in the mudline. The main block was stabbed in with the spear assembly attempting the BOP recovery with 1million (1022k) hook load (BOP weight ~ 950K), when the spear failed unexpectedly. An all stop was initiated and a traveling equipment inspection was performed. The pipe was removed from the BOP and the spear was found to be the failure point.   Inspections are currently in progress and any findings will be reported as they are found. 

There were no dropped objects, no injuries to personnel, and no environmental impact as a result of the incident.

While working with an tool string and when tool string was inside of lubricator we hit the rope socket and break wire and BHA dropped (cable was pushed out). Activated ESD 1. Well is secure with Lower Ram and after that we closed the upper ram. 

Notification email and phone call sent.

IP pulled pin out of csg. Csg shifted causing employee's right index finger to get caught between pin bar and kick plate in work basket. Laceration on right index finger, IP sent for further medical evaluation, it was determined IP required stitches. 

The IP was taken to X, received 10 
stitches and released to full duties with no restrictions.

During the lift of the Test Stump, The EDP moved forward and one of the bottom fins/gussets of the X impacted the 5" production bore gasket prep on the Test Stump Package. The impact damaged the gasket prep at the entry point.
No injuries occurred during the incident.

X submits the initial notification of a "fire" that was discovered.  Verbal and written notification were made immediately.

Upon weekly visit it was noted that the navigation horn was not operating.  Upon investigation, the battery box was opened and the charger had evidence of charring due to electrical fault.  
Incident Notification process followed.  Electrician will be sent to replace components.

While troubleshooting X evidence of charring/melting of a card in control panel was found. Operations stopped the job, replaced the card, and brought pump back online without issue.
No other accidents or injuries occurred during this event.

Platform operator noticed gas leaking from an insulated gas inlet line to the flash gas compressors.  Platform was manually shut in and line bled down.  Once the piping insulation was removed,  a pinhole from external corrosion was found.  Estimate gas volume released at 0.13 mcf.  Platform will remain shut in pending repairs.   No injuries. No other damages.

Operator smelled a burning rubber smell but saw no smoke. The fire alarm was initiated and all personnel mustered to their assigned emergency stations. Operators found the smell most concentrated at the pipeline pump and immediately turned it off. The smell ceased after a short time. There was never any smoke or fire at pump. It was determined that the brake malfunctioned and engaged locking up the pump allowing the electric motor to continue to spin on the belt.   Maintenance team is in process of trouble shooting the unit to determine the cause.  No fire, no injuries, and no equipment damage.

Operator was investigating a pressure safety low shutdown on the water injection pump #1 and found the base of the pump motor emitting black smoke. The operator discharged a fire extinguisher which ceased the smoke. Suction and discharge valves for injection pump #1 isolated and the electrician locked out the breaker.

Crane # 2 / fore-port, was P/U a bundle of pipe, per procedure operator slowly picked up the bundle about 2ft high from deck, at which point the synthetic strap failed/broke. No injuries reported.

Plastic pipe stacking tray was broken on impact.

While back-loading an tank from platform deck to the vessel deck of the MV a 5' pin lock scaffold pole (12.5 pounds) fell from the tank as it was being lowered to the vessel deck. It is unknown exactly where the scaffold pole was position on the vessel prior to the event. Deckhand on the vessel deck stated that the pole fell from a distance of approximately 10-15 feet and landed on the deck of the boat.

The MV was attempting to start a bulk fluid transfer to the rig.  As they came into the 500-meter zone, the rig made a 5-degree heading change to accommodate the current.  The crane operator on the rig requested the MV to move forward to assist with the crane operations.  The crane operator advised the M/V they were going to make contact. The Sr. Dynamic Positioning Operator (SDPO) on the deck attempted to adjust the heading to avoid collision; however, the MV came into contact with the rig.  

Damage teams were dispersed to assess damage.   No bilge alarms or flooding was observed on the rig.  The MV moved outside of the 500-meter zone to assess vessel damage.  At this time, damage is believed to be minimal - - limited to a 2-inch handrail on the MV. No personnel were injured.

While loading compressor tube on cooler it busted and gas escaped. The compressor was shut down and bled down and LOTO was administered at that time.
Plugs were installed in cooler on 12-23-21 at 8:45 am and unit was place back in service.

On January 6th at approximately 7:00am a contract Coiled tubing crew from Alliance Energy Services was in the process of rigging down coil equipment. Part of the process required the hook up of a Nitrogen bottle rack to blow compressed nitrogen into the coil tubing to flush fluids from within. The injured contractor opened 1 of the nitrogen bottle valves to begin the process when the brass nipple connecting the hose to the bottle rack broke at the hose fitting. The hose, now under pressure started whipping and struck two separate Alliance ES employees. One person was struck on the right hand with what appears to be a minor laceration and bruising, the other on the right forearm with abrasions and bruising.  As a precaution both contractors were sent to shore for medical evaluation and was accompanied by an Alliance ES representative to a Medical facility. 

On January 7th Alliance ES Representative contacted QNE with Medical Evaluation update on the condition of IPs. One IP  sustained fractures to his right index and forefinger, the other IP had an abrasion to his right forearm only.  QNE in conjunction with Alliance ES is investigating the incident to determine the cause of the fitting failure. 

___________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

UPDATE 1-26-22: Alliance ES reports that an IP had surgery the date of incident. That IP has been assigned to light duty and is currently working in AES shop on a regular work schedule. EWELL Injury status changed from LTA>3 to RW/JT >3. 
Incident Investigation: On 1-6-22 a nitrogen bottle rack, hoses and fittings were supplied to QNE as a rental component from Gulf Pro Services. Of the failure components: The nitrogen hose used is a pin pricked hydraulic hose suitable for use in nitrogen service. It has a nominal dimension of 1" and a crimped end fitting with a 1" NPT thread adapted to a brass quarter inch NPT x CGA-580 fitting. The CGA-580 is the industry standard for nitrogen bottle rack valves. The hose and fitting are rated for 3,000 psi which exceeds the maximum pressure of a compressed nitrogen bottle at 2,400 psi. 

The hose end connection at the brass fitting was previously identified (pre-event) by Gulf Pro Services as a potential area of failure. A such, Gulf Pro Services identified engineering controls to mitigate the risk. The nitrogen hoses / bottle racks, of the same configuration involved in this incident, were fitted with hose containment grips (tie-backs) and shackles on all bottle rack skids and supported by an internal QC check sheet to verify compliance of same prior to delivery to customers. The incident investigation revealed that 2 of the 4 hoses shipped by Gulf Pro Services did not have containment grips installed as required by their previous internal risk assessment. The failure was determined to be directly related to the weight of the unsupported nitrogen hose on the soft brass hose adapter causing the adapter to fail at the threaded connection, thus releasing the energy stored in the compressed gas cylinder. As a result the hose was unrestrained and released energy in an uncontrolled way thereby striking the injured worker on the hand. The failure of the Alliance ES employee to wear the QNE recommended impact gloves (PPE) was a factor in the severity of the injury. 

At the root of the event was a failure to verify engineering controls (containment grips - whip checks) were in place prior to delivery is said equipment...."Risk Assessment & Management", and a failure of site personnel (Alliance Coiled Tubing employees) to identify the hazard and/or missing tie-backs 2 of 4. Additionally, had the previously identified engineering controls been installed prior to shipping, which would have supported the weight of the hose to the brass fitting, the failure of the fitting would not have occurred. As mentioned, the injured person was not wearing the QNE recommended impact gloves at the time of the incident. The PPE barrier of impact gloves would have more likely than not reduced and/or eliminated the severity of the sustained injury.

The building was elevated to serve both as a distance barrier and to grant enough space for workers to safely perform torch cutting and removal of grating material. The elevation level was increased approximately 8-10" inches in height above the building's normal stationary position.  _x000D_
The hot-work activity was supported by a pre-task safety meeting, a job-safety-analysis (JSA), and a hot-work permit (HWP). There was also a construction supervisor assigned to the activity and a construction inspector that periodically engaged and observed the work throughout the shift. During the hot-work activity salt water from a pressurized hose was applied to saturate the subfloor and rafters under the building. Hot-work halted for a lunch period at 1130HRS and resumed at 1200HRS and then concluded for the day at 1700HRS. The assigned Firewatch remained on duty for thirty minutes afterwards during an area cool down period to saturate the area and for observance and to respond in the event of an ignition. All crew members had departed the work area by 1730HRS. At approximately 1745HRS the construction inspector noticed a small fire located at the rear lower southwest side of the building. At this time, he was already heading in that direction to inspect areas of work affiliated with the activities of the day. Upon recognizing the fire, he reacted quickly and extinguished the flames with saltwater from a hose. Internal reporting and investigative proceedings of the incident began immediately after the scene was safe and secure.   The building was impacted with minor damages from the flame and heat of the fire.
