One gallon of waste oil was released to secondary containment.

While performing welding work on the Microturbine exhaust system, a spark fell on the air inlet foam insulation and caught fire.  The air inlet opening below the welding area was not covered with a fire blanket. The small fire was quickly extinguished with a utility water hose.

An emergency shutdown occurred. An Operator went to the WC 72 #3 caisson and noted a fire near the panel on the fuel gas regulator. The operator extinquished the flame with a 30# dry chemical extinguisher. _x000D_
The SO cord near the heater became overheated and caught alight causing the Big Joe regulator to catch fire at the gas port. This in turn activated the TSE and led to the ESD initiation. _x000D_
_x000D_There were no injuries or pollution involved with this event, and all safety systems functioned as intended. Estimated cost of repairs is approximately $1500.00.
After cleaning reserve pit #6, the Tri-State pit cleaner leaned over his pump to undo a discharge line, lost his footing, and fell at grade. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation.

A galley hand was caramelizing some sugar on the stove and he turned away to assist an employee at the serving line.  While he was turned away, the sugar boiled over onto the stove, creating enough smoke and steam to activate two smoke detectors in the galley.  The ship completed a full muster.  Note: there were no injuries, pollution or damage to equipment resulting from this incident.

Prior to going home on crew change day, the injured employee was walking out of the pumpers shack. He stepped down to the deck from the second step and injured himself.
_x000D_IP was sent in for further evaluation.

An alarm sounded indicating a fire in portable accomodations building #2. Personnel mustered, and fire team responded. There was no fire found, but team could smell what appeared to be wiring insulation. After building was secured, and all clear was given, electricians investigated, and found blower motor on air conditioner unit was frozen up.

The Gloria A was experiencing difficulty maintaining DP position due to the thruster current coming from the rig while the rig was attempting to backload equipment. The Gloria A captain and the crane operator discussed the thruster current and positioning of the equipment on the deck of the boat and decided to continued with the backloading operation. The crane operator picked up a 4'x12' tool basket to lower to the crew boat. During the process, the crew boat drifted toward the load being lowered and one of the pad eyes came in contact with a Schlumberger wire line satellite dome causing surface damage to the dome (repair cost $3000).  _x000D_

Employees were attempting to pick up a riser slick joint from the riser storage bay in order to test the re-fabricated saddles for proper orientation.  The riser joint was at the bottom of the hull. Employee lowered the crane and hooked onto the slick joint. With the joint of riser lifted approximately 2' above the deck the port aft winch cable parted causing the aft end of the slick joint to fall 2' leaving the forward end suspended 2' high. No personnel were in the immediate area and no one was injured.

While removing racking mats from the setback area, the load was caught broadside by the wind pushing it outboard. The lift was landed safely on the pipe deck where the deck crew utilized the tag line and push pull sticks. _x000D_After landing the load, the roustabout (spotter) reported the contact to the crane operator. On closer inspection it was observed that the backscratcher had been damaged and is suspected to have happened when the load swung into the backscratcher._x000D_ Repair to the Backscratcher is less than $1000. The matting (equipment being lifted) was not damaged._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
_x000D_

Crew observed smoke and a small flame coming from the oven control panel on the galley's stove.  An extinguisher was used to extinguish flame and all electrical power to the stove was disconnected. Preliminary investigation indicates a short in the wiring for the oven controls. The only damage was to galley stove and the duration from visual to flame being extinguished was less than 5 min.  Estimated galley stove damage is $7500_x000D_

The crane operator was cradling the starboard aft crane boom into the boom rest after pulling a barite hose off of boat when he felt the boom strike the boom rest. The job was stopped and one of the Teflon boom rest pads was found lying on the deck. The pad weighs 18 lbs and fell an estimated 42 feet. An announcement was made prior to cradling the boom as per procedure. No personnel were in the area at the time of the incident and no one was injured.

During normal production operations, personnel noticed smoke coming from the exhaust stack on the Heater Treater (NBK-1800). After shutting off the fuel gas to the burner, the operator noticed a small fire inside the fire tube and left to retrieve a handheld fire extinguisher. When he returned, the fire was already out. The treater was drained of all fluids, and the fire tube was removed and sent to a fabrication and repair yard in Scott, Louisiana. BSEE inspectors were there on December 29, 2016, to witness the sandblasting and cleaning of the fire tube, as well as to assess the damage.

The IP was squatting to pick up a case of water bottles whenhe slipped. IP returned to shore for evaluation._x000D_
_x000D_

Ms Jolie on DP. Weather conditions caused the Ms Jolie to move while setting basket on deck and it came into contact with gangway damaging handrail._x000D_
_x000D_No personnel were injured with this incident and the estimated repair cost is less than $700. _x000D_
_x000D_
Worker was assisting another worker with unloading and putting away supplies when one of the workers experienced discomfort.
The IP was assisting in unloading groceries from a grocery cargo container; after unloading boxes and then returning empty boxes to the cargo container IP was injured.
While stepping up to perform maintenance on one of the shakers, he was injured.

A fire lasting approximately 5 minutes occurred.  The fire was contained to the skid for Therminol pump number 2 and was fully extinguished.  A full muster was performed, there were no injuries to personnel.

The hinges for the door on the grocery box failed while box was suspended by a crane adjacent to the handrail, this resulted in the door falling in the GOM. It appears that the top hinge on the door was damaged but was not noticed. As the door was shut, the top hinge failed and the bottom hinge alone could not support the door. The bottom hing then failed and the door fell off.

A failed vessel apparatus (sight glass) discharging product saturated an exhaust system which caused an ignition. Subsequent attempts to extinguish fire were un-successful at which time UWA elected to abandon facility and commence emergency response efforts. _x000D_A Fast Response Vessel (FRV) was mobilized and there were no recoverable hydrocarbons. An estimate of 3.75 total bbls and 2.25 bbls after evaporation from the facility run-off was caused by the water being introduced during firefighting efforts. _x000D_There were no injuries. _x000D_
_x000D_
Components involved: NBK 1700 (oil treater) and PAX 4100 (pipeline pump #1)_x000D_
_x000D_
Necessary Repairs: Quality assurance and mechanical integrity/repairs on electrical apparatus, and equipment from seawater deluge during firefighting efforts and replacement in kind of NBK 1700 due to damages. Preliminary cost: 2.7 million._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
_x000D_
A cleaning tech of the Hull Entry Crew fell approximately 5-6' in the hull and was injured. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

Well shut-in on flowline PSL.  Upon inspection,  a hole in flowline segment downstream of chokes on topsides causing release of gas and shut-in of well was discovered.  The flowline removed and replaced.

While rigging up from the cellar deck to the deck above, (riser pipe) slacked off on crane too much causing the 15'pipe to skid across the deck. The Rigger had the tag line, but the weight of the pipe was too much, causing the rigger to let go of the tag line to get out of the way. The bottom of the pipe hit the handrail causing it (the handrail) to go into the water. No injuries resulted from this incident.  _x000D_
_x000D_The estimated cost to replace the damaged equipment is about $2500.00._x000D_  The load and/or materials being used was the Chiksan pipe, which damaged the  handrail.

The Subsea team was in the process of reassembling a failsafe valve off the BOP on the portside setback area. The failsafe valves were removed for inspection. The (IP) Injured Person and (SST) Subsea Trainee were using the (BOP) Blowout preventer gantry crane to pick up the actuator during this task. _x000D_The two grease plates became loose from inside the valve body, so the decision was made by the Subsea Engineer to reassess the task and re-rig the assembly. _x000D_They were having trouble assembling the valve using the gantry crane so they decided to reassemble it piece by piece without the use of the gantry crane. _x000D_
While installing the gate and stem by hand the weight of the gate was approximately 33 pounds. As the IP and SST were trying to reassemble it from within the valve body the grease plate slid into the IP's body. _x000D_

An Operator was pumping potable water to the platform and when he finished, he disconnected hose and started picking it up with crane. The hose hung up on the tire pads on boat and snapped hose. There were no injuries or damage.

While the mechanics were working on the #1 generator, the right bank was having power issues. The generator was beginning to warm up the engine.  Once at rated speed, the turbo temperature was brought up approximately 1000 degrees F (normal operating temp). The right bank turbo insulation began to smoke, at which point one of the mechanics immediately proceeded to SD the engine from the production MCC. A small flame (approx. 3"x3") appeared.  The other mechanic grabbed a fire extinguisher nearby and put the small flame out after 2-3 attempts w/the fire extinguisher._x000D_
The cost to repair was approximately $5000.

The operators were using a chain hoist to hold up a choke bonnet while trying to remove it so they could repair the choke.  As there was no tie-off point directly above the choke, they used the crane as a tie-off point for the chain hoist. Because of scale build-up, they had trouble removing the bonnet so they decided to use the crane winch to rock the bonnet so that it would free up for removal. The IP placed his left hand on the strap that was attached to the bonnet in an attempt to shake and rock the bonnet as it had started to move a small amount.  At that moment, the chain hoist hook slipped and the chain hoist came down, striking the IP, causing an injury.  The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

While offloading 2 joints of 2" x 20' galvanized pipe, the deck hand of the vessel attached the (2) nylon slings to the hook of the stinger.  The slings were in a choker position. The crane operator then signaled to pick up the pipe and swing out over the water.  Once the load was over the water the pipe shifted which put the load out of balance and it fell into the water. The 2 joints were not retrievable._x000D_

While opening the main deck hatch into Engine Room #1 using the installed winch, the winch handle came loose from the IP's right hand.  The handle free-spun and hit the IP. The employee was flown in for further evaluation.

The 2-man production crew and the M/V Emily G work boat finished a solvent soak job on the departing pipeline.  Weather was deteriorating & the job was finished. Upon attempting to position the boat for the 2nd operator to swing-rope to the boat, a swell pushed the boat under and into the 180 degree wrap-around boat landing causing the boat to crack the weld attaching the boat landing to the caisson. No muster was required, no injuries and no pollution._x000D_ The damage was +/- $100,000._x000D_
_x000D_

While M/ V Odyssey Champion was backing up to the platform to drop off personnel, a swell pushed the boat into the platform's landing causing damage.  No damage to the boat and no injuries were reported.
While using a 36 inch pipe wrench to remove a meter, an employee was injured.

The starboard side Chevron G&G Conex was struck by a lifted crane load damaging the exterior junction box that controls power to the unit of the box. The lifted load, a 6' x 8' chemical container box, was being backloaded by crane #1 from the starboard side sack room porch staging area to a supply vessel. A 3" aluminum handle, weighs 5 oz., that switches the power to the On / Off position was the primary part damaged in this incident.

A small fire was discovered in the designated smoking area of MC-280 (Lena) platform. A temporary wind wall was made with a tarp in the area.  The operator smelled something burning and followed the smell to the smoking area where he saw an area at the bottom of the tarp burning approximately 3" wide and 10" high.  The fire was immediately extinguished with a nearby 20 lb ABC dry chemical hand held fire extinguisher.  There were no injuries to personnel or damage to the facility.  No muster was required.

While Offloading a cutting box from the supply vessel to the rig, the box twisted during lift as it came up and the corner of the box caught under the middle pipe of the headache rack bending and breaking welds holding the pipe._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

An employee stepped up onto a spreader bar that was leaning up against one of the cutting boxes to check inside the box. The spreader bar had been utilized to place the facilities survival craft onto the deck of the platform for repair/maintenance in early December 2016. As he stepped off of the spreader bar and began walking away, he heard the injured employee yell and ask the PIC to remove the spreader bar. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation.

An employee was addressing a deficiency in a barricade. The only way inside the sub structure is to climb under or climb over an area that is about waist high. While climbing under the structure the IP was injured. The IP was taken to shore for further evaluation.

The facility was shut-in due to Regulatory testing requirements when the platform
experienced an Emergency Safety System loss of power resulting in loss of power
generation, ESD activation, blowdown, full deluge of all zones and sounding of the
abandon platform alarm. There was a full muster and fire squads were sent out to
investigate. The emergency generator did not start and Uninterruptible Power Supply
(UPS) bank 4 did not energize to supply backup power, resulting in impacts to the
communication system and control system visualization.

While lifting the personnel basket from the deck of the boat, the personnel basket was swung into the side of the boat (On deck. Not on outside of boat) Three personnel were injured. They were evacuated and taken to a medical facility for evaluation. The estimated cost to repair the crane is $12,314.0.

The OSV Breeze was on location at the Pacific Sharav, in working position under the starboard aft crane. The deck crew had the RadScan unit (15.6 lbs.) ready to send up to the rig. They notified the crane operator that they were ready to send the unit up and the operator lowered the hook. The deck crew then placed the RadScan unit on the hook using the nylon sling and the wire rope sling. Also on the hook was a mail bag used to send up paperwork. The deck crew signaled the crane operator to hoist up and them cleared the area (approximately 45 feet away). The crane lifted the RadScan unit up and when it got to a height of roughly 15-20 feet, the crane operator stop crane movement in order to respond to the boat captain radio call and then the RadScan unit came off the hook, falling to the deck._x000D_
_x000D_
The IP was removing the cable clamps from the MUX line when he was caught between the IRS (Independent Riser System) and the handrail. Injured was flown in for evaluation.

A crane crew unloading 14" casing doubles from a work boat had 2 sets of doubles attached to crane. The crew hoisted casing up and swung it over the rig and had to hold in position while waiting on casing to turn so it could be slacked off into casing bay. At that point the sling slipped on one of the doubles causing the casing to slip down 11' coming to rest on the hand rails at the riser crane level.  No one was in the area.

The construction floor drill crew was in the process of laying down riser.  A worker hoisted up on the port air hoist to raise the RT-40 wrench over the handrail of the spider/gimble after it was used by coworkers on the gimbal.  Upon raising the wrench, worker stopped the air hoist and noticed that the air hoist still continued to hoist line upwards.  Worker attempted again to stop the hoist with the control lever and then pressed E-Stop.  Neither of the actions performed stopped the air hoist from hoisting up on the line.  The rig floor was cleared as the hoist line with the RT-40 wrench still attached was traveling upwards.  At approximately 45 feet from the deck, the spring balancer line attached to the RT-40 wrench parted, due to tension against hydraulic control lines causing the wrench to fall to the deck of the construction floor.  The hoist wire with the spring balancer continued hoisting upward to the crown sheave, the control air was shutdown to stop the hoist winch. The RT-40 Wrench weighed 240-lbs. No/Go zones were in place and all personnel were out of the area._x000D_

2 joints of 4" pipe were being lowered to the deck of the boat. One end of the joints of pipe were sitting on the deck of the boat and the other end was still off the deck. The deck hand stated he had signaled to the crane operator to lower the load the rest of the way but, while he was holding the tag line he was attempting to swing the end of the pipe that was still off the deck into position. As he was doing this the crane operator came down with the load the rest of the way and it struck the deck hand. The IP was flown in for further evaluation._x000D_

Personnel was in the process of installing a section of grating on top of 400 bbl tanks following their installation. The grating covers a small gap_x000D_
between the tanks. The grating is 15 1/2'' wide x 76'' long weighing approximately 42 pounds. A cement line which runs across the top of the_x000D_
tanks made installation of the grating more difficult. With personnel on each end of the grating, they were having to manipulate the grating at_x000D_
different angles to work around the cement line and a handrail. The IPwas caught between the grating and the lip on which it_x000D_
sits after_x000D_ the grating suddenly slipped into place. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.
The IP was ascending stairs performing deck rounds and felt sharp pain. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.

While attempting to dislodge and lift the swing gear from the crane with an air tugger, the nylon strap holding snatch block parted. There were no injuries or pollution associated with this incident. The only damage was to the nylon strap.

A DPO on watch noticed a small fire coming from fluorescent light unit on the intermediate landing going up to the Port Crane.  The fire was immediately extinguished using a local handheld unit.  All power to topside lights on deck was secured.  Operator stood by on fire watch for 30 minutes after fire was extinguished.  There was no damage (except for the light fixture) and no injuries.  Investigation is ongoing._x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
While loading scrap iron basket, a piece of metal slipped and injured the IP.  The IP was sent to shore for treatment.
During decommissioning dive operations a diver was injured.
Employees were sliding 3.5 inch manual elevators across the rig floor.  While moving the elevators, one of the employees felt some pain.  The IP was sent to shore for evaluation.

While welding to replace a corroded pipe on the vent system identified within Renaissance's ALM system, the nitrogen differential dislodged the secondary plumbers plug and residual product flashed from the end of pipe . The fire was extinguished (< 5 minutes) with a 30 lb purple "K" semi-portable._x000D_ The equipment was not damaged, therefore not cost involved. The welder was injured and sent to shore for further evaluation.

_x000D_

An employee was injured while operating a stand mixer in the galley. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation._x000D_
_x000D_
While performing rigging duties on pipe bundles, the IP stepped on the permanent wooden running boards on deck and injured themselves. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.

On February 10, 2017 a Rowan Floorhand was evacuated from the drillship Rowan
Resolute while working for Anadarko Petroleum Corp in Green Canyon Block 859. The
Floorhand was injured while assisting on the rig floor with pulling the 5-7/8 inch
work string out of the hole (tripping out of the hole). Several stands into the
tripping operation, a rope holding the manual tongs out of the way broke and allowed
the tongs to swing forward and struck the Floorhand in the back. The Floorhand was
sent in on a medevac flight for evaluation.
Crane cab glass panel was struck and "spidered" when a temporary building lift led to a small swing of the load and hit same.  No injuries were caused by this incident.
Employee reported he was working on G-2 turbine and leaning in the opening of the turbine package when he was injured. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation.

While moving a propane tank with a crane, a portion of the propane tank framework struck the handrail when being lifted and dislodged the handrail from the handrail pocket.  The handrail fell overboard to ocean.  No damage was noted to propane tank unit.

A control room operator reported 10% LEL alarm inside the water injection #1 package. I&E technicians were dispatched to the package to investigate. Upon further investigation the technicians determined that there was a leak emanating from 3/8 inch to one half inch MPT tubing fitting spool thread on the fuel gas line.  Shut down on LEL is set at 25% for this package. For this event, the equipment was already shut in, but a full personnel muster was conducted._x000D_

column19: semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23:
A fire/smoke alarm was received from the UPS battery charger room. The audible alarm sounded and power was shunt tripped to building as per safety system.  The Crew mustered and fire team investigated.  No flames or glowing found, only smoke in affected area.  Upon investigation, found the main 120V instrumentation power transformer for the UPS had shorted to ground. No indications of fire, only smoke and soot observed on the transformer._x000D_
_x000D_

A combustible gas release alarm sounded. All 51 personnel mustered within 5 minutes. The Fire Team Leader and On Scene Commander (OSC) were dispatched to the methanol skid where the LEL was detected. Winds were reported out of the SSE at approximately 6 knots. When the OSC and fire team leader arrived at the methanol skid, they discovered methanol flowing from what appeared to be a damaged fitting at the bottom of the pulsation dampener on PBE 9350. Approximately 5 gallons of methanol was released into the chemical injection skid secondary containment with some methanol spraying over onto the secondary containment on the deck. No chemical went over the side into the Gulf. The leak was immediately isolated and the muster came to a stand down. _x000D_
While testing installation of cable on the life boat winch, the employee was using the brake override cable resulting in an injury. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.
The IP was involved in setting up the completion fluid filter press when he was injured. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation.

While Attempting to position the #2 knuckle boom crane (Port FWD) to make a lift off of the rig floor the operator made contact with the platform above the V-door of the derrick. The guarding around the mounted camera on the end of the crane boom became bent inwards as results of the impact. NO object were dropped. _x000D_
_x000D_
While walking from the Cutting box deck to the rig floor, the IP stepped on an uneven surface and was injured. The IP was sent to shore for evaluation.

While placing a full 550 gallon steel chemical tote in the raised staging area during crane options, the full tote bumped an empty 550 gallon steel tote causing it to shift approximately 6". The shift of the empty tote caused a corner of the tote to fall 18 inches, damaging a 12"x12" piece of steel grating and cracking the plastic valve on the tote. No personnel were injured as a result of the incident.

The maintenance group was in the process of installing a turbine output hub.  The procedure required heating of the hub using a heating strip to heat the hub.  The hub was placed in a metal bucket to be heated.  The hub had been heated to approximately 200 degrees Fahrenheit.  A third party mechanic stationed to watch the temperature noted flame in the bucket.  The power was shut off to the heat strip.  A fire extinguisher was present at the site which the mechanic used to extinguish the flame immediately. The fire was extinguished before the alarm could be sounded.  The heat strip was inadvertently 'doubled' which increased heat. No injuries occurred as a result of this incident.

While attempting to crank the #2 gas compressor, a flash fire was noticed in the flywheel / starter area. The platform ESD was activated and the fire was extinguished immediately. There were no injuries. Malfunctioning of the starter was direct cause of fire _x000D_resulting in the replacement of the starter costing $862.00._x000D_

_x000D_

column19: semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23: A crane crew was moving the East Crane over the north end of the upper deck in order to pick up a load that was sitting on the intermediate deck porch.  While the hook on the Main Block was over the load the middle section of the crane boom was directly over the exhaust fan of the East Field Gas Compressor (FGCE).  After the load was securely fastened to the hook, the Main Block hook was hoisted back up and the crane operator boomed up and rotated eastward in the direction of the boat.  While swinging the load towards the boat, the crane operator noticed smoke coming from some wires on the boom.  The wires were for the crane boom camera and lights.  Upon noticing this, the crane operator immediately placed the load safely on the deck.  The crane boom was then returned to the boom rest.  No injuries to personnel, no harm to environmental occurred.

In the process of running riser, the gantry crane (with spreader bar attached) was utilized to transport riser from the riser holds to the Aft Catwalk Machine. In the process of transporting a joint of riser to the Aft CWM, the forward end of the spreader bar made contact with the Telescopic Man Basket pedestal which is located on the port side of the construction floor. No workers were in the area.

While lifting items from access shaft_x000D_, the IP was guiding the rope being spooled through the sheaves of a tripod lifting device that was set over the hull access shaft when he was injured. IP was sent in for further evaluation. 
_x000D_

_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
An employee found a mop head in designated smoking area a flame. The employee immediately extinguished mop utilizing water hose in sink and then reported the incident._x000D_

While attempting to drill hole in angle iron (to fasten deck grating), an employee was standing on a ladder to access angle iron over head. The drill bit became stuck and the torque turned drill in the employee's hand. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

The IP was measuring bulk barite tanks in the P-Tank room in preparation for taking onmore barite from the work boat. 
_x000D_
While the cook was opening the oven door, the heat from the oven caused the thermal detector to activate. The crew on location mustered and the PIC gave all clear orders after roll call.

The MGC compressor A was offline, but was being returned to service after maintenance. _x000D_
There was an unrelated event that resulted in a signal to open the blowdown valve on the compressor. After that, while ramping the facility there was backpressure on the HP flare system, resulting in backflow of gas from the flare to the compressor suction scrubber via the BDV. A loose flange on the suction scrubber resulted in a gas release leading to activation of the gas detection system and the muster._x000D_
_x000D_
During Tote tank transfer operation, a contractor was injured when caught between two tote tanks. Contractor was sent in for further evaluation.

column19: Semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23: Employees were staging equipment for an upcoming job.  While moving a control panel weighing approximately 1000 lbs., the team had to navigate a tight area between two structural steel members.  The team was using a pallet jack and jacked the control panel up with the pallet jack to clear the diagonal member.  While moving the control panel through the tight area, the control panel shifted causing an injury to an IP.  The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation.
While removing bolts from pressure washer the employee was injured.
An employee was injured while working in the heavy tool storage room. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

On March 14, 2017 at 2400 hours, Exxon reported that a fire had occurred on a diesel
driven cement pump at MI 657B, Lease G10228 while conducting decommissioning
operations from the Lift Boat (L/B) Jamie G Eymard. There were no injuries or
pollution involved in the incident.

The chief engineer was stationed on the deck below as per the standing orders for bringing engines online while bringing on Engine 3.  After bringing the engine online, a member of the deck crew observed smoke coming from the deck below the stacks and notified the crane operator via radio.  The crane operator issued orders to respond to the fire and notified the bridge of the situation.  Two members of the deck crew responded to the fire with 2 fire extinguishers.  The general alarm was sounded and a muster was called.  The fire was immediately extinguished and the muster was cancelled.  _x000D_
_x000D_
A crate cover snagged on turbine housing as being lifted off by crane, causing $6,400 in minor damage to turbine.  No injuries or other property damage.

While unloading equipment off of motor vessel to the P/F, the crane operator heard a noise and felt the crane shake. He got out to inspect the crane and noticed the cable had come off the sheave. Crane was placed OOS until repairs are made.The load being transferred from the boat to the facility was a test pump used for wire line operations. The weight of the pump is 5000#. The total cost of repairs is $5642.00.

An employee was working as a thread inspector and he was moving 7" lift nubbins (~65 lbs. ea.) to a position approximately 10 feet away where he could apply pipe dope to the threads. The first 3 nubbins were moved without any issues. The IP was injured  IP when he put the 4th nubbin down. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.
_x000D_

column19: Semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23: A fire and gas alarm was received from the NW hull column methanol pump room. This activated the F&G alarm (20% LEL) as per design and the crew mustered while the alarm was investigated.  Upon investigation, the crew identified that a fitting on the methanol pump discharge piping had developed a small leak, triggering the 20% LEL alarm.  The 40% LEL HH shutdown was not reached, thus this was an alarm only, not a facility shut in.  Pump was shut down, pump room was ventilated, and fitting was replaced to eliminate leak.  _x000D_

Four workers were repositioning a 14' portable ladder several feet away.  Each worker was lifting a corner and sliding the ladder when the leading corners caught on the deck allowing the ladder to close unexpectedly.  Then it ladder closed, the IP was injured._x000D_ The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation

After powering up and running the HOS compressor for around 1 hour in time, a fuse in the Harmonic Capacitor Panel powering the HOS compressor blew causing a small smoldering fire of a card board box containing spare fuses for the panel. The spare fuses box was stored inside of the Harmonic Panel and was in direct contact with the blown fuse cables. Upon opening of the panel no visible fire was seen, just smoke and smoldering remnants of the card board box. A fire extinguisher was used as a_x000D_ precautionary method on the spare fuses to prevent any rekindle._x000D_
No alarms, muster or injuries resulted from the incident._x000D_
_x000D_
Property Damaged: Harmonic Capacitor Panel fuses and associated parts._x000D_
Nature of Damage Internal smoke or fire damage to Harmonic Capacitor Panel and spare fuses. _x000D_
_x000D_

A Mechanic and Operator went to FGC #1 panel to observe reason for compressor going down. Noticed high level in 1st. stage scrubber and level was dropping. After LSH cleared, the mechanic reset the panel and started up FGC #1 without load. The operator was walking around FGC #1 and noticed fire between starter and engine block, and immediately hit the facility ESD station and used a fire reel in close proximity of FGC#1 to extinguish flame and keep area cooled down. The general alarm was sounded. All personnel on facility mustered to their assigned locations for further orders as per the general alarm that was activated.
IP was injured during a workbasket transfer from motor vessel. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

The construction crew was replacing grating in the well bay. After making a cut on a new piece of grating, the grating struck a bull plug and a rust bubble chipped off allowing some trapped gas to be released. This resulted in a small flame at the bull plug and the crew grabbed a nearby fire extinguisher and extinguished it immediately. The crew called for a stand down to re-evaluate the situation._x000D_
There was no damage associated with this incident. The job was shut down and the pressure behind the bull plug was bled to zero._x000D_

Gas was detected by the ASHs located at the BCG B & C units. The units shut down and personnel responded to the area and found gas leaking from the filter separator hatch. The vessel was isolated and locked out.  Ignition sources were secured, control of work was utilized to manage risks associated with the maintenance, and a systematic repair was completed for reinstatement of the vessel after verification of the condition of the equipment._x000D_ It was determined that the cause was an O-ring failure.

The crane crew was in the process of lifting the TIS umbilical sheave with the port forward crane and landing it on the forward side of the main rig floor in preparation to install the sheave. As the crane was booming down and knuckling out, the boom tip camera guard came into contact with a derrick platform resulting in damage to the camera guard.  There were no dropped objects or injury to personnel. The operation of the port forward crane was suspended and a stand down meeting was held with the crew.

A crane operator was lifting a load off the supply boat. After swinging the load over water, he began to winch up on the fast line when the Anti-Two-Block device came loose and the weight slid down the load line cable coming to rest on the headache ball._x000D_ There were no injuries or additional damage._x000D_ The cable was replaced and crane placed back in service.

An Oiler was assisting the Mechanic or Engineers to ensure that the regular preventative maintenance activities occur in a timely manner so as to minimize down time and ensure the efficient and continual functioning of the mechanical equipment on board the drilling rig. The Oiler was unaware that the integrated fall arrest gin pole on a tank was not fully seated and grabbed ahold of it to assist in balancing himself while moving from one tank to another.  In the process the Oiler was injured. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation. 
_x000D_

While workers were de-inventorying the float cell to prepare the facility for upcoming turnaround, the drain hose was disconnected midway between the isolation points.  When the hose was disconnected, it released LP gas. The gas detectors sensed the LP gas cloud shutting in the facility._x000D_ This was not a blowdown and no muster.  The estimated volume of gas released was .022 kg and dissipated immediately.  _x000D_
_x000D_

An 11' portion of 3/8" Pneumatic winch wire and chain weighing 4.2lbs in total (heaviest portion is .5lb hook)  parted as the derrick man was using the hydraulic winch line to pull back tubulars into the derrick finger.  The chain and wire remained fasted to the pipe until it was 30' off the ground unlatching on the pipe collar upset.  The Derrick Man maintained control of the drill pipe and racked it.  The Pneumatic air operated winch is used by the derrick man as an alternative for using rope to rack pipe._x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

Galley  towels were found smoldering in the galley after being taken out of the clothes  dryer and folded. They were removed from the galley and put into a bucket with water. There were no injuries and no damage to facility.

A crane operator was lifting the #1 well bay hatch. One of the pad eyes broke during the lift causing the hatch to fall approximately 12" to the deck. No injuries or damage occurred (other than broken pad eye). _x000D_
_x000D_

While offloading a NuTek 4-way test stand skid, it contacted and damaged an adjacent skid package sitting on the boat. The damaged skid was a_x000D_
satellite communications package and the impact punctured a fiberglass dome shell over the dish antenna. The total estimated cost for the repairs is $4,000.

While working on the exterior battery bank on the compressor module that provides DC power, a spark initiated a flash fire. _x000D_
The TLP ESD was manually tripped and the fire was quickly extinguished._x000D_ The damage amount was $1100.00_x000D_.

An employee was assisting with rigging down the wire line equipment from the drill floor. A wire line sheave shifted in the box and injured the employee. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

Two buffer plates (12.5lbs each) fell (33ft) from Riser Gantry crane to the riser bay. While pulling the BOPs, the Crane Operator had just landed a joint of riser in the STBD Riser Bay and had raised the Riser Gantry Crane Spreader Bar back to a height of 33ft when the inner and outer tubes became stuck about 2ft apart. While attempting to slack off tubes to correct the problem, the 2 tubes suddenly became free causing the outer tube to fall into the inner tube resulting in the "inner tube buffer stop plate" shearing the bolts off causing the plates to fall to the main deck. The area was a Red Zone Management Area and Danger (red) taped off with the nearest person 85ft away. The 2 pieces that fell weighed 12.5lbs each for a total of 25lbs._x000D_
_x000D_

During crane operations, a crane operator was in process of lowering the boom when the boom bumped the top of a production compressor's separator. The compressor was OOS at time of incident and there was no damage to the separator however, during inspection of the crane one bent lattice was identified. The load being handled was a 4" section of PVC pipe used for storing stainless steel tubing. The crew was attempting to re-position the PVC  pipe to the backside of the compressor for storage.

A mechanic was in the process of changing out the retract arm on the Main Top Drive. A power pack was being used to push out the retainer pins from the existing arm. Upon freeing one of the pins, the power pack became wedged in the pin hole. While attempting to free the power pack, something shifted causing the power pack to cock over to the bottom and contacting the IP. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.

While performing coil tubing operations the small block of the crane was being utilized with a nylon sling  to prevent the pack off from tilting, resulting in bending of the coil tubing. Coil tubing was functioned utilizing the injector head to slack off and pick up, with a pre-job planned designated range of 10,900 to 13,800 lbs. per coil tubing weight indicator. At the time of the incident, the coil tubing operator was attempting to calculate hydraulic pressure while the weight indicator dipped down to 5000 lbs., indicating additional tension on the nylon sling resulting in the sling parting. Because it was not lifting anything no equipment was damaged or fell. No personnel were injured during the event.

A worker was in the process of moving boxes with computer parts when he was injured. The IP was flown in to seek further medical treatment.  
  _x000D_
_x000D_
While hoisting up a section of cut out piping from sump deck level, crane operator felt the crane bind up.  The fast line cable came of off the winch drum.

While attempting to bring gas generator online, a small fire was noticed around wiring at the wiring/electronics box.  The flame was quickly extinguished with #30 hand held fire extinguisher.  The platform was immediately shut in and there were no injuries or evacuations.

The PDPH crane ( Knuckle boom ) was handling a 9 7/8'' joint of casing from the aft pipe bay to the forward pipe bay. When the pipe was approximately 4' off the deck the starboard gripper inadvertently released from the pipe. This resulted in the pin end of the pipe to fall, striking the deck and jarring the opposite gripper free from the pipe. The joint came to rest on the wood covered pipe bay support beams directly underneath the previously suspended load. All personnel were standing in a safe zone - no injuries and no damage to equipment.

While offloading a basket from the platform to a motor vessel, a 550 gallon tote tank was struck causing the tote tank to fall on it's side. Oil and chemicals leaked from the tank minimally as a result of the incident. 
_x000D_
While making personnel lift from crew boat with MUA-103 Offshore Platform crane the boat shifted and rolled causing the boat to come back up under the basket jolting the riders.

While laying boom back in pedestal, the boom tip came in contact with the heliport skirting and the skirting was bent.  There was no damage to the boom tip or aux cable. The crane was placed back in full service. No personnel were injured. The total cost to repair the damaged heliport skirting is $20,000._x000D_

column19: semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23:
While moving a joint of riser in the riser bay, one of the hooks on the riser capture device on the riser gantry crane released and the joint of riser fell 15 ft into the riser bay. There were handrails damaged during the incident._x000D_ No personnel were injured as a result of this incident._x000D_
_x000D_

The pump went down on a PSL due to a small fire that was extinguished with a 30lb ABC Fire extinguisher. The shaft on the pump end failed and caused the coupler housing to contact the coupling and ignite.

The crane operator was swinging the crane into place in preparation to lift a cargo basket off the boat that had a 1500# valve in it. The crane was being operated in moderate winds (10-12 kts.) when a hydraulic fitting broke on the pressure side of swing motor causing loss of swing pressure. This allowed the wind to swing boom until it contacted flare boom. Section of crane boom was damaged and gear box was shocked and loosened. No load was on hook at the time and there were no personnel injured. The fitting has been replaced and gear box tightened down.   At the time of the incident there was no load on the crane._x000D_
The estimated cost to replace the section of boom is approximately $26,000._x000D_

While making rounds the operator noticed smoke coming from the diesel generator louvers.  When he and the PIC opened the generator package door they saw a flame on top of the generator engine.  They immediately secured a 30# ABC fire extinguisher and extinguished the flame. The generator and platform had already shut-in from a TSE in the generator enclosure. Upon further investigation of the incident the mechanic and electrician found a broken diesel injector line on top of the engine as the cause of the fire. Fuel was sprayed onto the turbo. The cost to repair the generator was $14,100.

An employee was assisting with installing ball valves on the low pressure wellhead housing in the moon pool with the ball valve suspended with a tugger line. While threading the valve into the wellhead housing, the IP was injured.

A LACT train meter failure alarm occurred.  Smoke emanated from the LACT room, between the engine and the pump of LACT Pump #1.  A brief flare up of small flames was also visable.  _x000D_
Tthe engine was shut down and the fire was extinguished.  The clutch shoes on the heavy duty clutch between the engine and the pump were the main cause of the incident._x000D_ _x000D_
There were no personal injuries associated with this event._x000D_
_x000D_

The rig personnel mustered with the intention to evacuate the rig due to gas detected in the Shaker Building.  The cause of gas was discovered to be due to oil being drained out of the separator during a back surge which allowed gas to come down the piping and into the shaker building._x000D_

While moving bit breaker base from rotary, IP assisted with carrying the base when he was injured.
_x000D_
While retrieving the MS1000 scanning sonar tripod on deck, the IP was injured. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.
column55: Prep for Coil Tubing and HWO

column23: The Motor Vessel Wildcat was passing though Chevron's Bay Marchand field. The vessel made impact with our ST 23 S facility. The facility did not sustain any damage from the vessel. We verified this with survey work which was the only costs incurred from the event. No one was injured and no pollution resulted from the event. The vessel is not contracted to Chevron and has been in contact with the USCG.
While moving a laundry dryer up stairs, the employee was injured.

While performing seal replacement maintenance on a Cameron Integral Connector (CIC) aboard the M/V Ross Candies, the deck crane was utilized as an additional safeguard to help stabilize the equipment which was concurrently being supported by sea-fastening chains on the deck of the boat. In this configuration the sea-fastening chains were providing the primary means of stabilization and not the crane. At no time was the CIC lifted off of the deck by the crane.  The crane was providing support via the pad eyes located on the CIC's frame. Once the seal replacement was complete, the crane operator noticed the CIC beginning to tip and reacted by over pulling on the controls of the crane. This action caused the bolts, which were securing the pad eyes to the frame of the CIC, to break. _x000D_There were no injuries to personnel and the extent of damage was limited to the bolts of the pad eyes. _x000D_
 _x000D_

During P/A operations, a nylon strap used to lift a 30" casing stub on the MP 187 SS001 well parted, while lifting from the seafloor to the L/B Nashville.  No injuries, divers were not in the water at the time of the incident.  This incident is under further investigation.

The Motor Vessel Roman Elie struck the Southeast corner of the platform, damaging the support structure. There were no injuries on the boat (or platform) and no pollution. The platform sustained minor property damage to +10 boat bumper, jacket and grating._x000D_Damages are approximately $75,000._x000D_

A nipple failed on the sight glass connected to suction scrubber of the compressor resulting in a gas release. The ESS system detected the gas release and shut in all production. No injuries or fire occurred. Minimal amount of gas was released to the atmosphere.

Smoke in the General Electrical Equipment Room (GEER) set off a smoke alarm on the bridge as a result of a failed inverter from IAS UPS #8.  The general alarm was sounded, all non-essential personnel were instructed to muster at the assigned muster points. The Rapid Response Team was dispatched to investigate. There was light smoke with no visible flames in the Geert, and the cabinet which held the inverter was quickly identified as the source of smoke._x000D_

A fire was extinguished on the grill in the galley. There were no injuries. There is a tray under the grill that funnels grease to a trap. It appears this funnel was lined with aluminum foil to make it easier to clean but it also prevented the grease from falling into the trap which is further away from the heating element. When they were heating up the grill, the grease caught fire. They were able to extinguish it by throwing a fire blanket on top of it.

The platform crew was attempting to backload and pick up several lifts from the M/V Miss Julie. As crane operator started the lift, the deckhand went back toward the tote in an attempt to reposition one leg of the four part sling which had wrapped around shackle at top of tote.  The tote came off the deck in an unbalanced manner and inured the IP. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation.

column19: Semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23:
While removing exhaust bellows from the main generator unit using the trolley system in the unit, the trolley came off the trolley beam when trying to lower the exhaust bellows to the platform deck outside the generator enclosure. The exhaust bellows dropped 4ft to the platform deck. _x000D_The cause of the incident has been identified as a failure to utilize an A-frame (engine removing handling kit) designed specifically for removal of ancillary equipment from the generator enclosure. Damage to the bellows is estimated at $7,500._x000D_
_x000D_

The crane was used to move compressor maintenance equipment from the drilling deck to the main deck of the platform. The damage was noted once the lifts were complete and the crane boom was in the rest. The damage was to the heel section which consisted with overriding the high angle kick-out and bringing the boom into mechanical stops.

The Level Safety Low (LSL) alarm went off on the coolant tank of the FGC #2. A flame was detected at FGC #2. The flame was extinguished immediately with a fire extinguisher and a fire watch posted to ensure it did not reignite. ESD of the facility and a full muster occurred.

The IP was involved in an operation on the lower turret. While stepping down onto a grating step, IP lost his footing and fell forward on a section of tubing. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation. 
_x000D_
_x000D_

When transporting material from boat to platform, the boat dropped beneath the boat landing deck,  causing the deck to push upward towards the latter.  The boat landing was a total loss, and will be removed.  A new boat landing will be constructed off-site and reinstalled.
An employee was installing a motor when the rigging failed resulting in an injury. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

A shrimp boat struck non-flowing satellite with outrigger which caused damage to the facility. The shrimp boat sustained minor damage to outrigger and cabin.  No injuries or pollution. Estimated repair cost is $24,000.
While an employee unscrewed the 3" inch service hose hammer union a hose sprung forward striking the IP. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

While exiting the cab of the wireline unit a wind gust caught door and and injured an employee. The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation. _x000D_
_x000D_

Crew mustered when smoke alarm went off this morning. It was discovered that insulation on the A/C unit was smoking. There was no fire or embers discovered.The piece of insulation that was smoking was removed. There were no injuries. Our investigation found that a bearing seized up on a pulley of the fan motor and spun the fan belts. This caused the overheating.

While offloading the motor vessel for grocery and chemicals, the box swung to the stern of the boat stiking a handrail and cracking the sockets that held it in place. No one was on back side of grocery box, no one was injured.  _x000D_The damage is approximately < $1,000.

A 120 volt Subsea UPS transformer in the 806 building shorted out resulting in the transformer overheating and smoking. No visible flame was detected but the transformer was burnt up. The response team responded and opened the feeder breaker and the smoke subsided. The platform performed a full muster. There were no injuries to personnel _x000D_
The estimated total cost of damages to be at ~$20K. _x000D_
_x000D_

All four leads for each phase of the generator were spliced. The fire originated on the leads from the main stator to the "B" phase on the buss bar. Operators immediately discharged the handheld extinguisher and extinguished the flame.  There were no injuries or damage other than to the generator itself.

Personnel were being transferred from a motor vessel to a barge. Three people were on the personnel basket when the incident occurred. When the basket was lifted off the deck to the supply boat the crane block was off center of the basket causing it to swing and contact the bull works. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.
_x000D_

An operator was doing monthly inspections. The oil filler cap was removed from compressor number 11 to take an oil sample and check the level.  After screwing the cap back on and a few moments later the cap blew off and sprayed oil onto the turbine, causing a small fire.  He shut off the compressor as well as compressor 14 and sounded the fire alarm.  He extinguished the flame with a fire hose. There were no injuries and no damage.

A NOV fluid control hand was performing a task involving transferring water from a marine portable tank to the skimmer tank to process through the deck drainage treatment system when he was injured. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

A rig received a smoke detector activation in the laundry room. General alarm was manually activated. It was determined that the clothes dryer in laundry room overheated due to an inadequate amount of air flow. Soiled laundry began to emit "white smoke".

While conducting decommissioning activities the Derrick Barge "D-85" crew were picking up the "Airlift" utilizing a dual crane method (common procedures for this lifting process). The crew had a verbal tool box meeting and started the lifting process. The small auxiliary crane (linkbelt) sustained a failure at the gantry which allowed the crane boom cable support to fail.  The crane boom fell onto the deck. No injuries were sustained by crew. No pollution_x000D_ or injuries_x000D_ occurred as a result of this incident. Estimated damage costs are $8,500_x000D_ to the crane. 
_x000D_
_x000D_

A manifold blanket located on top of #2 EMD began smoldering and the high temp alarm sounded on EMD. There was no visible flame observed. The EMD #1 started as a backup and the EMD #2 was taken off line. When exhaust blanket was removed from exhaust manifold on #2 EMD, air exposure to manifold was enough to combust the hot residual oil located on top of the EMD valley into a 4" tall flame in a 2" area for a less than 10 seconds. The flame was extinguished with 1 short burst of portable fire extinguisher. No fire alarms sounded. _x000D_

Well work personnel were being transferred via personnel basket from the platform to a motor vessel.  During the transfer, the personnel basket made contact with the vessel's deck partially collapsing the basket. In the process one man was injured and sent to shore for further evalution.

The Port ROV was in the process of removing a Transponder from the AHC winch carousel. At that time the Port side ROV's winch lost control and unspooled with the umbilical parting at the winch spool. ROV lost video and communications with surface when the umbilical parted at the winch spool. The TMS was ~75' off the seabed and dropped to the sea floor together with 14,000' of wire. The cost of damage is estimated  to be $100,000.

While lowering a cargo box to the motor vessel, a swell caused the boat to move and the cargo box struck the boards on the rescue zone of the  boat. The strike broke the boards. There was no damage to the crane or facility. There were no injuries. The cost to repair the boat's wooden gate was $25_x000D_.
_x000D_

At the time of this event the Starboard Forward Crane was being used to lift the belly of the HFL umbilical to the ROV grab-handle on the LMRP.  The sling had been placed around the sling guide of the hosebun as a lifting point instead of running under and being choked around the hosebun/HFL assembly.  This caused the sling guide of the hosebun to tear under the weight of the suspended HFL.  In the process an employee was injured. No equipment or structural damage resulted from this event (with the exception of the torn hosebun).

A mechanic monitoring the compressor noticed smoke coming from the compressor exhaust. Upon further examination, he noticed a small flame coming from the insulation on the exhaust.  The mechanic shut in the unit and quickly grabbed a 30lb hand held extinguisher and extinguished the flame. At that point, operations staff removed the remaining insulation and soaked it with water. There were no injuries associated with this event and no damage was noted to the compressor other than the insulation.
A cook was injured while cooking. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

Platform crane was used to lift a section of pipe from the cellar deck. While the crane operator was lifting the pipe, the tag line slipped out of the rigger's hands causing the load to swing away from him. The load contacted a handrail nearby causing it to lift out of its sockets and fall overboard into the Gulf of Mexico. The crane did not sustain any damage nor were any personnel injured as a result of the incident. 
_x000D_

While feeding a nylon strap under a joint of casing and up between the joints an employee was injured. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation. 
_x000D_
Crews were manually unloading temporary pipework from a basket. As two workers moved a joint of pipe, one worker was injured. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

Fieldwood Energy is currently performing P&A activity at GI 90A and utilizing GI 93C Platform for equipment storage and crew living. The MV Starfleet Viking was at GI 93C for the purposes of transferring several pieces of equipment from its' deck to the platform for storage.  During the lift of a conex box, it was noticed the bottom plate of the boom's Anti-Two Block devise dislodged from the unit and fell to the vessel's deck.  The lift was completed with no incident.  The Anti-Two Block base plate did not strike any one and there was no damage to the vessel's deck.  The crane was immediately taken out of service to allow unit inspection, troubleshooting, and repair.  Fieldwood Energy will submit a final report following completion of our investigation
Operator reported 6 feet of handrail went overboard and could not be recovered due to working in the wellhead deck (center) lifting a bin and the feet got caught on the handrail.

While on VR-252-I unloading a well operator was down stairs on the production deck and there was a small flame burning on the charge regulator. He removed the power source from the charge regulator and smothered out the flame. There was no damage to the battery or the battery box itself,  the charge regulator was damaged.
While working on the surface BOP gripper assembly the connector plate moved to the closed position injuring an emaployee.  The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

During site clearance verification of VR 171 "A" platform utilizing DSV Kelly Morrison, a crane cable parted while setting 8' x 16'  basket on sea floor for scrap collection.  As the basket made contact with the sea floor, the DSV surged and shock loaded the crane causing the crane to part approximately 9' above the ball.  The crane swung  back over the DSV and an additional 40' of cable was cut from the crane.

Production personnel were moving a construction tool box from the platform cellar deck to the drill deck using the main crane (Titan 5400) on the facility.  As the load was being lifted from cellar deck, the load came in contact with a piece of metal channel (approximately one foot long) which protrudes from one of the structural members.  Once the load cleared the metal channel it caused the load to sway.  This movement of the load resulted in an employee being caught between the load and the handrail.  The IP was transported to shore for further evaluation. 
_x000D_
A worker was injured while opening a heavy exterior door.  The IP was sent in for further evaluation.

An employee bent down to pick up bolts and was injured. The IP was transported to shore for medical evaluation._x000D_
_x000D_
A driller was injured while slacking off on block while putting a joint of tubing in v-door.

A fire was observed at the Crosby Gas Compressor engine exhaust.  Operations were re-starting the unit after performing maintenance over the weekend.  The control room initiated emergency response and the first responders were dispatched.  Personnel were mustered and the facility was secured by means of ESD.  The fire was suppressed and there were no injuries to personnel._x000D_
Fire was suppressed and investigation deemed two pieces of plywood utilized to support the job was left unattended and leaning against the unit.  The hot exhaust ignited the wood._x000D_
There were no other damage to the TLP._x000D_The fire lasted approximately 8 minutes._x000D_
_x000D_

During severe thunderstorms the vent/ flare boom became lit from a lightning strike. Personnel on the facility snuffed out the fire once weather conditions did not pose a threat to employees being outside.

A valve on the Methanol tank was misaligned causing the Methanol tank to be over filled.  Some Methanol escaped out of the Vent lines on the tank and spilled into the drip pan and on the deck. The Vapors from the Methanol triggered a Gas alarm in the nearby air intakes for aft machinery spaces. The Alarms sounded and everyone reported to the appropriate muster areas as directed by the bridge. A full muster was completed.
An employee was going to check on the buy-back valve when he was injured. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.
A crane was lifting a wire line value and assembly and this struck a empty cargo basket and the empty basket struck a worker The injury was first aid only and no evacuation.
The IP was in the process of sandblasting an overhead beam when he was injured.  The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

In the course of operations to disconnect PSN 13235 from the MP 261 JP Platform while working subsea off the MSV Grand Canyon II, the diver installed reciprocating saw to methanol line. Saw was hanging from crane and physically clamped to line for cutting. Diver backed away to allow crane operation to slack rigging. Prior to rigging going slack, vessel heave caused the rigging to tighten more causing the 4 lifting eye bolts on saw to break. Diver was clear, no injury or damage to the saw or asset.

A fire occurred in bedroom #220 due to an electric outlet shorting out. The fire was extinguished immediately. There where no injuries to personnel._x000D_
_x000D_
A rig hand was going about his duties in the shaker house cleaning the shale shaker screens when he became ill.  The IP was sent in for further evaluation.

At approximately 3:15 pm during normal startup operations, the Cooper gas compressor
ran for approximately twenty minutes before shutting down due to a diesel air
compressor problem. After two failed attempts to restart the compressor, the mechanic
made adjustments between the magnetic pickup and the flywheel. Two attempts later,
the compressor appeared to be starting. After approximately 2-3 seconds, the engine
backfired, sending the scavenger box and debris airborne and igniting the paper
filters in the filter housing. The fire was immediately extinguished, and the
surrounding area was secured. The mechanic was standing next to the air box and was
injured by some of the flying debris that contacted his chin and upper body.
While lifting the slips an employee was injured.  The IP was sent in for further evaluation.

While moving a basket on the deck with a crane, a 3"chicksan component in the basket shifted injuring an employee. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation. 
_x000D_

_x000D_
_x000D_

While in the process of laying down drill pipe with the knuckle boom pipe handling crane (KBPH) the roustabout operating the KBPH crane was placing a double of drill pipe in the east bay of the east pipe deck. The catwalk was in the process of being raised to receive the next double. During these movements contact was made with the catwalk machine and causing damage to an hydraulic fitting cover on the KBPH crane.  The catwalk had been stopped 4' short of the receiving point on the drill floor to allow the floor hands to retrieve the strap attached to the catwalk skate, the strap is used to assist pulling doubles into the catwalk.  Once the strap was retrieved the floor hand began to move the catwalk the last 4' to the drill floor, concurrent with the crane positioned over the catwalk while landing the double.  This is when the incident occurred causing damage to hydraulic fitting resulting in an LOPC of 4 gallons BioBar 46 to deck area and loosening a fitting on the KBPH.  No injuries, dropped object or harm to the environment occurred.
While removing a ratchet strap holding a breathing air cylinder to the North crane hand rail an employee was injured.

The IP was lancing a sand trap discharge line, located in the shaker house pit tank when he was injured. 



_x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_

While tightening a flange, the wrench slipped off of the bolt and struck the injured person.  _x000D_
_x000D_
While carrying two scaffold bars across an area of the deck that transitioned from grating to deck plating and IP was injured.

The platform crane operator was using the load line to pick up a cargo basket off of the back deck of the supply boat M/V "GIS Linda".  As the load was lifted, the boat began to move backwards, toward the load.  The crane operator was unable to get the load up quickly enough and it made contact with the stern control doghouse of the supply boat, cracking the glass on one of the doghouse windows.  The window remained intact.

The M/V Thunder America was moving into position to have a full cutting box placed on his back deck to be sent to shore.  During the landing of the lift, the stinger got away from the deckhand and became lodged in the cutting box latch cover.  The captain maintained control of the vessel.  The crane big block was lowered and main D-ring was detached.  The stinger was removed from the cutting box and sent back up to the lift boat.  _x000D_
_x000D_

The IP was walking in the aft direction on the port A-Deck walkway. As the IP began to turn the corner on the walkway he felt his right knee pop. Afterword, the IP felt pain when straightening and bending fully as well when putting weight on it. IP reported to the Medic approx. 5 hours later at 0016 hrs for evaluation. IP was given OTC Ibuprofen and instructed to elevate & rest the knee. IP was on tour, but not performing any task at the time of event, only transiting to work area._x000D_
_x000D_
IP will depart the rig on his scheduled crew change on Wednesday 6/21/17. He will be met by ACI and transported to company physician upon his arrival to shore._x000D_
_x000D_
Follow Up 06/28/2017:_x000D_
Per Seadrill's oral communication, the IP will undergo some therapy to his knee and as of now does not appear that he will miss any time away from work. He is currently on his three weeks off period.

column19: Semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23: While carrying PSV parts from the warehouse to an area on the Lower Deck an employee was injured on the stairs. The IP was sent in for further evaluation.
A floor hand  fell and came in contact with the BOP dolly beam resulting in an injury. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.
An employee lost their balance while working in the galley cooler.  The IP was sent ashore for further evaluation._x000D_
The crane boom function failed while Crane Operator was making a lift from the vessel. The estimated damage amount is $ 66,000_x000D_

While conducting paint & blast operations an employee was injured while operating a cable hoist on spider equipment. _x000D_
The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

After routine maintenance on Field Gas Compressor #3, an undetermined amount of residual lube oil ignited in the compressor exhaust manifold during start-up of the compressor.   The fire extinguished itself and was confirmed out by the fire team who were dispatched to the location.  No injuries occurred and damage is estimated to be less than 25K._x000D_

During load testing of a lifeboat, after having changed the falls, with the boat loaded to approximately 1.1 times max weight, the bracket holding one of the sheaves leading the forward fall parted from its position on the support beam. There were no injuries, no pollution, and nothing else appears to have been damaged aside from rendering the forward fall wire most likely unusable. The lifeboat and davit remain unusable at this time._x000D_
_x000D_

A broken seawater  line caused the turbine generator building to fill with water.  Water traveled along conduit from the general building  into the MCC and entered generator "C" generator switchgear.  This caused some relay components to fail and release smoke into the building. A battery charger alarm was triggered and an electrician went to investigate.  He smelled smoke and initiated the fire alarm._x000D_All personnel mustered in the quarters until the situation was secured._x000D_ The "C" switchgear was isolated from the main bus and normal power was restored.  Personnel were released from the muster area.
While helping to move valve off palette an employee was injured. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.

Construction employee was working on the +12' deck replacing grating on the boat landing.  When a sheet of grating was being lowered down to the +12', the grating swung and pushed the employee outward, causing him to jump into the water.  The crew threw a ring buoy and pulled him toward the ladder and he climbed back onto the platform.  He was wearing all PPE including his PFD and sustained no injuries.  The main cause of this incident was the fact that he was outside of the load.

column19: Semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23: A smoke detector alarm sounded in the lab building. The facility mustered and the fire team was dispatched to the location. Upon entering the building no smoke or evidence of a fire was identified. Further investigation found a belt on the Air conditioner unit had broken likely triggering the alarm. After this discovery and all clear was given on the facility. No one was injured nor was there any pollution from this event.

While in the process of hooking up a hose from a chart recorder to top of the tree on the HI-170 A-1 well, the recorder was not reading pressure and after closing the valve an employee removed the line from the chart and was injured._x000D_

As the crane operator was lowering the boom to the boom rest, there was a platform alarm. Unknowingly, the crane operator had his leg against the override switch (see attached photo) and the boom was actually lowered to the ball on the auxiliary line as the ball was being sucked up to the boom jib extension. When the boom was near the boom rest, the crane operator noticed the crane cables slack off so he thought the boom was sitting in the boom rest when it was actually sitting on the ball of the crane. He shut the crane down and left the cab to see about the alarm. Soon thereafter, the weight of the boom sheered the auxiliary crane cable, releasing the ball into the water. The crane operator was unaware that this had occurred. There were no injuries. The estimated cost to repair the crane is approximately $6000-$8000._x000D_

While securing the diesel generator to the platform, one of the firewatch personnel located on the production deck noticed a small fire coming from fire resistant tarps that were being utilized to protect wiring and electrical tray below the generator.  Personnel on facility mustered and the fire was quickly extinguished using portable handheld extinguishers. The current estimated cost to repair/replace equipment is $1,410.

A platform flare arrestor fire occurred due to a lightening strike. Platform personnel engaged the CO2 suppression system leading up to the arrestor, but the flame did not fully extinguish.  Personnel then ESD the platform shutting in all production and extinguished the arrestor fire with a 30# hand held unit.  _x000D_
_x000D_

While in the process of replacing the overboard water line due to barnacle build-up and metal integrity, slag caused a brief flash fire, which was immediately extinguished by the fire watch with a hand held fire extinguisher.  No injuries and no damages resulted in this flash fire.

column19: Semi Submersible (Column Stabilized Unit) Floating Production System
column23: The IP experienced a work related illness and was sent to shore for further evaluation.
While assisting with lifting a cuttings box when one of the slings became caught under the lid. An employee was injured attempting to free the sling.  The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation.
While using an open-ended wrench on a butterfly valve an employee was injured.

During demobilization operations one of our heavy lifts made contact with a cargo basket. While lifting the rig substructure (approx.. 800 MT) the load shifted due to the heaving and sea state causing an "I" beam on the substructure to make contact with an 8 x 24 cargo basket and portable stairwell. Both have minor damage. There were no injuries to personnel and no pollution from the incident. The 8 x 24 cargo basket and portable stairwell were damaged with an estimated cost of less than $5000.

After completing riser running operations with the riser yoke assembly attached to the #3 crane the riser yoke assembly was removed. A Tool Box Talk was held with deck crew members for reeving a 5 part 100- ton crane block to the #3 crane. After completing the reeving of the 5 part 100- ton block both # 3 & 4 cranes were rigged to the slip joint in preparation for a tandem complex lift to the rig floor. After completing the Tool Box Talk for the lifting operations both cranes began to hoist the slip joint. At this point the #3 crane operator observed his weight indicator was taking on weight in an unusual manner and called all stop. Upon inspection to the # 3 crane and rigging, damage was observed on a section of the crane cable due to the crane cable being reeved on the outside of a retainer pin for the sheave block. Once the #3 crane hoisted the load, the weight of the load bent the retainer pin, resulting in damage to the crane cable._x000D_ The estimated cost to replace the crane wire and retainer pin is approximately 10K.  _x000D_

While walking near equipment located on the top deck (C-Drill) of the facility, a construction worker on location noticed smoke coming from a rental air compressor (being used in paint and blast operations).  He alerted a nearby member of paint crew that the unit was smoking.  The painter walked directly to the unit and pulled the ESD.  As the two workers walked to the rear of  the unit, they noticed a small flame near the cooler shroud.  The construction worker grabbed a nearby handheld extinguisher and immediately extinguished the flame (less than 1 minute).  No injuries are associated with this event and the only equipment damaged is the rental air compressor.  The cause of the issue is unknown at this time.  The unit will be returned to vendor for investigation.

While offloading a welding machine onto the M/V Chad Michael the welding machine being lowered to the vessel struck another welding machine that was already on the deck of the vessel. The muffler and the radiator cap on the welding machine on the back of the vessel was damaged and there was no damages to the welding machine being lowered. _x000D_
The damages are minor and are well under $25,000.

While booming up-out of the crane cradle, rigging from the gas buster 6" vent pipe had become hung up on a U bolt which is attached to a cable guide within the crane boom lattice.   We had the crane cradled due to high winds associated with a squall that had just blown through ( 55 + mph wind).  When the rigging was pulled tight it pulled the 6" 12' long vent piping free from its connection.  No injuries to personnel.  _x000D_
_x000D_

Welder landing on to a table to fit it to a metal frame when lightning traveled down the crane boom injuring the employee. The IP was sent to shore for further evaluation. 
_x000D_

At approximately 4:30 pm on July 16 during normal start-up operations, the Waukesha
Reciprocating Compressor ran for approximately five minutes without being loaded.
Then the engine shut down due to low fuel gas supply. Once the fuel gas problem was
corrected, the compressor was restarted without being purged or loaded. The engine
ran in idle for approximately ten minutes with the blowdown valve (BDV) in the open
position. At that time, an explosion occurred, causing damage to the 3rd stage cooler
and associated piping. Renaissance states that, "[t]he internal detonation was caused
by the ignition of a [lower explosive limit] LEL mixture (air and natural gas) within
the process piping and components. This internal detonation [resulted in an
explosion] upon ignition[,] causing the damage. The unit was not loaded or
compressing gas at the time of the incident, and air from the bleed points [was] not
properly purged[,] which allowed a continuous source of air into the process and
components." As such, the probable cause of this incident is the failure to purge.
Furthermore, purging was not even recognized as a key step in the job safety analysis
(JSA). At the time of the incident, Renaissance had no general purging procedure in
place.

General         
BSEE Incident Reporting Requirements can be found at: 30 CFR 250.187-190.         
Effective July 17, 2006, the Incident Reporting regulations were revised. Related to this chart, revisions were made to the reporting criteria for Injuries, Loss of Well Control incidents, Collisions. In addition, new incident categories were required to be reported, including incidents involving lifting operations and gas releases. The number of incidents shown in these categories for 2006 and beyond may be affected by this change when compared to previous years.         
Incidents may be counted in more than one category. For example, a fire resulting in an injury would be counted in both the fire and injury categories.         
Statistics in the chart above are based on Fiscal Year.  Statistics shown in the Incident Archive are based on Calendar Year.         
         
Injuries         
DART – Days away from work; days of restricted work; or days of job transfer.         
Effective July 17, 2006, BSEE reporting requirements were revised.  These revisions required that injuries be reported if the injured person was evacuated from the facility for medical treatment or if the injury resulted in one or more days away from work, restricted work, or job transfer (DART). A combined total for Injuries in the BSEE Annual Report includes:  1) injuries that resulted in more than three days away from work, restricted work or job transfer, 2) injuries that resulted in one 1-3 days away from work, restricted work, or job transfer, and 2) injuries that required medical treatment, but did not result in any days away from work, restricted work, or job transfer (DART). 
         
Loss of Well Control incidents include:         
Uncontrolled flow of formation or other fluids where the flow is to an exposed formation (an underground blowout).         
Uncontrolled flow of formation or other fluids where the flow is at the surface (a surface blowout).         
Flow through a diverter.         
Uncontrolled flow resulting from a failure of surface equipment or procedures.         
         
Fire/Explosion Categories are based on the amount of property damage caused by the incident:         
Catastrophic – destruction of a facility worth more than $10 million         
Major – property damage greater than $1 million         
Minor – property damage greater than $25,000 but less than or equal $1 million         
Incidental – property damage equal to or less than $25,000         
Incidents involving both an explosion and a fire are only counted once.                         
The total used for this category in the Annual Report are a combined total for the Fire and Explosion Categories.

Collision 
Categories are based on the amount of property damage caused by the incident:         
Major – property damage greater than $25,000         
Minor – property damage less or equal to $25,000 (this is below the reporting threshold, some of these are reported).  
Major and minor collision categories are a combined total in the BSEE Annual Report.          
         
Spills         
The calculation used for spill events in the BSEE Annual Report is provided by OSPD and the data is not contained here within.      
         
Gas/H2S Releases         
Only unignited gas releases are counted in this category; ignited gas releases are included under Fires/Explosions. Gas releases related to losses of well control are also not counted in this category and are listed under Loss of Well Control Incidents.         
Some H2S Releases counted here may be below the reporting threshold.         
The Gas/H2S Release categories are a combined total in the BSEE Annual Report.  

Lifting     
For statistical purposes, incidents that involve both a crane and other lifting device are counted as one incident for the BSEE Annual Report.
